items.title: 马克思主义基本原理
items.content: 马克思主义基本原理 0 导论 0.1 什么是马克思主义? 马克思主义的三个基本组成部分：马克思主义哲学、马克思主义政治经济学、科学社会主义 学习把马克思主义基本原理： 基本立场：马克思主义观察、分析和解决问题的根本立足点和出发点，以无产阶级的解放和全人类的解放为己任，以人的自由而全面发展为美好目标，以人民为中心，坚持一切为了人民，一切依靠人民，全心全意为人民谋幸福 基本观点： 关于自然、社会和人类思维发展一般规律的科学认识 对资本主义社会和社会主义社会发展规律的科学认识 对人类思想成果和社会实践经验的科学总结 基本方法：是建立在辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义世界观和方法论基础上，指导我们正确认识世界和改造世界的思想方法和工作方法 0.2 马克思主义的创立和发展 马克思主义的社会根源、阶级基础和思想根源： 社会根源： 社会两极分化，工人极端困苦 周期性经济危机频繁爆发 阶级基础：工人运动的兴起，标志着现代无产阶级作为独立的政治力量登上了历史舞台。 法国里昂工人起义 英国宪章运动 德国西里西亚织工起义 思想根源： 直接的理论来源：德国古典哲学、英国古典政治经济学、英法空想社会主义 自然科学前提：19 世纪的三大科学发现，即细胞学说、能量守恒与转化定律、生物进化论 著作： 马恩合写《德意志意识形态》，首次系统阐述了历史唯物主义的基本观点，实现了历史观上的伟大变革。 《共产党宣言》发表，标志着马克思主义的公开问世。 《资本论》系统阐述了剩余价值学说。唯物史观和剩余价值学说是马克思一生的两个伟大发现。 1876-1878，恩格斯写出了《反杜林论》，全面阐述了马克思主义理论体系。 马克思主义创新发展的基本路径： 本土化和时代化是马克思主义创新发展的基本路径。 本土化：马克思主义基本原理与各国国情相结合，并在各国落地生根、开花结果的过程； 时代化：马克思主义基本原理与时代特征相结合，回答新的时代问题，始终把握时代、引领时代的过程。 马克思主义中国化成果： 毛泽东思想、邓小平理论、“三个代表”重要思想、科学发展观、习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想。 0.3 马克思主义的基本特征 马克思主义的基本特征：鲜明的科学性、人民性、实践性、发展性（科学性与革命性的统一），这些是马克思主义的本质、使命、理论形象。 科学的理论：马克思主义是对自然、社会和人类思维发展本质和规律的正确反映。它是在社会实践和科学发展的基础上产生的，并在自身发展过程中不断总结实践经验，吸取自然科学和社会科学发展的最新成就。 人民的理论：人民性是马克思主义的本质属性，人民至上是马克思主义的政治立场。 实践的理论：马克思主义是从实践中来、到实践中去、在实践中接受检验，并随实践而不断发展的学说。 发展的理论：马克思主义是不断发展的开放的学说，具有与时俱进的理论品质。马克思主义是时代的产物，并随着时代、实践和科学的发展而不断发展。 1世界的物质性及发展规律 1.1 世界的多样性与物质统一性 1.1.1 物质及其存在方式 全部哲学的基本问题： 存在和思维的关系问题（物质和意识的关系问题） 哲学基本问题主要包括两方面内容： 谁为本原（何者为第一性）——唯心主义&唯物主义 是否具有同一性的问题（思维能否正确地反映存在、人能否认识或彻底认识世界的问题）——可知论&不可知论 唯物主义哲学的理论基石：物质范畴 哲学中，物质的定义： 物质是不依赖于人类的意识而存在，并能为人类的意识所反映的客观实在。 马克思主义的物质观：客观实在性是物质的唯一特性。 坚持唯物主义一元论 坚持能动的反映论和可知论 唯物论和辩证法的统一 唯物主义自然观与历史观的统一。 物质的根本属性： 物质的根本属性是运动。 运动绝对，静止相对（空间相对位置、事物根本属性的相对静止） 基本存在属性：时间（一维性）和空间（三维性） 两者不可分割，证明了两者客观性。 物质、运动、时间、空间具有内在的统一性，要求我们想问题要看具体时间地点条件 物质世界的二重化 世界分化为自然界与人类社会 世界分化为客观世界和主观世界 人的实践活动是分化和统一的关键 1.1.2 物质与意识的辩证关系 物质决定意识 意识 人脑的机能和属性 客观世界的主观映象 客观内容和主观形式的统一 物质对意识的决定作用表现在意识的起源和本质上 意识对物质具有反作用 目的性、计划性 创造性 指导实践改造客观世界的作用 调控人的行为和生理活动的作用 主观能动性和客观规律性的统一 尊重客观规律是正确发挥主观能动性的前提 只有充分发挥主观能动性，才能正确认识和利用客观规律 前提：从实际出发 根本途径：实践 依赖于物质条件和物质手段 坚持遵循客观规律与发挥主观能动性相统一，要求充分发扬历史主动精神 意识与人工智能 人类意识是知情意的统一体，而人工智能只是对人类的理性智能的模拟和扩展 社会性是人的意识所固有的本质属性，而人工智能不可能真正具备人类的社会属性 人类的自然语言是思维的物质外壳和意识的现实形式，而人工智能难以完全具备理解自然语言真实意义的能力 人工智能能够获得人类意识中可以化约为数字信号的内容，但人脑中总有许多东西是无法被化约的 规律： 规律是事物变化发展过程中本身所固有的内在的、本质的、必然的联系 1.1.3世界的物质统一性 世界的统一性在于它的物质性，世界统一于物质。这是辩证唯物主义最基本、最核心的观点，是马克思主义的基石 自然界是物质的。 人类社会本质上是生产实践基础上形成的物质体系。 人的意识统一于物质。 ⭐️1.2 事物的普遍联系和变化发展 1.2.1 联系和发展的普遍性 联系和发展的观点是唯物辩证法的总观点，集中体现了唯物辩证法的总特征。 事物的普遍联系： 客观性 ，坚持联系的客观性，就是在联系的观点上坚持了唯物论 普遍性 （三重含义） 事物内部不同部分和要素之间相互联系（内在结构性） 任何事物不能孤立存在，都同其他事物处于一定的联系之中 整个世界是相互联系的统一整体 多样性 直接联系与间接联系 内部联系与外部联系 本质联系与非本质联系 必然联系与偶然联系 条件性 支持或制约作用 条件可以改变 改变和创造条件不是任意的 事物的变化发展： 实质：新事物的产生和旧事物的灭亡 判断新旧，不在于形式与出现时间先后 新事物是指合乎历史前进方向、具有远大前途的东西 旧事物是指丧失历史必然性、日趋灭亡的东西。 在新陈代谢的发展中，新事物不可战胜的 新事物与环境：有新的要素、结构和功能，它适应已经变化了的环境和条件 新事物与旧事物：新事物是在旧事物的“母体”中孕育成熟的，否定了旧事物中消极腐朽的东西，又保留了旧事物中合理的、适应新条件的因素，并添加了旧事物所不能容纳的新内容。 社会历史领域：根本上符合人民群众的利益和要求，能够得到人民群众的拥护，因而必然战胜旧事物。 1.2.2 对立统一规律是事物发展的根本规律 对立统一规律是唯物辩证法的实质和核心。 对立统一规律揭示了事物普遍联系的根本内容和变化发展的内在动力，从根本上回答了事物为什么会发展的问题。 事物变化发展的一般规律 对立统一规律 （根本规律）（内在动力） 量变质变规律（状态、过程和趋势） 否定之否定规律（状态、过程和趋势） 矛盾是反映事物内部、之间对立统一关系 基本属性：对立（斗争性）和统一（同一性），两者相互依存、相互转化 同一性作用 是事物存在和发展的前提 使矛盾双方相互吸取有利于自身的因素，在相互作用中各自得到发展 同一性规定着事物转化的可能和发展的趋势 矛盾的斗争性在事物发展中的作用表现在： 矛盾双方的斗争促进矛盾双方力量的变化，造成双方力量发展的不平衡，为对立面的转化、事物的质变创造条件 矛盾双方的斗争是一种矛盾统一体向另一种矛盾统一体过渡的决定性力量。 矛盾的同一性和斗争性相互联结、相辅相成 没有斗争性就没有同一性，没有同一性也没有斗争性 斗争性寓于同一性之中，同一性通过斗争性来体现。 矛盾的同一性是有条件的、相对的，矛盾的斗争性是无条件的、绝对的 矛盾的同一性和斗争性相结合，构成了事物的矛盾运动，推动着事物的变化发展 要善于把二者结合起来 ⭐️1.2.2.2 矛盾的普遍性和特殊性及其相互关系 矛盾的普遍性：矛盾存在于一切事物的一切发展过程中 矛盾的特殊性：每个事物、阶段各有其特点；决定了事物的不同性质。 事物的性质是由主要矛盾的主要方面所决定的： 主要矛盾&次要矛盾 在每一对矛盾中，主要方面&次要方面。 要坚持“两点论”和“重点论”的统一： “两点论” 不仅要看到矛盾双方的对立，而且要看到矛盾双方的统一； 不仅要看到矛盾体系中存在主要矛盾、矛盾的主要方面， 而且要看到次要矛盾、矛盾的次要方面。 “重点论”是指要着重把握主要矛盾、矛盾的主要方面，并以此作为解决问题的出发点。 “两点论”和 “重点论”的统一要求我们，看问题既要全面地看，又要看主流、大势、发展趋势 矛盾的普遍性与特殊性的辩证统一关系：矛盾的普遍性和特殊性是辩证统一、相互联系、不可分割的：p47 矛盾的共性是无条件的、绝对的，矛盾的个性是有条件的、相对的。 普遍性寓于特殊性之中 特殊性包含普遍性 普遍性和特殊性在一定条件下相互转化（对于范围的视角的变化） 1.2.2.3 量变质变规律和否定之否定规律 量变质变的辩证关系 量变是质变的必要准备：质变以量变积累为前提 质变是量变的必然结果，并为新的量变开辟道路：量变积累达到一定程度，突破界限时，必然引起质变 量变和质变相互渗透 量变过程包含着部分质变/阶段性质变。 质变过程包含着量的扩张或收缩 事物的发展表现为：由量变到质变，在新质的基础上又开始新的量变，再到新的质变，如此循环往复，不断前进。 量变质变规律体现了事物发展的渐进性和飞跃性的统一。 量变质变规律的方法论意义：重视量的积累；抓住时机，促成质变 否定之否定规律 事物的发展：通过其内在矛盾运动以自我否定的方式而实现的 否定之否定规律：揭示事物自己发展自己的完整过程及本质。 唯物辩证法的否定观（否定的深刻内涵） 事物内部存在肯定因素（维持现存事物存在）和否定因素（促使现存事物灭亡） 是自我否定、自我发展，是事物内部矛盾运动的结果，非外力强加 是发展的环节、通过且仅通过否定，旧事物向新事物转变 联系的环节： 新旧事物是通过否定环节联系起来的。 辩证否定的实质是“扬弃”，即新事物对旧事物既批判又继承，既克服其消极因素又保留其积极因素 事物的辩证否定经过三个阶段：肯定一否定一否定之否定 事物发展的周期性：一个新的、更高层次的肯定阶段，然后又开始新的否定之否定的螺旋上升过程。 前进性（每一次否定都是质变）和曲折性（前进性是趋势，但是并非一帆风顺）的统一 扬弃： 克服其消极的、过时的因素，保留和发扬其积极的、合理的因素，并增添新的内容 1.2.2.4 联系和发展的基本环节 内容与形式、本质与现象、原因与结果、必然与偶然、现实与可能 2 实践与认识及其发展规律 2.1 实践与认识 2.1.1 科学实践观（不断丰富发展的） 意义： 克服旧唯物主义缺陷，为辩证唯物主义奠定理论基础 揭示了实践对认识的决定作用，为能动的、革命的反映论的创立奠定了科学的理论基础 第一次揭示了社会生活的实践本质 为人们能动地认识世界和改造世界提供了基本的思想方法和工作方法 2.1.2 实践的本质与基本结构 2.1.2.1 实践的本质 实践：人类能动地改造世界的社会性的物质活动 特征：客观实在性、自觉能动性和社会历史性 2.1.2.2 实践的基本结构 三项基本要素：实践的主体、客体和中介 实践的主体、客体关系：实践关系（根本）、认识关系和价值关系 实践基本结构发展，表现为主体客体化和客体主体化的双向运动 主体客体化：简单来说就是主体基于主观意识对于客体的改造与创造 客体主体化：简单来说就是主体使用客体，将其内化为一种发展主体的工具 两者都既有物质层面，又有精神层面 2.1.2.3 实践形式的多样性 物质生产实践 社会政治实践 科学文化实践 （产生新的实践形式：虚拟实践） 2.1.2.4 实践对认识的决定作用 实践是认识的基础，有决定作用 实践是认识的来源（与世界相互作用形成感性认识，大脑加工形成理性认识；直接（主要）、间接经验） 实践是认识发展的动力（根本动力、提供必要条件、实践本身也会增加认识） 实践是认识的目的 实践是检验认识真理性的唯一标准 认识具有真理性与否只有在实践中才能得到验证。 实践标准的确定性 （唯一标准） 与不确定性 （历史发展性） 是辩证统一的。 2.1.3 认识的本质与过程 2.1.3.1 认识的本质 辩证唯物主义认识论（反映论）：认识的本质是主体在实践基础上对客体的能动反映。这种能动反映具有两个基本特征： 反映性：人类认识的基本规定性，指认识必须以客观事物为原型，在思维中再现其状态、属性和本质 能动的创造性：一种在思维中进行的能动、创造性的活动，人需要透过现象把握本质，用辩证思维方法在观念中加工和改造对象 两者辩证统一、不可分割的。它们不是同一本质的两个方面： 创造离不开反映：创造过程是在对多个方面进行反映的基础上实现的。 反映也离不开创造：反映是在创造过程中实现的。 两种错误的倾向及其危害： 只坚持反映性而忽视创造性，会重蹈旧唯物主义直观反映论的覆辙。 只坚持创造性而脱离反映的前提，会使创造变成主观随意，从而滑向唯心主义和不可知论。 2.1.3.2 从实践到认识 认识的过程：认识到实践，实践再到认识 实践与认识的两次飞跃： 实践与认识的辨证运动，是一个由感性认识到理性认识，又由理性认识到实践的飞跃。 感性认识和理性认识的辩证关系： 感性认识（直接，包括感觉（各个感觉）->知觉（整体反应）->表象（对过去感觉、直觉的回忆）） 理性认识（概念->判断->推理） 理性认识依赖于感性认识（认识论的唯物论） 感性认识有待于发展和深化为理性认识 感性认识和理性认识相互渗透、相互包含 感性认识到理性认识条件：实践->思考 认识过程中有非理性因素 2.1.3.3 从认识到实践 从认识回到实践的必要性和重要性： 认识世界的目的是改造世界： 认识的真理性只有在实践中才能得到检验和发展： 2.1.4 实践与认识的辨证运动及其规律 说实践与认识“完成了”，是针对具体事物的认识而言的 实现预期目的，使预想的思想、理论或计划在实践中大体变为事实，部分甚至全部调整 说它“又没有完成”，是针对实践和认识运动的持续发展而言的 人类的实践是不断向前推移和发展的，因此人们的认识也必须随之发展 客观现实世界的运动变化永不完结，因此人们在实践中对真理的认识也永远没有完结 2.2 真理与价值 2.2.1 真理的客观性、绝对性和相对性 真理的定义： 标志主观与客观相符合的哲学范畴，是对客观事物及其规律的正确反映。 真理的客观性： 真理的内容是对客观事物及其规律的正确反映（决定真理（内容而非形式）的一元性） 真理的绝对性和相对性： 真理的绝对性 ：主客观统一的确定性、发展的无限性 真理的相对性：在一定条件下对客观事物及其本质和发展规律的正确认识总是有限度的、不完善的 客观世界的整体来看，任何真理都只是对客观世界的某一阶段、某一部分的正确认识，有待扩展 就特定事物而言，任何真理都只是对客观对象一定方面、一定层次和一定程度的正确认识，任何真理都只能是主观对客观事物近似正确即相对正确的反映 真理的绝对性和相对性的辩证统一 两重性：两者相互包含 发展上：人类的认识是一个无限的过程，永远在从相对真理走向、接近绝对真理。 真理与谬误的对立统一 在确定的对象和范围内，两者相互对立 在一定范围内才有绝对的意义，超出之后就相对了 2.2.2 真理的检验标准 2.2.2.2实践是检验真理的唯一标准 实践之所以能够作为检验真理的唯一标准，是由真理的本性和实践的特点决定的。 本性：真理是人们对客观事物及其发展规律的正确反映，其本性在于主观和客观相符合。 实践：实践具有直接现实性。实践的直接现实性是它的客观实在性的具体表现。 2.2.2.3 实践标准的确定性与不确定性 确定性：绝对性，是指实践作为检验真理标准的唯一性、归根到底性、最终性 不确定性：相对性，实践作为检验真理标准的条件性 实践受到主客观制约 实践收到历史条件限制 2.2.3 真理与价值的辩证统一 2.2.3.1 价值 主体性、客观性、多维性和社会历史性 价值的主体性：直接与主体相联系，始终以主体为中心 价值关系的形成依赖于主体的存在 价值关系的形成依赖于主体的创造，使客体潜在的价值转化为现实的价值 价值的客观性：一定条件下客体对于主体的意义不依赖于主体的主观意识而存在 主体的存在和需要是客观的，而不是抽象的 客体的存在、属性及作用是客观的 价值的多维性：同一客体相对于主体的不同需要会产生不同的价值 价值的社会历史性：主体和客体的不断变化决定了价值的历史性 2.2.3.3 价值评价及其特点 价值评价是对客观价值关系的主观反映 评价以主客体之间的价值关系为认识对象 评价结果与评价主体直接相关 评价结果的正确与否依赖于对客体状况和主体需要的认识 评价结果有正确与错误之分，价值评价也有科学与非科学之别 2.2.3.5真理与价值在实践中的辩证统一 人们的实践活动总是受着真理尺度和价值尺度的制约 辩证关系： 价值尺度必须以真理为前提，脱离了真理尺度，价值尺度就偏离了合理的、正确的轨道 人类自身需要的内在尺度，推动着人们不断发现新的真理，脱离了价值尺度，真理就缺失了主体意义 实践的具体性和历史性->真理尺度与价值尺度的统一也是具体的、历史的 两者是否达成统一，用实践验证 2.3 认识世界和改造世界 2.3.1 认识世界的根本目的在于改造世界 2.3.1.1 认识世界和改造世界有辩证关系 认识世界有助于改造世界 人们只有在改造世界的实践中才能不断地深化、拓展对世界的正确认识 2.3.1.2 改造客观世界和改造主观世界及其辩证关系 只有在改造客观世界的实践中，才能深入改造主观世界 只有认真改造主观世界，才能更好地改造客观世界 2.3.1.3 认识世界和改造世界的过程是从必然走向自由的过程 自由的条件： 认识条件：对客观事物（的发展）的正确认识 实践条件：能够将获得的规律性认识运用于指导实践，实现改造世界的目的 3 人类社会及其发展规律 3.1 人类社会的存在与发展 3.1.1 社会存在与社会意识 社会存在：社会物质生活条件，是社会生活的物质方面 自然地理环境 人口因素 物质生产方式 是人类社会赖以存在和发展的基础，是人类其他一切活动的首要前提。 决定社会的结构、性质和面貌 决定整个社会历史的变化发展，决定社会形态从低级向高级的更替和发展。 社会意识：社会存在的反映，是社会生活的精神方面 意识形态（政治法律思想、道德、艺术、宗教、哲学等） 非意识形态（自然科学和语言学、形式逻辑） 社会存在与社会意识的辩证关系： 社会存在决定社会意识 社会存在是社会意识内容的客观来源，社会意识是社会物质生活过程及其条件的主观反映 社会意识是人们进行社会物质交往的产物。 社会意识是具体的、历史的。 社会意识是社会存在的反映，并反作用于社会存在 （社会意识具有相对独立性）： 社会意识与社会存在发展具有不完全同步性和不平衡性 社会意识内部各种形式之间存在相互影响且各自具有历史继承性 社会意识对社会存在具有能动的反作用，这是社会意识相对独立性的突出表现。 3.1.2 社会基本矛盾及其运动规律 3.1.2.1 生产力与生产关系的矛盾运动及其规律 生产力： 生产实践中所需的物质力量，客观现实性、社会历史性 基本要素包括：劳动资料、劳动对象、劳动者 劳动者是生产力中最重要、最活跃、起决定性作用的因素。 在生产过程中，劳动者使用劳动资料，作用于劳动对象，从而生产出物质产品。劳动资料和劳动对象合称为 “生产资料”。 科学技术是生产力中的重要因素： 引起劳动资料、劳动对象和劳动者素质的深刻变革和巨大进步 提高管理效率 提高劳动生产率 科学技术是第一生产力 生产关系：生产关系是人们在物质生产过程中形成的不以人的意志为转移的经济关系，其中生产资料所有制关系最基本，目前公有制和私有制并存 生产力与生产关系的相互关系是 生产力决定生产关系。 生产力状况决定生产关系的性质 生产力的发展决定生产关系的变化。生产关系是生产力发展需要的产物，只有当它为生产力提供足够的发展空间时才能够存在。 生产关系对生产力具有能动的反作用 当生产关系适合生产力发展的客观要求时，对生产力的发展起推动作用 当生产关系不适合生产力发展的客观要求时，就会阻碍生产力的发展。 3.1.2.2 经济基础与上层建筑的矛盾运动及其规律 经济基础： 经济基础是指由社会一定发展阶段的生产力所决定的生产关系的总和。 决定一个社会性质的是其中占支配地位的生产关系。 上层建筑： 上层建筑是建立在一定经济基础之上的意识形态以及与之相适应的制度、组织和设施 政治上层建筑居于主导地位 国家政权：用暴力把社会冲突保持在秩序范围内 在整个上层建筑中，政治上层建筑居于主导地位，国家政权是政治上层建筑的核心 国体：社会各阶级在国家中的地位 政体：统治阶级用何形式组织自己的政权 经济基础与上层建筑的辩证统一关系： 经济基础决定上层建筑。 决定其产生（怎样的上层建筑） 决定其性质（为谁服务） 决定其变更 上层建筑对经济基础具有反作用。 上层建筑积极地服务于经济基础。 促进作用：当上层建筑适合经济基础状况时，促进经济基础的巩固和发展 阻碍作用：当上层建筑不适合经济基础状况时，阻碍新的、先进的经济基础的形成和发展。 再次，经济基础与上层建筑的相互作用构成二者的矛盾运动 上层建筑的不完善部分、没有反映经济基础要求的部分同经济基础发生矛盾 现在占统治地位的经济基础同旧上层建筑的残余、未来上层建筑的萌芽之间的矛盾，新旧上层建筑之间、新旧经济基础之间的矛盾 社会形态上升时，上层建筑适应经济基础，下降时则为对抗 最后，经济基础和上层建筑之间的内在联系构成了上层建筑“一定要适合”经济基础状况的规律 经济基础状况决定上层建筑的发展方向，决定上层建筑相应的调整或变革； 上层建筑的反作用也必须取决于和服从于经济基础的性质和客观要求 3.1.3 交往 作用： 促进生产力的发展 促进社会关系的进步 促进文化的发展与传播 促进人的全面发展 3.1.4 社会进步与社会形态更替 社会形态从低级到高级的发展、同一社会形态内部的发展，社会进步促进人的发展、推动人类解放 社会形态更替的统一性和多样性： 统一性：原始社会、奴隶社会、封建社会、资本主义社会和共产主义社会依次更替 多样性：可能跨越，可能不典型，可能迅速缓慢，可能曲折 社会形态更替的必然性与选择性： 必然性 社会形态依次更替客观 生产力与生产关系矛盾运动的规律性，从根本上规定了社会形态更替的必然性 选择性 必然性造成了社会发展的基本趋势，为选择性提供空间 主观能动性与客观规律性相统一的过程 人们的历史选择性归根结底是人民群众的选择性 3.2 社会发展的动力 3.2.1 社会基本矛盾是历史发展的根本动力 社会基本矛盾： 生产力与生产关系之间的矛盾（根本） 经济基础与上层建筑之间的矛盾（体现） 作用体现在： 生产力是社会基本矛盾运动中最基本的动力因素 生产力是社会存在和发展的物质基础 生产力决定生产关系的性质 生产力是社会进步的根本内容 社会基本矛盾特别是生产力和生产关系的矛盾，决定着社会中其他矛盾的存在和发展 生产力和生产关系的矛盾决定经济基础和上层建筑的矛盾的产生和发展 经济基础和上层建筑的矛盾也会影响和制约生产力和生产关系的矛盾 社会基本矛盾具有不同的表现形式和解决方式 社会形态改变：革命 统一社会形态的发展：改革 社会主要矛盾：不同于基本矛盾，会不断向下变化，是基本矛盾的体现 社会主要矛盾双方的内容发生一定变化 矛盾的地位发生变化 3.2.2 阶级斗争、社会革命在社会发展中的作用 阶级斗争是社会基本矛盾在阶级社会中的表现 社会革命是社会基本矛盾所引起的广泛而深刻的社会变革的统称 阶级斗争 是阶级社会发展的直接动力 根源于阶级之间物质利益的根本对立，根源于社会经济关系的冲突 作用表现在社会形态的更替 受到一定社会历史条件的制约 社会革命 根源于社会基本矛盾的尖锐化，需要客观和主观条件 实现社会形态更替的重要手段和决定性环节 改革 为了解决社会基本矛盾而对生产关系和上层建筑进行的深刻的改变和革新 社会制度的自我调整和完善 量变和部分质变 3.2.3 科学技术在社会发展中的作用 科技革命是推动经济和社会发展的强大杠杆 对生产方式产生了深刻影响。 改变了社会生产力的构成要素（使劳动力结构向着智能化趋势发展） 改变了人们的劳动形式（由机械自动化走向智能自动化、由局部自动化走向大系统管理和控制自动化的根本性变革） 改变了社会经济结构，特别是导致产业结构发生变革。（第三产业人数比例增长） 对生活方式产生了巨大影响 促进了思维方式的变革 3.2.3 文化在社会发展中的作用 文化是推动社会发展的重要力量，为社会发展提供：思想指引、精神动力、凝聚力量 3.3 人民群众在历史发展中的作用 3.3.1 人民群众是历史的创造者 唯物史观与唯心史观的对立，在历史创造者问题上表现为群众史观（唯物史观）与英雄史观（唯心史观）的对立。 群众史观并不否认英雄在历史上的重要作用。ta们顺应了历史发展的规律，反映人民群众的愿望和要求，加速历史的进程，无法改变其根本方向 唯物史观： 立足于现实的人及其本质来把握历史的创造者 立足于整体的社会历史过程来探究谁是历史的创造者 唯物史观从社会历史发展的必然性入手来考察和说明谁是历史的创造者 唯物史观从人与历史关系的不同层次上考察谁是历史的创造者 人民群众在创造历史过程中的决定作用： 人民群众是社会历史的主体，是历史的创造者。 人民群众是社会物质财富的创造者（物质生产是基础，群众是生产者） 人民群众是社会精神财富的创造者（虽然常常由杰出的知识分子和艺术家集中体现，但其最终源泉依然是人民群众的社会实践。） 人民群众是社会变革的决定力量（阶级斗争的主力、社会革命的根本动力） 4 资本主义的本质及规律 4.1 商品经济和价值规律 4.1.1 商品经济的形成和发展 自然经济：产的目的是直接满足生产者个人或经济单位的需要 原始社会、奴隶社会、封建社会，因为生产力水平很低，社会分工极不发达 商品经济：以交换为目的而进行生产的经济形式 产生的历史条件： 存在社会分工（前提） 生产资料和劳动产品属于不同的所有者（决定性） 商品的二因素： 二因素： 使用价值（自然属性，客观、具体、商品价值的物质承载） 价值（社会属性，人脑力和体力的耗费，是由社会必要的劳动时间而非劳动者实际的劳动时间决定的） 1234567891011flowchart TD A[一个物品存在]:::green --> B{是否有用}:::green B -->|是| C{是否人类劳动的产物}:::green B -->|否| D[无用物]:::green C -->|是| E{是否为了交换而生产}:::green C -->|否| F[自然物（如空气）<br>有使用价值，无价值]:::green E -->|是| G[商品<br>有使用价值、价值]:::green E -->|否| H[自用品<br>有使用价值，无价值]:::green classDef green fill:#e6ffe6,stroke:#2db300,color:#006600,text-align:center class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H green 商品的使用价值和价值之间是对立统一的关系： 对立性： 商品的使用价值和价值是相互排斥的，生产者关心价值而不是使用价值，将使用价值让渡给购买者，才能取得价值 统一性： 作为商品，必须同时具有使用价值和价值两个因素 使用价值是价值的物质承担者，价值寓于使用价值之中 商品是劳动产品，生产商品的劳动具有二重性 具体劳动：创造商品的使用价值（例如种地） 抽象劳动：形成商品的价值（例如劳动了5小时） 劳动的二重性决定了商品的二因素：任何劳动，既是特殊的具体劳动，又是一般的抽象劳动 具体劳动和抽象劳动也是对立统一的关系： 两者不独立存在，在时间上和空间上统一的两个方面 两者反映劳动的不同属性，前者自然属性，后者社会属性。 商品价值量的决定 第一层面：核心尺度是“社会必要劳动时间”，而非“个别劳动时间” 第二层面：价值量与“劳动生产率”成反比 第三层面：价值量以“简单劳动”为尺度，复杂劳动可换算（自发计算，而非主动计算，产生数倍于简单劳动的价值） 4.1.2 价值规律及其作用 价值规律在市场配置资源过程中的作用表现在： 自发地调节生产资料和劳动力在社会各生产部门之间的比例 自发地刺激社会生产力的发展 自发地调节社会收入的分配 消极后果： 社会资源浪费 阻碍技术进步 收入两极分化 以私有制为基础的商品经济的基本矛盾： 123456flowchart LR A[商品<br>使用价值与价值的矛盾]-->|根源于|B[私人劳动与社会劳动的矛盾] C[生产商品<br>具体劳动和抽象劳动的矛盾]-->|根源于|B B-->|构成|D[商品经济的基本矛盾] classDef green fill:#e6ffe6,stroke:#2db300,color:#006600,text-align:center class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H green 理解：在私有制商品经济中，每个人的劳动表面上是为自己干的、独立的私人劳动，但本质上又是互相联系、 为社会生产的社会劳动。这两者之间存在着深刻的矛盾。这个矛盾需要通过市场交换来临时解决，但又因为解决得不彻底而不断引发新的矛盾，从而推动着整个商品经济的运行、发展乃至危机 私人劳动和社会劳动的矛盾构成私有制基础上商品经济的基本矛盾 决定着商品经济的本质及发展过程 是商品经济其他一切矛盾的基础 决定着商品生产者的命运 4.2 资本主义经济制度 4.2.2 劳动力成为商品与货币转化为资本 G代表货币，W代表商品 代表货币的货币：W-G-W 代表资本的货币：G-W-G' 劳动力：人的劳动能力，人的脑力和体力的总和，其成为商品的基本条件： 劳动者在法律上是自由人，能够把自己的劳动力当作自己的商品来支配； 劳动者没有任何生产资料，没有生活资料来源，因而不得不依靠出卖劳动力为生。 劳动力的价值：（生产、发展、维持和延续劳动力所必需的生活必需品的价值决定的） 维持劳动者本人生存所必需的生活资料的价值； 维持劳动者家属的生存所必需的生活资料的价值; 劳动者接受教育和训练所支出的费用。 （通俗地讲，就是工人的“饭钱、房租、衣食住行、养家糊口”等费用的总和。） 劳动力商品的特点： 使用价值是价值的源泉，创造新的大于劳动力本身价值价值，而且这个新的价值比劳动力本身的价值更大。（因此产生了剩余价值） 因此：货币所有者购买到劳动力以后，在消费过程中，不仅能够收回他在购买这种特殊商品时支付的价值，还能得到一个增殖的价值即剩余价值。（为什么资本能够盈利） 资本是能够带来剩余价值的价值。剩余价值是由雇佣工人的剩余劳动创造的。 4.2.3 生产剩余价值是资本主义生产方式的绝对规律 资本主义生产过程具有二重性，为以下两者的统一： 生产物质资料的劳动过程； 生产剩余价值的过程 雇佣工人的劳动分为两部分： 必要劳动，用于再生产劳动力的价值 剩余劳动，用于无偿地为资本家生产剩余价值。 不变资本与可变资本： p211 不变资本是以生产资料形态存在的资本 生产资料的价值通过工人的具体劳动被转移到新产品中，其转移的价值量不会大于它原有的价值量。（只转移，不增值） 可变资本是用来购买劳动力的那部分资本 可变资本的价值在生产过程中不是被转移到新产品中去，而是由工人的劳动再生产出来。 要确定资本家对工人的剥削程度，就应该用剩余价值和雇佣劳动者的可变资本相比，而不应该把它去同全部资本相比 4.2.3.2 剩余价值生产的两种方法 绝对剩余价值生产：劳动时间不变，延长工作日长度/提高劳动强度 相对剩余价值生产：指在工作日长度不变的条件下，通过缩短必要劳动时间而相对延长剩余劳动时间所生产的剩余价值（提高社会劳动生产率） 4.2.3.3 资本积累 资本积累：剩余价值的资本化 资本积累的源泉是剩余价值 资本积累规模的大小取决于 资本家对工人的剥削程度 劳动生产率的高低 所用资本和所费资本之间的差额 资本家预付资本的大小。 导致财富占有两极分化、失业现象 4.2.4 资本主义的基本矛盾与经济危机 资本主义基本矛盾：p225 生产社会化和生产资料资本主义私人占有之间的矛盾，是资本主义的基本矛盾。 在现实中主要表现为两大具体矛盾： 单个企业内部生产的有组织性和整个社会生产的无政府状态之间的矛盾。 资本主义生产无限扩大的趋势与劳动人民有支付能力的需求相对缩小之间的矛盾。 资本主义经济危机： p226 本质特征：（相对）生产过剩 这种过剩是相对过剩，即相对于劳动人民有支付能力的需求，而不是相对于劳动人民的实际需要 5 资本主义的发展及其趋势 5.1 垄断资本主义的形成与发展 垄断原因： 当生产集中发展到相当高的程度，极少数企业就会联合起来，操纵和控制本部门的生产和销售，实行垄断，以获得高额利润 企业规模巨大，形成对竞争的限制，也会产生垄断 激烈的竞争给竞争各方带来的损失越来越严重，为了避免两败俱伤，企业之间会达成妥协，联合起来，实行垄断 垄断与竞争关系：在自由竞争中形成的，是作为自由竞争的对立面产生的。但是，垄断并不能消除竞争，反而使竞争变得更加复杂和激烈： 垄断没有消除产生竞争的经济条件 垄断必须通过竞争来维持 任何垄断组织都不可能把包罗万象的社会生产全部包下来，使竞争更加激烈 垄断价格既不能增加也不能减少整个社会所生产的价值总量，它只是对商品价值和剩余价值作了有利于垄断资本的再分配。 国家垄断资本主义：国家垄断资本主义是国家政权和私人垄断资本融合在一起的垄断资本主义。 国家所有并直接经营企业 国家与私人共有、合营企业 国家通过多种形式参与私人垄断资本的再生产过程 宏观调节 微观规制 经济全球化的表现：生产全球化（国际分工）、贸易全球化、金融全球化 经济全球化的动因： 科学技术的进步和生产力的发展为经济全球化提供了坚实的物质基础和根本的推动力。（特别是信息革命） 跨国公司的发展为经济全球化提供了适宜的企业组织形式。（利用各地的优势组织生产） 各国经济体制的变革和国际经济组织的发展是经济全球化的体制与组织保障。 5.3资本主义的历史地位 5.3.1 历史地位 与封建社会相比，资本主义显示了巨大的历史进步性 资本主义将科学技术转变为强大的生产力 资本追求剩余价值的内在动力和竞争的外在压力推动了社会生产力的迅速发展 资本主义的意识形态和政治制度动了社会生产力的迅速发展，促进了社会进步 局限性 资本主义的基本矛盾阻碍社会生产力的发展 财富占有两极分化，引发经济危机 资产阶级支配和控制资本主义经济和政治的发展和运行，不断激化社会矛盾和冲突 5.3.2被替代的历史必然性 资本主义基本矛盾随发展不断显现 资本积累推动资本主义基本矛盾不断激化并最终否定资本主义自身 国家垄断资本主义是资本社会化的更高形式，将成为社会主义的前奏 资本主义社会存在着资产阶级和无产阶级两大阶级之间的矛盾和斗争 6 社会主义的发展及其规律 6.1 社会主义五百年的历史进程 6.1.1社会主义从空想到科学 空想社会主义发展阶段： 16-17世纪的早期空想社会主义 18世纪的空想平均共产主义 19世纪初期批判的空想社会主义 开山之作：1516 年托马斯·莫尔所的《乌托邦》 空想社会主义理论的意义： 对资本主义旧制度的辛辣批判，包含重要见解 反映了早期无产阶级迫切要求改造现存社会、建立理想的新社会的愿望 空想社会主义“提供了启发工人觉悟的极为宝责的祠料”，但是不具备科学的和实践的品格。 空想社会主义的局限性： 没有指出社会发展的真正出路。没有阐明资本主义雇佣制的本质 没有发现资本主义发展规律 没有找到成为新社会的创造者的社会力量 科学社会主义：唯物史观和剩余价值学说 科学社会主义>空想社会主义 科学理论 经济根源 揭示资本主义基本矛盾 依靠人民作为埋葬力量 提供路径指引、实现方式 6.3 在实践中探索社会主义的发展规律 社会主义建设过程的长期性 生产力发展状况的制约 经济基础和上层建筑发展状况的制约。 国际环境的严峻挑战 马克思主义执政党对社会主义发展道路的探索和对社会主义建设规律的认识，需要一个长期的过程。 7 共产主义崇高理想及其最终实现 7.1 展望未来共产主义新社会 预见未来社会的方法论原则 在揭示人类社会发展一般规律的基础上指明社会发展的方向 在剖析资本主义社会旧世界中阐发未来新世界的特点 在社会主义社会发展中不断深化对未来共产主义社会的认识 立足于揭示未来社会的一般特征，而不作详尽的细节描绘 共产主义社会的基本特征 物质财富极大丰富，消费资料按需分配 社会关系高度和谐，人们精神境界极大提高 阶级将会消亡 国家将会消亡（政府不会） 战争将不复存在。 由于社会生产力的巨大发展，工业与农业、城市与乡村、脑力劳动与体力劳动的差别即“三大差别”必将归于消失。 不仅社会是和谐的，而且社会与自然之间也将达成和谐。 人们的精神境界将得到极大提高。 实现每个人自由而全面的发展，人类从必然王国向自由王国的飞跃 实现人的自由而全面的发展，是马克思主义追求的根本价值目标也是共产主义社会的根本特征。 旧式分工的消除为人的自由而全面的发展创造条件 自由时间的延长为人的自由而全面的发展提供了广阔的前景 劳动不再是单纯的谋生手段，而成为“生活的第一需要”
items.content_en: Basic Principles of Marxism 0 Introduction 0.1 What is Marxism? The three basic components of Marxism: Marxist philosophy, Marxist political economy, and scientific socialism When studying the basic principles of Marxism, we focus on: Basic stand: The fundamental standpoint and starting point of Marxism in observing, analyzing, and solving problems. It takes the liberation of the proletariat and all humanity as its mission, and the free and comprehensive development of human beings as its ultimate goal. It is people-centered, insisting on doing everything for the people, relying on the people, and wholeheartedly seeking happiness for the people. Basic views: Scientific understanding of the general laws governing the development of nature, society, and human thought Scientific understanding of the laws of development of capitalist and socialist societies Scientific summary of the achievements of human thought and the experience of social practice Basic methods: Methods of thought and work that are founded on the worldview and methodology of dialectical materialism and historical materialism, guiding us to correctly understand and transform the world. 0.2 The Creation and Development of Marxism The social roots, class basis, and intellectual roots of Marxism: Social roots: Extreme polarization of society, with workers in extreme misery Frequent outbreak of cyclical economic crises Class basis: The rise of the workers' movement marked the modern proletariat's appearance on the historical stage as an independent political force. The Lyon workers' uprising in France The Chartist movement in Britain The Silesian weavers' uprising in Germany Intellectual roots: Direct theoretical sources: German classical philosophy, British classical political economy, and French and British utopian socialism Premises from the natural sciences: The three great scientific discoveries of the 19th century, namely cell theory, the law of conservation and transformation of energy, and the theory of biological evolution. Major Works: Marx and Engels co-wrote The German Ideology, which for the first time systematically expounded the basic viewpoints of historical materialism and achieved a great revolution in the conception of history. The publication of The Communist Manifesto marked the public debut of Marxism. Das Kapital systematically expounded the theory of surplus value. Historical materialism and the theory of surplus value are the two great discoveries of Marx's life. From 1876 to 1878, Engels wrote Anti-Dühring, which comprehensively expounded the theoretical system of Marxism. The basic path of Marxist innovation and development: Indigenization and modernization are the basic paths of Marxist innovation and development. Indigenization: The process of integrating the basic principles of Marxism with the national conditions of different countries, taking root and flourishing in each country. Modernization: The process of combining the basic principles of Marxism with the characteristics of the times, answering new questions of the era, and always grasping and leading the times. The fruits of the Sinicization of Marxism: Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Important Thought of "Three Represents," the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. 0.3 The Basic Characteristics of Marxism The basic characteristics of Marxism: distinct scientificity, people-centeredness, practicality, and developmental character (the unity of scientificity and revolutionaryness). These are the essence, mission, and theoretical image of Marxism. A scientific theory: Marxism is a correct reflection of the nature and laws of the development of nature, society, and human thought. It arose on the basis of social practice and scientific development, and in the course of its own development it constantly summarizes practical experience and absorbs the latest achievements of the natural and social sciences. A people's theory: People-centeredness is the essential attribute of Marxism; putting the people first is the political stance of Marxism. A practical theory: Marxism is a doctrine that comes from practice, goes to practice, is tested in practice, and develops continuously with practice. A developing theory: Marxism is an ever-developing and open doctrine, with the theoretical quality of advancing with the times. Marxism is a product of the times and develops continuously with the times, with practice, and with science. 1 The Materiality of the World and Its Laws of Development 1.1 The Diversity of the World and Its Unity in Matter 1.1.1 Matter and Its Modes of Existence The fundamental question of all philosophy: the relation between being and thinking (the relation between matter and consciousness) The fundamental question of philosophy mainly includes two aspects: Which is primary (which is the first principle) — Idealism & Materialism Whether they have identity (whether thinking can correctly reflect being; whether humans can know or completely know the world) — Agnosticism & Gnosticism (knowability) The theoretical cornerstone of materialist philosophy: the category of matter In philosophy, the definition of matter: Matter is objective reality that exists independently of human consciousness and can be reflected by human consciousness. The Marxist view of matter: Objective reality is the only property of matter. Adhering to materialist monism Adhering to active reflection theory and knowability The unity of materialism and dialectics The unity of the materialist view of nature and the materialist view of history. The fundamental property of matter: The fundamental property of matter is motion. Motion is absolute, rest is relative (relative rest in spatial position and in the fundamental properties of things) Basic modes of existence: time (one-dimensionality) and space (three-dimensionality) The two are inseparable, which proves their objectivity. Matter, motion, time, and space have inherent unity, requiring us to consider specific time, place, and conditions when thinking about problems. The duality of the material world The world is divided into nature and human society The world is divided into the objective world and the subjective world Human practical activity is the key to both the division and the unity. 1.1.2 The Dialectical Relationship between Matter and Consciousness Matter determines consciousness Consciousness Is a function and attribute of the human brain Is the subjective image of the objective world Is the unity of objective content and subjective form The determining role of matter over consciousness is manifested in the origin and essence of consciousness. Consciousness has a reaction on matter Purposefulness and planning Creativity Its role in guiding practice to transform the objective world Its role in regulating human behavior and physiological activities The unity of subjective initiative and objective law Respecting objective laws is the prerequisite for correctly exercising subjective initiative Only by fully exercising subjective initiative can we correctly understand and utilize objective laws Prerequisite: proceeding from reality Fundamental path: practice Dependence on material conditions and material means To insist on the unity of following objective laws and exercising subjective initiative requires giving full play to the historical initiative spirit. Consciousness and artificial intelligence Human consciousness is a unity of cognition, emotion, and will, whereas artificial intelligence is only a simulation and extension of human rational intelligence. Sociality is an inherent essential attribute of human consciousness, and artificial intelligence cannot truly possess human social attributes. Human natural language is the material shell of thought and the actual form of consciousness, while artificial intelligence can hardly fully possess the ability to understand the true meaning of natural language. Artificial intelligence can obtain the content in human consciousness that can be reduced to digital signals, but there is always much in the human brain that cannot be reduced. Laws: A law is the inherent, essential, and necessary connection that exists in the process of the change and development of things. 1.1.3 The Unity of the World in Matter The unity of the world lies in its materiality; the world is unified in matter. This is the most basic and most important viewpoint of dialectical materialism and the cornerstone of Marxism. Nature is material. Human society is essentially a material system formed on the basis of material production practice. Human consciousness is unified in matter. ⭐️1.2 The Universal Connection and Change and Development of Things 1.2.1 The Universality of Connection and Development The viewpoints of connection and development are the overall viewpoints of materialist dialectics, embodying its general characteristics. The universal connection of things: Objectivity: Insisting on the objectivity of connection means adhering to materialism from the perspective of connection. Universality (three meanings) Different parts and elements within a thing are interconnected (internal structure) No thing can exist in isolation; everything is connected with other things to some degree. The whole world is a unified whole of interconnected things. Diversity Direct connections and indirect connections Internal connections and external connections Essential connections and non-essential connections Necessary connections and accidental connections Conditionality Supports or restricts Conditions can be changed Changing and creating conditions is not arbitrary. The change and development of things: Essence: The emergence of new things and the extinction of old things To judge whether something is new or old, we do not rely on its form or the time of its appearance. New things are those that conform to the direction of historical progress and have a promising future. Old things are those that have lost historical necessity and are heading toward extinction. In the metabolism of development, new things are invincible. New things and the environment: They have new elements, structures, and functions, and they adapt to the changed environment and conditions. New things and old things: New things mature in the "womb" of old things. They negate the negative and decadent elements of old things, preserve the reasonable factors in old things that suit new conditions, and add new content that old things cannot contain. In the field of social history: They fundamentally conform to the interests and demands of the people, win the support of the masses, and therefore necessarily defeat old things. 1.2.2 The Law of the Unity of Opposites Is the Fundamental Law of the Development of Things The law of the unity of opposites is the essence and core of materialist dialectics. The law of the unity of opposites reveals the fundamental content of the universal connection of things and the internal motive force of their change and development, fundamentally answering the question of why things develop. The general laws of the change and development of things The law of the unity of opposites (fundamental law) (internal motive force) The law of quantitative and qualitative change (state, process, and trend) The law of the negation of negation (state, process, and trend) Contradiction reflects the unity of opposites within and between things. Basic attributes: opposition (struggle) and unity (identity), which are interdependent and mutually transform. The role of identity It is the premise of the existence and development of things. It enables the two sides of a contradiction to absorb factors favorable to themselves and develop through mutual interaction. Identity determines the possibility of transformation and the trend of development. The role of struggle in the development of things: The struggle between the two sides of a contradiction promotes changes in their respective forces, creating an imbalance in their development and preparing the conditions for the transformation of opposites and for qualitative change. The struggle between the two sides of a contradiction is the decisive force that enables one contradictory unity to transition to another. The identity and struggle of contradictions are interconnected and mutually reinforcing. Without struggle there is no identity, and without identity there is no struggle. Struggle resides in identity, and identity is manifested through struggle. The identity of contradictions is conditional and relative, while the struggle of contradictions is unconditional and absolute. The combination of identity and struggle constitutes the contradictory movement of things, driving their change and development. We should be good at combining the two. ⭐️1.2.2.2 The Universality and Particularity of Contradictions and Their Interrelationship The universality of contradictions: Contradictions exist in the entire process of development of all things. The particularity of contradictions: Each thing and each stage has its own characteristics; this determines the different qualities of things. The quality of a thing is determined by the principal aspect of the principal contradiction: Principal contradiction & secondary contradiction Within each pair of contradictions, the principal aspect and the secondary aspect. We must adhere to the unity of "two-point theory" and "key-point theory": "Two-point theory" We must see not only the opposition but also the unity of the two sides of a contradiction. We must see not only the principal contradiction and the principal aspect of a contradiction in the system of contradictions, but also the secondary contradictions and the secondary aspects. "Key-point theory" means focusing on the principal contradiction and the principal aspect of the contradiction, and taking them as the starting point for solving problems. The unity of "two-point theory" and "key-point theory" requires us to look at problems comprehensively, and also to grasp the mainstream, the general trend, and the direction of development. The dialectical unity of the universality and particularity of contradictions: The universality and particularity of contradictions are dialectically unified, interconnected, and inseparable: p47 The commonality of contradictions is unconditional and absolute, while the particularity of contradictions is conditional and relative. Universality resides in particularity. Particularity contains universality. Universality and particularity can transform into each other under certain conditions (with changes in the scope of perspective). 1.2.2.3 The Law of Quantitative and Qualitative Change and the Law of the Negation of Negation The Dialectical Relationship between Quantitative and Qualitative Change Quantitative change is the necessary preparation for qualitative change: Qualitative change is premised on the accumulation of quantitative change. Qualitative change is the inevitable result of quantitative change and opens up new possibilities for further quantitative change: When quantitative accumulation reaches a certain degree and breaks through the limit, qualitative change inevitably occurs. Quantitative change and qualitative change interpenetrate each other. The process of quantitative change contains partial qualitative change / qualitative change at certain stages. The process of qualitative change contains quantitative expansion or contraction. The development of things manifests as: from quantitative change to qualitative change, then on the new basis of the new quality a new round of quantitative change begins, followed by another qualitative change, and so on in an endless cycle, continuously advancing. The law of quantitative and qualitative change embodies the unity of the gradualness and leap in the development of things. Methodological significance of the law of quantitative and qualitative change: Attach importance to the accumulation of quantity; seize the moment to bring about qualitative change. The Law of the Negation of Negation The development of things: Realized through the movement of internal contradictions in the form of self-negation. The law of the negation of negation: Reveals the complete process and essence of things developing themselves. The materialist dialectical view of negation (the profound connotation of negation) Within things there are affirmative factors (maintaining the existence of the existing thing) and negative factors (promoting the extinction of the existing thing). Negation is self-negation and self-development, a result of the movement of internal contradictions of things, not something imposed by external forces. Negation is the link of development. Only through negation does an old thing transform into a new thing. Negation is the link of connection: Old and new things are connected through the link of negation. The essence of dialectical negation is "sublation" (Aufhebung), meaning that the new thing both criticizes and inherits the old thing, both overcomes its negative factors and retains its positive factors. The dialectical negation of things passes through three stages: affirmation — negation — negation of negation The periodicity of the development of things: A new, higher stage of affirmation, then a new spiral upward process of negation of negation begins. The unity of progressiveness (each negation is a qualitative change) and tortuousness (progressiveness is the trend, but it is not smooth sailing). Sublation: Overcome its negative and outdated factors, retain and develop its positive and reasonable factors, and add new content. 1.2.2.4 The Basic Links of Connection and Development Content and form, essence and appearance, cause and result, necessity and contingency, reality and possibility. 2 Practice and Cognition and Their Laws of Development 2.1 Practice and Cognition 2.1.1 The Scientific View of Practice (Constantly Enriched and Developed) Significance: Overcame the defects of old materialism and laid the theoretical foundation for dialectical materialism. Revealed the determining role of practice in cognition, providing a scientific theoretical foundation for the establishment of active, revolutionary reflection theory. For the first time revealed the practical essence of social life. Provided basic methods of thought and work for people to actively understand and transform the world. 2.1.2 The Essence and Basic Structure of Practice 2.1.2.1 The Essence of Practice Practice: The social material activity in which humans actively transform the world. Characteristics: Objective reality, conscious initiative, and social historicity. 2.1.2.2 The Basic Structure of Practice Three basic elements: The subject of practice, the object of practice, and the medium of practice. The relationship between the subject and object of practice: Practical relationship (fundamental), cognitive relationship, and value relationship. The development of the basic structure of practice is manifested as the bidirectional movement of the subject's objectification and the object's subjectification. Subject's objectification: Simply put, the subject's transformation and creation of the object based on subjective consciousness. Object's subjectification: Simply put, the subject uses the object and internalizes it as a tool for developing the subject. Both have material and spiritual dimensions. 2.1.2.3 The Diversity of Forms of Practice Material production practice Social and political practice Scientific and cultural practice (New form of practice emerging: virtual practice) 2.1.2.4 The Determining Role of Practice in Cognition Practice is the basis of cognition and has a determining role. Practice is the source of cognition (interaction with the world forms perceptual cognition; the brain processes it into rational cognition; direct (primary) and indirect experience). Practice is the driving force of cognition (fundamental motive force; provides necessary conditions; practice itself also increases knowledge). Practice is the purpose of cognition. Practice is the only criterion for testing the truth of cognition. Whether cognition has truthfulness can only be verified in practice. The certainty of the criterion of practice (it is the only criterion) and its uncertainty (historical development) are dialectically unified. 2.1.3 The Essence and Process of Cognition 2.1.3.1 The Essence of Cognition Dialectical materialist epistemology (reflection theory): The essence of cognition is the active reflection of the subject on the object on the basis of practice. This active reflection has two basic characteristics: Reflectivity: The basic stipulation of human cognition, meaning that cognition must take the objective thing as the prototype and reproduce its state, properties, and essence in thought. Active creativity: An active, creative activity carried out in thought; people need to penetrate through appearances to grasp the essence and process and transform the object in ideas using dialectical thinking methods. The two are dialectically unified and inseparable. They are not two aspects of the same essence: Creation cannot be separated from reflection: The process of creation is realized on the basis of reflecting multiple aspects. Reflection also cannot be separated from creation: Reflection is realized in the process of creation. Two erroneous tendencies and their dangers: Insisting only on reflectivity and ignoring creativity would repeat the mistake of the intuitive reflection theory of old materialism. Insisting only on creativity and departing from the premise of reflection would turn creation into subjective arbitrariness, thereby sliding into idealism and agnosticism. 2.1.3.2 From Practice to Cognition The process of cognition: From cognition to practice, and from practice back to cognition. Two leaps between practice and cognition: The dialectical movement of practice and cognition is a leap from perceptual cognition to rational cognition, and then from rational cognition back to practice. The dialectical relationship between perceptual cognition and rational cognition: Perceptual cognition (direct, including sensation (individual senses) → perception (holistic response) → representation (recollection of past sensations and perceptions)) Rational cognition (concept → judgment → reasoning) Rational cognition depends on perceptual cognition (materialism in epistemology). Perceptual cognition needs to develop and deepen into rational cognition. Perceptual cognition and rational cognition interpenetrate and include each other. Conditions for moving from perceptual to rational cognition: practice → thinking. There are non-rational factors in the cognitive process. 2.1.3.3 From Cognition to Practice The necessity and importance of returning from cognition to practice: The purpose of understanding the world is to transform it. The truthfulness of cognition can only be tested and developed in practice. 2.1.4 The Dialectical Movement of Practice and Cognition and Its Laws Saying practice and cognition are "completed" is only in reference to cognition of a specific thing. Achieving the expected purpose, making the anticipated thought, theory, or plan largely become fact in practice, with partial or even full adjustment. Saying it is "not yet completed" is in reference to the continuous development of the movement of practice and cognition. Human practice continuously moves forward and develops, so people's cognition must also develop accordingly. The movement and change of the objective real world are never finished, so people's understanding of truth in practice is never finished. 2.2 Truth and Value 2.2.1 The Objectivity, Absoluteness, and Relativity of Truth Definition of truth: A philosophical category that signifies the correspondence between the subjective and the objective; it is the correct reflection of objective things and their laws. The objectivity of truth: The content of truth is a correct reflection of objective things and their laws (which determines the oneness of truth — unity of content rather than form). The absoluteness and relativity of truth: The absoluteness of truth: The certainty of the unity of subject and object; the infinity of development. The relativity of truth: Under certain conditions, a correct understanding of objective things, their essence, and laws of development is always limited and imperfect. From the perspective of the objective world as a whole, any truth is only a correct understanding of a certain stage or part of the objective world and needs to be expanded. With respect to a particular thing, any truth is only a correct understanding of a certain aspect, level, and degree of the objective object. Any truth can only be an approximately correct, i.e., relatively correct, reflection of the objective thing by the subject. The dialectical unity of the absoluteness and relativity of truth Duality: The two include each other. In development: Human cognition is an infinite process, forever moving from relative truth toward and approaching absolute truth. The unity of opposites between truth and error Within a definite object and scope, the two are opposed to each other. They have absolute significance only within a certain scope; beyond that, they become relative. 2.2.2 The Criterion for Testing Truth 2.2.2.2 Practice Is the Only Criterion for Testing Truth Practice can serve as the only criterion for testing truth because of the nature of truth and the characteristics of practice. Nature of truth: Truth is a correct reflection by people of objective things and their laws of development; its nature lies in the correspondence between the subjective and the objective. Practice: Practice has direct reality. The direct reality of practice is a concrete manifestation of its objective reality. 2.2.2.3 The Certainty and Uncertainty of the Criterion of Practice Certainty: Absoluteness, meaning that practice is the only, ultimate, and final criterion for testing truth. Uncertainty: Relativity, meaning the conditionality of practice as the criterion for testing truth. Practice is constrained by subjective and objective factors. Practice is limited by historical conditions. 2.2.3 The Dialectical Unity of Truth and Value 2.2.3.1 Value Subjectivity, objectivity, multidimensionality, and social historicity. The subjectivity of value: Directly related to the subject, always centered on the subject. The formation of value relations depends on the existence of the subject. The formation of value relations depends on the subject's creation, transforming the potential value of the object into actual value. The objectivity of value: Under certain conditions, the significance of the object to the subject exists independently of the subject's subjective consciousness. The existence and needs of the subject are objective, not abstract. The existence, properties, and functions of the object are objective. The multidimensionality of value: The same object can produce different values relative to different needs of the subject. The social historicity of value: The constant change of subject and object determines the historicity of value. 2.2.3.3 Value Evaluation and Its Characteristics Value evaluation is a subjective reflection of objective value relations. Evaluation takes the value relationship between subject and object as its cognitive object. The result of evaluation is directly related to the evaluating subject. The correctness of the evaluation result depends on the understanding of the state of the object and the needs of the subject. Evaluation results can be correct or incorrect; value evaluation can also be scientific or unscientific. 2.2.3.5 The Dialectical Unity of Truth and Value in Practice People's practical activities are always constrained by the scale of truth and the scale of value. Dialectical relationship: The scale of value must presuppose truth; if it departs from the scale of truth, the scale of value deviates from a reasonable and correct track. The internal scale of human needs drives people to constantly discover new truths; if it departs from the scale of value, truth loses its subjective meaning. The concreteness and historicity of practice imply that the unity of the scale of truth and the scale of value is also concrete and historical. Whether the two achieve unity is verified through practice. 2.3 Understanding and Transforming the World 2.3.1 The Fundamental Purpose of Understanding the World Is to Transform It 2.3.1.1 The Dialectical Relationship between Understanding and Transforming the World Understanding the world helps to transform the world. Only in the practice of transforming the world can people continuously deepen and expand their correct understanding of the world. 2.3.1.2 Transforming the Objective World and Transforming the Subjective World and Their Dialectical Relationship Only in the practice of transforming the objective world can we deeply transform the subjective world. Only by earnestly transforming the subjective world can we better transform the objective world. 2.3.1.3 The Process of Understanding and Transforming the World Is a Process from Necessity to Freedom Conditions for freedom: Cognitive conditions: Correct understanding of objective things (and their development). Practical conditions: The ability to apply the acquired knowledge of laws to guide practice and achieve the purpose of transforming the world. 3 Human Society and Its Laws of Development 3.1 The Existence and Development of Human Society 3.1.1 Social Existence and Social Consciousness Social existence: The material conditions of social life; the material aspect of social life. Natural geographical environment Demographic factors Material mode of production It is the basis for the existence and development of human society and the primary premise for all other human activities. It determines the structure, nature, and appearance of society. It determines the whole process of social historical change and development, and the succession and development of social forms from lower to higher stages. Social consciousness: The reflection of social existence; the spiritual aspect of social life. Ideology (political and legal thought, morality, art, religion, philosophy, etc.) Non-ideology (natural science and linguistics, formal logic) The dialectical relationship between social existence and social consciousness: Social existence determines social consciousness. Social existence is the objective source of the content of social consciousness; social consciousness is the subjective reflection of the material process and conditions of social life. Social consciousness is the product of people's material social intercourse. Social consciousness is concrete and historical. Social consciousness reflects social existence and reacts on social existence (social consciousness has relative independence): Social consciousness and social existence develop with incomplete synchronization and imbalance. Various forms within social consciousness influence each other and each has historical continuity. Social consciousness has an active reaction on social existence; this is the prominent manifestation of its relative independence. 3.1.2 The Basic Contradictions of Society and the Laws of Their Movement 3.1.2.1 The Contradictory Movement of Productive Forces and Relations of Production and Its Laws Productive forces: The material forces needed in production practice; objective reality and social historicity. Basic elements include: Means of labor, objects of labor, and laborers. Laborers are the most important, most active, and decisive factor in the productive forces. In the process of production, laborers use means of labor to act on objects of labor, thereby producing material products. The means of labor and the objects of labor are collectively called "means of production." Science and technology are important factors in the productive forces: They cause profound changes and great progress in the means of labor, objects of labor, and the quality of laborers. They improve management efficiency. They raise labor productivity. Science and technology are the primary productive forces. Relations of production: The economic relations formed by people in the process of material production, independent of human will. Among them, ownership of the means of production is the most basic relationship. At present, public ownership and private ownership coexist. The relationship between productive forces and relations of production: Productive forces determine relations of production. The state of the productive forces determines the nature of the relations of production. The development of the productive forces determines changes in the relations of production. Relations of production are the product of the needs of productive forces development; they can exist only when they provide sufficient space for the development of the productive forces. Relations of production have an active reaction on the productive forces. When relations of production fit the objective requirements of the development of the productive forces, they promote their development. When relations of production do not fit the objective requirements of the development of the productive forces, they hinder their development. 3.1.2.2 The Contradictory Movement of the Economic Base and the Superstructure and Its Laws Economic base: The economic base is the sum total of the relations of production determined by the productive forces at a certain stage of social development. What determines the nature of a society is the dominant relations of production within it. Superstructure: The superstructure is the ideology established on a certain economic base, together with the corresponding institutions, organizations, and facilities. The political superstructure occupies a dominant position. State power: Uses violence to keep social conflict within the bounds of order. In the whole superstructure, the political superstructure occupies a dominant position, and state power is the core of the political superstructure. State system: The position of the various social classes in the state. Form of government: The form in which the ruling class organizes its state power. The dialectical unity of the economic base and the superstructure: The economic base determines the superstructure. It determines its emergence (what kind of superstructure). It determines its nature (in whose service it is). It determines its changes. The superstructure reacts on the economic base. The superstructure actively serves the economic base. Promotive role: When the superstructure fits the condition of the economic base, it promotes the consolidation and development of the economic base. Obstructive role: When the superstructure does not fit the condition of the economic base, it hinders the formation and development of a new, advanced economic base. Third, the interaction between the economic base and the superstructure constitutes their contradictory movement. The imperfect parts of the superstructure and those that do not reflect the requirements of the economic base come into contradiction with the economic base. Contradictions between the currently dominant economic base and the remnants of the old superstructure, and the embryos of the future superstructure; contradictions between the new and old superstructures, and between the new and old economic bases. When a social form is rising, the superstructure adapts to the economic base; when it is declining, there is antagonism. Finally, the inherent connection between the economic base and the superstructure constitutes the law that the superstructure "must necessarily fit" the condition of the economic base. The condition of the economic base determines the direction of development of the superstructure and determines the corresponding adjustment or transformation of the superstructure. The reaction of the superstructure must also depend on and be subordinated to the nature and objective requirements of the economic base. 3.1.3 Intercourse Functions: Promotes the development of productive forces. Promotes the progress of social relations. Promotes the development and spread of culture. Promotes the all-round development of human beings. 3.1.4 Social Progress and the Succession of Social Forms The development of social forms from lower to higher stages, and development within the same social form; social progress promotes human development and drives human liberation. The unity and diversity of the succession of social forms: Unity: Primitive society, slave society, feudal society, capitalist society, and communist society succeed each other in turn. Diversity: There may be leaps, non-typical forms, rapid or slow processes, and tortuous paths. The inevitability and selectivity of the succession of social forms: Inevitability The successive replacement of social forms is objective. The law of the contradictory movement between productive forces and relations of production fundamentally determines the inevitability of the succession of social forms. Selectivity Inevitability creates the basic trend of social development and provides space for selectivity. It is a process of unifying subjective initiative and objective law. People's historical selectivity is, in the final analysis, the selectivity of the masses. 3.2 The Motive Forces of Social Development 3.2.1 The Basic Contradictions of Society Are the Fundamental Motive Force of Historical Development The basic contradictions of society: The contradiction between productive forces and relations of production (fundamental) The contradiction between the economic base and the superstructure (manifestation) Their role is manifested in: The productive forces are the most basic motive factor in the movement of the basic contradictions of society. The productive forces are the material basis for the existence and development of society. The productive forces determine the nature of the relations of production. The productive forces are the fundamental content of social progress. The basic contradictions of society, especially the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, determine the existence and development of other contradictions in society. The contradiction between productive forces and relations of production determines the emergence and development of the contradiction between the economic base and the superstructure. The contradiction between the economic base and the superstructure also influences and constrains the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. The basic contradictions of society have different forms of manifestation and modes of resolution. Change of social form: Revolution. Development within the same social form: Reform. The principal contradiction of society: Different from the basic contradiction; it constantly changes downward and is a manifestation of the basic contradiction. The content of the two sides of the principal contradiction of society changes to some extent. The status of the contradiction changes. 3.2.2 The Role of Class Struggle and Social Revolution in Social Development Class struggle is the manifestation of the basic contradictions of society in class society. Social revolution is a general term for the broad and profound social changes caused by the basic contradictions of society. Class struggle It is the direct motive force of the development of class society. It is rooted in the fundamental opposition of material interests between classes, and rooted in the conflict of socio-economic relations. Its role is manifested in the succession of social forms. It is constrained by certain social historical conditions. Social revolution It is rooted in the sharpening of the basic contradictions of society and requires objective and subjective conditions. It is an important means and decisive link in realizing the succession of social forms. Reform It is a profound change and renovation of the relations of production and the superstructure in order to solve the basic contradictions of society. It is the self-adjustment and self-improvement of the social system. It is quantitative change and partial qualitative change. 3.2.3 The Role of Science and Technology in Social Development The scientific and technological revolution is a powerful lever driving economic and social development. It has a profound impact on the mode of production. It changes the constituent elements of social productive forces (the structure of the labor force tends toward intellectualization). It changes people's forms of labor (from mechanical automation to intelligent automation, from partial automation to fundamental transformation toward large-system management and control automation). It changes the socio-economic structure, especially causing changes in the industrial structure (the proportion of workers in the tertiary sector increases). It has a huge impact on the mode of life. It promotes changes in the mode of thinking. 3.2.3 The Role of Culture in Social Development Culture is an important force promoting social development. It provides social development with: ideological guidance, spiritual motivation, and cohesive strength. 3.3 The Role of the People in Historical Development 3.3.1 The People Are the Creators of History The opposition between historical materialism and historical idealism is manifested on the question of who creates history as the opposition between the mass view of history (historical materialism) and the heroic view of history (historical idealism). The mass view of history does not deny the important role of heroes in history. They conform to the laws of historical development, reflect the wishes and demands of the people, accelerate the course of history, but cannot change its fundamental direction. Historical materialism: Grasps the creators of history on the basis of real people and their essence. Explores who creates history from the overall social historical process. Examines and explains who creates history starting from the inevitability of social historical development. Examines who creates history from different levels of the relationship between people and history. The decisive role of the people in the process of creating history: The people are the subject of social history and the creators of history. The people are the creators of social material wealth (material production is the foundation, and the people are the producers). The people are the creators of social spiritual wealth (although it is often concentratedly embodied by distinguished intellectuals and artists, its ultimate source is still the social practice of the people). The people are the decisive force in social change (the main force of class struggle, the fundamental motive force of social revolution). 4 The Nature of Capitalism and Its Laws 4.1 Commodity Economy and the Law of Value 4.1.1 The Formation and Development of the Commodity Economy Natural economy: Production is directly aimed at satisfying the needs of the individual producer or economic unit. Primitive society, slave society, and feudal society, because the level of productive forces was very low and the social division of labor was extremely underdeveloped. Commodity economy: An economic form in which production is carried out for the purpose of exchange. Historical conditions for its emergence: The existence of social division of labor (premise). The means of production and the products of labor belong to different owners (decisive condition). The two factors of a commodity: Two factors: Use value (natural attribute, objective, concrete, and the material bearer of commodity value) Value (social attribute, the expenditure of human brainpower and physical labor; determined by socially necessary labor time, not by the actual labor time of the individual worker) flowchart TD A[An item exists]:::green --> B{Is it useful?}:::green B -->|Yes| C{Is it a product of human labor?}:::green B -->|No| D[Useless object]:::green C -->|Yes| E{Is it produced for exchange?}:::green C -->|No| F[Natural object e.g., air<br>Has use value, no value]:::green E -->|Yes| G[Commodity<br>Has use value and value]:::green E -->|No| H[Self-use item<br>Has use value, no value]:::green classDef green fill:#e6ffe6,stroke:#2db300,color:#006600,text-align:center class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H green The use value and value of a commodity are in a relationship of unity of opposites: Opposition: The use value and value of a commodity are mutually exclusive. The producer cares about value rather than use value, and must give up the use value to the buyer in order to obtain value. Unity: As a commodity, it must possess both use value and value. Use value is the material bearer of value; value resides in use value. A commodity is a product of labor, and the labor that produces a commodity has a twofold character: Concrete labor: Creates the use value of the commodity (e.g., farming). Abstract labor: Forms the value of the commodity (e.g., laboring for 5 hours). The twofold character of labor determines the two factors of the commodity: All labor is both particular concrete labor and general abstract labor. Concrete labor and abstract labor are also in a unity of opposites: They do not exist independently but are two aspects unified in time and space. They reflect different attributes of labor: the former is a natural attribute, the latter a social attribute. The determination of the magnitude of commodity value: First level: The core measure is "socially necessary labor time," not "individual labor time." Second level: The magnitude of value is inversely proportional to "labor productivity." Third level: The magnitude of value is measured in terms of "simple labor"; complex labor can be converted (spontaneously calculated, not actively calculated, producing value several times that of simple labor). 4.1.2 The Law of Value and Its Role The role of the law of value in the market allocation of resources is manifested in: Spontaneously adjusting the proportion of means of production and labor among the various production departments of society. Spontaneously stimulating the development of social productive forces. Spontaneously adjusting the distribution of social income. Negative consequences: Waste of social resources. Hindering technological progress. Polarization of income. The basic contradiction of the commodity economy based on private ownership: flowchart LR A[Commodity<br>Contradiction between use value and value]-->|Rooted in|B[Contradiction between private labor and social labor] C[Production of commodities<br>Contradiction between concrete labor and abstract labor]-->|Rooted in|B B-->|Constitutes|D[The basic contradiction of the commodity economy] classDef green fill:#e6ffe6,stroke:#2db300,color:#006600,text-align:center class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H green Understanding: In a commodity economy based on private ownership, each person's labor appears on the surface to be independent private labor done for oneself, but in essence it is also social labor that is interconnected and produced for society. There is a profound contradiction between these two aspects. This contradiction needs to be temporarily resolved through market exchange; but because it is not thoroughly resolved, it continually gives rise to new contradictions, thereby driving the operation, development, and even crises of the entire commodity economy. The contradiction between private labor and social labor constitutes the basic contradiction of the commodity economy based on private ownership. It determines the essence and development process of the commodity economy. It is the basis of all other contradictions in the commodity economy. It determines the fate of commodity producers. 4.2 The Capitalist Economic System 4.2.2 Labor Power Becoming a Commodity and Money Transforming into Capital G stands for money, W stands for commodity. Money as money: W-G-W Money as capital: G-W-G' Labor power: A person's labor capacity, the sum of their mental and physical abilities. The basic conditions for it to become a commodity: The laborer is legally a free person and can dispose of their own labor power as a commodity. The laborer has no means of production and no means of subsistence, and therefore is forced to sell their labor power in order to live. The value of labor power: (determined by the value of the necessities of life required to produce, develop, maintain, and sustain labor power) The value of the means of subsistence needed to maintain the laborer's own survival. The value of the means of subsistence needed to maintain the laborer's family. The expenses the laborer incurs for education and training. (In simple terms, it is the total cost of the worker's "food money, rent, clothing, food, housing, transportation, and supporting the family," etc.) The characteristics of labor power as a commodity: Its use value is the source of value; it creates a new value greater than the value of labor power itself, and this new value is greater than the value of labor power itself. (Hence surplus value arises.) Therefore: After the money owner purchases labor power, in the process of consuming it, he can not only recover the value he paid when purchasing this special commodity but also obtain an increased value, i.e., surplus value. (This is why capital can be profitable.) Capital is value that can bring surplus value. Surplus value is created by the surplus labor of wage workers. 4.2.3 Producing Surplus Value Is the Absolute Law of the Capitalist Mode of Production The capitalist production process has a twofold character, being the unity of: The labor process of producing material goods. The process of producing surplus value. The labor of wage workers is divided into two parts: Necessary labor, used to reproduce the value of labor power. Surplus labor, used to produce surplus value for the capitalist free of charge. Constant capital and variable capital: p211 Constant capital is capital existing in the form of means of production. The value of the means of production is transferred to the new product through the concrete labor of the workers. The amount of transferred value is not greater than its original value. (It only transfers, it does not increase in value.) Variable capital is the part of capital used to purchase labor power. The value of variable capital is not transferred to the new product in the production process; rather, it is reproduced by the labor of the workers. To determine the degree of exploitation of workers by capitalists, we should compare surplus value with the variable capital employed, not with the total capital. 4.2.3.2 Two Methods of Surplus Value Production Absolute surplus value production: Keeping the necessary labor time unchanged and extending the length of the working day / increasing the intensity of labor. Relative surplus value production: With the length of the working day unchanged, shortening the necessary labor time to relatively extend the surplus labor time, thereby producing surplus value (by raising social labor productivity). 4.2.3.3 Capital Accumulation Capital accumulation: The capitalization of surplus value. The source of capital accumulation is surplus value. The scale of capital accumulation depends on: The degree of exploitation of workers by capitalists. The level of labor productivity. The difference between capital employed and capital consumed. The size of the capital advanced by the capitalist. It leads to the polarization of wealth and unemployment. 4.2.4 The Basic Contradiction of Capitalism and Economic Crises The basic contradiction of capitalism: p225 The contradiction between the socialization of production and the capitalist private appropriation of the means of production is the basic contradiction of capitalism. In reality, it is mainly manifested in two concrete contradictions: The contradiction between the organized nature of production within individual enterprises and the anarchy of production in society as a whole. The contradiction between the unlimited tendency of capitalist production to expand and the relatively shrinking demand of the laboring people with the ability to pay. The capitalist economic crisis: p226 Its essential feature: (Relative) overproduction. This overproduction is relative overproduction, i.e., relative to the purchasing power of the laboring people, not relative to their actual needs. 5 The Development of Capitalism and Its Trends 5.1 The Formation and Development of Monopoly Capitalism Reasons for monopoly: When concentration of production reaches a fairly high level, a very small number of enterprises will combine to manipulate and control the production and sale of their sector, implementing monopoly in order to obtain high profits. Large enterprise scale creates barriers to competition, which also produces monopoly. Fierce competition causes increasingly severe losses to all parties; to avoid mutual destruction, enterprises reach compromises and combine to implement monopoly. The relationship between monopoly and competition: Monopoly emerged from free competition and arose as its opposite. However, monopoly cannot eliminate competition; on the contrary, it makes competition more complex and intense: Monopoly does not eliminate the economic conditions that give rise to competition. Monopoly must be maintained through competition. No monopoly organization can monopolize all of the all-encompassing social production, which makes competition even fiercer. Monopoly prices can neither increase nor decrease the total value produced by society as a whole; they merely redistribute commodity value and surplus value in favor of monopoly capital. State monopoly capitalism: State monopoly capitalism is monopoly capitalism in which state power and private monopoly capital are fused together. The state owns and directly operates enterprises. Joint state-private ownership and joint operation. The state participates in the reproduction process of private monopoly capital through various forms. Macro regulation. Micro regulation. The manifestations of economic globalization: Globalization of production (international division of labor), globalization of trade, globalization of finance. The drivers of economic globalization: Advances in science and technology and the development of productive forces provide a solid material foundation and fundamental driving force for economic globalization. (Especially the information revolution.) The development of multinational corporations provides a suitable enterprise organizational form for economic globalization. (Making use of advantages of different regions in organizing production.) Changes in national economic systems and the development of international economic organizations provide institutional and organizational guarantees for economic globalization. 5.3 The Historical Position of Capitalism 5.3.1 Its Historical Position Compared with feudal society, capitalism demonstrates great historical progressiveness: Capitalism turned science and technology into a powerful productive force. The internal motive force of capital's pursuit of surplus value and the external pressure of competition drove the rapid development of social productive forces. The ideology and political system of capitalism promoted the rapid development of social productive forces and social progress. Limitations: The basic contradiction of capitalism hinders the development of social productive forces. Polarization of wealth ownership triggers economic crises. The bourgeoisie dominates and controls the development and operation of the capitalist economy and politics, continuously intensifying social contradictions and conflicts. 5.3.2 The Historical Necessity of Its Replacement The basic contradiction of capitalism becomes increasingly manifest with its development. Capital accumulation drives the continuous intensification of the basic contradiction of capitalism and ultimately negates capitalism itself. State monopoly capitalism is a higher form of the socialization of capital and will become a prelude to socialism. In capitalist society there exists the contradiction and struggle between the bourgeoisie and the proletariat. 6 The Development of Socialism and Its Laws 6.1 The Five-Hundred-Year Historical Process of Socialism 6.1.1 Socialism from Utopia to Science The stages of development of utopian socialism: Early utopian socialism of the 16th-17th centuries. Utopian equalitarian communism of the 18th century. Critical utopian socialism of the early 19th century. The pioneering work: Thomas More's Utopia, published in 1516. The significance of utopian socialist theory: It offered sharp criticism of the old capitalist system, containing important insights. It reflected the urgent desire of the early proletariat to transform the existing society and establish an ideal new society. Utopian socialism "provided extremely valuable materials for enlightening the consciousness of workers," but it did not possess a scientific and practical character. The limitations of utopian socialism: It did not point out the real way out for social development. It did not clarify the essence of capitalist wage labor. It did not discover the laws of capitalist development. It did not find the social force that would become the creator of the new society. Scientific socialism: Historical materialism and the theory of surplus value. Scientific socialism > utopian socialism Scientific theory. Economic roots. Revealed the basic contradiction of capitalism. Relied on the people as the force to bury it. Provided path guidance and methods of realization. 6.3 Exploring the Laws of Socialist Development in Practice The protracted nature of the process of socialist construction: Constrained by the state of development of the productive forces. Constrained by the state of development of the economic base and the superstructure. Severe challenges from the international environment. The exploration by Marxist ruling parties of the path of socialist development and their understanding of the laws of socialist construction require a long process. 7 The Lofty Ideal of Communism and Its Ultimate Realization 7.1 Looking Forward to the New Communist Society Methodological principles for foreseeing the future society. Pointing out the direction of social development on the basis of revealing the general laws of the development of human society. Elaborating the characteristics of the future new world in the analysis of the old world of capitalist society. Continuously deepening understanding of the future communist society in the development of socialist society. Focusing on revealing the general features of the future society rather than making detailed descriptions. The basic characteristics of communist society. Material wealth is enormously abundant, and consumer goods are distributed according to need. Social relations are highly harmonious, and people's spiritual realm is greatly elevated. Classes will disappear. The state will wither away (the government will not). War will cease to exist. Due to the immense development of social productive forces, the differences between industry and agriculture, between town and country, and between mental and manual labor—the "three great differences"—will inevitably disappear. Not only will society be harmonious, but harmony will also be achieved between society and nature. People's spiritual realm will be greatly elevated. The free and full development of every individual is realized, and humanity leaps from the kingdom of necessity to the kingdom of freedom. Realizing the free and comprehensive development of every individual is the fundamental value goal pursued by Marxism and also the fundamental feature of communist society. The elimination of the old division of labor creates the conditions for the free and comprehensive development of human beings. The extension of free time provides broad prospects for the free and comprehensive development of human beings. Labor is no longer merely a means of earning a living but becomes "the primary need of life."
