items.content: 图论整理 第一章 基本概念 1.1 图的概念 $(V(G),E(G))$称为图，$V(G)$是非空集合，称为顶点集，$E(G)$是$V(G)$诸顶点之间边的集合。常用$G=(V,E)$表示图 只讨论有限图，$|V|=n$称为图的阶，$|E|=m$ 一些概念： $e_k=(v_i,v_j)$ 称$v_i与v_j是相邻顶点；e_k分别与v_i,v_j关联$ 称$v_i是e_k的始点，v_j是e_k的终点，v_i是v_j的直接前趋，v_j是v_i的直接后继$ 邻接边：有一个共同顶点的两条边 有向图：全部由有向边构成的图 **无向图：**全部由无向边构成的图 **混合图：**既有有向边又有无向边构成的图 **自环：**只与一个顶点关联的边 **多重边：**同一对顶点之间存在多条边 **多重图：**含有重边的图 **孤立点：**没有与任何边关联的顶点 **度$d(v)$：**与顶点关联的边的数目 **入读：**入边条数 **出度：**出边条数 **奇点：**度为奇数的点 **偶点：**度为偶数的点 **简单图：**不存在自环的无向图 $\sum\limits_{v\in{V(G)}}d(v)=2m$ G中奇数的顶点必为偶数个 G中出度之和=入度之和 Kn的变数是$\cfrac12n(n-1)$ 非空简单图G中一定存在度相同的顶点 n阶完全图：Kn 完全二分图：Km,n **平凡图：**n=1的图 **空图/零图：**m=0的图 **（k度）正则图：**所有顶点度数均相等（为k）的图 阶为k的(k-1)-正则图：k-完全图 **正权图：**权为正实数的赋权图 子图：$V'\in V,E'\in E$ 支撑子图/生成子图：$V'=V,E'\in E$ 导出子图：$V'\in V,E'_V = E_V$ 邻点集：$\Gamma(v)$ 直接后继集/外邻集：$\Gamma^+(v)$ 直接前趋集/内邻集：$\Gamma^-(v)$ 1.2 图的代数表示 邻接矩阵 对称矩阵 可以表示自环 无法表示重边 权矩阵 邻接矩阵基础上加入权值信息 关联矩阵 n x m的矩阵 $b_{ij}=\begin{cases}1,&e_j=(v_i,v_k)\in E\-1,&e_j=(v_k,v_i)\in E\0,&其他\end{cases}$ 无法表示自环 可以表示重边 边列表 边列表是对关联矩阵的列进行压缩的结果 两个m维向量$\vec A$和$\vec B$，前者存放起点，后者存放终点 可选的$\vec Z$，存放权值 可以表示自环 可以表示重边 正向表 对邻接矩阵的行进行压缩的结果，把每个顶点的直接后趋集中在一起存放 n+1维向量$\vec A$，m维向量$\vec B$ $d^+(v_i)=A(i+1)-A(i)$ $B(A(i))$到$B(A(i+1)-1)中的任一个值，都是v_i的直接后继$ 可选的$\vec Z$，存放权值 可以表示自环 可以表示重边 逆向表 与正向表类似，把每个顶点的直接前趋放在一张表里存放 邻接表 每一个表顶点|a|b|c|，a存放点编号，b存放边的数值，c存放下一表顶点的地址指针 可以存放权值 可以表示自环 可以表示重边 第二章 道路和回路 2.1 图的连通性 有向图中： 有向道路、有向回路：字面意思 无重边：简单有向道路/简单有向回路 无重边、无重顶点：初级有向道路/初级有向回路，简称路和回路 无向图中： 道路/链、回路/圈：字面意思 无重边：简单道路/简单回路 无重边、无重顶点：初级道路/初级回路 **弦：**圈中不相邻顶点的边 **连通图：**G的任意两点之间都存在道路H不是G任何连通子图的真子图 **树：**不含回路的连通图 **割边/割点：**移去后使得原有图不再连通的边/顶点 **块：**G中极大的没有割点的连通子图 割点相关等价命题： v是G的一个割点 存在与v不同的点u,w，使得任何一条u到w的道路Puw经过v V-v可以划分为两个顶点集U，W，任意$u\in U,w\in W$，u在每一条道路Puw上 割边相关等价命题： e是G的一条割边 e不属于G的任何回路 存在G得顶点u，w，e属于u和w的任何一条道路Puw G-e可以划分为两个顶点集U和W，使得对任何顶点$u\in U,w\in W$，在G中的道路Puw都经过e 图G移去若干顶点后分为两个连通子图或者剩下一个孤立的点，这些点的集合称为点断集/断集A $\mathcal K(G)=\min\limits_{A\in\emptyset}{|A|}$为断量 同理边断集B，边断量$\lambda(G)$ 若$\mathcal K(G)\geq k$称G为k连通图，同理k边连通图 $\mathcal K(G)\leq \lambda(G)\leq \delta(G),\delta(G)是顶点的最小度$ 2.3 欧拉道路与回路 **欧拉回路/道路：**经过所有边的简单回路/道路 **欧拉图：**存在欧拉回路 **半欧拉图：**存在欧拉道路而不存在欧拉回路 $存在欧拉回路\Leftrightarrow 各顶点的度为偶数/出度入读相等$ $存在欧拉道路\Leftrightarrow 只有两个度为奇数的点$ 2.4 哈密顿道路与回路 **哈密顿回路/道路：**无向图的一条过全部顶点的初级回路 **哈密顿图：**含有H回路的无向连通图 **半哈密顿图：**含有H道路而不含H回路的无向连通图 一些充分定理： $\forall v_i,v_j，恒有d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n-1，则G中存在哈密顿道路$ $\forall v_i,v_j，恒有d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n，则G中存在哈密顿回路$ $若简单图每个顶点的度均大于等于\cfrac n2，则G有H回路$ $设G是简单图，v_i,v_j是不相邻顶点，且满足d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n，则G存在H回路的充要条件是G+(v_i,v_j)有H回路$ $先定义闭合图:若d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n，令G'=G+(v_i,v_j)，重复，直到不存在这样的顶点对为止，得到的即为闭合图，记作C(G)$ $简单图G存在哈密顿回路的充要条件是其闭合图存在哈密顿回路$ $若C(G)是完全图，则G有H回路$ 2.6 最短路径：Dijkstra算法 2.7 关键路径：AOE 2.8 中国邮路 先找到奇点，选择最小的几条路径，加上使这些奇点变偶，然后欧拉回路 第三章 树 3.1 树的相关定义 不含任何回路的连通图称为树（T），T中的边称为树枝，度为1的顶点称为树叶 若T是G的支撑子图，且又是一棵树，则T使G的支撑树/生成树，又称G的树 3.5 Huffman树 小在左，大在右，0在左，1在右 3.6 最短树 Kruskal算法：不断加入最短边，如成环则换次短边 Prim算法：选到已选区域最近的点 第四章 平面图与图图的着色 4.1 平面图 平面图：能放在一个平面上，任何两条边都不相交，称G可嵌入平面，G是可平面图，其中一个嵌入称为平面图 G同构于平面图P，称P是G的一个平面嵌入 面/域：不含任何顶点和边的区域，其中诸边称为边界 欧拉公式：对于平面连通图，$d=m-n+2$ 若G有k个连通支，则$n-m+d = k+1$ 对于一般平面图G，恒有$n-m+d\geq 2$ 若平面连通图G没有割边，且每个域的边界数至少t，则$m\leq\cfrac{t(n-2)}{t-2}$ 4.2 极大平面图 极大平面图： 连通 不存在割边 每个域边界数为3 3d=2m, m=3n-6, d=2n-4 简单平面图满足$m\leq 3n-6,d\leq 2n-4$ 简单平面图G中存在度小于6的顶点 4.3 非平面图 K5是非平面图，也称K(1) K3,3是非平面图，也称K(2) K(1)和K(2)图上任意加一些度为2的顶点之后得到的图称为K(1)型图和K(2)型图，统称为K型图 G是可平面图的充要条件是G不存在K型子图 4.4 对偶图 域->顶点，共边->相邻，求对呕吐的过程称为D过程（draw） 性质 若G是平面图，则G一定有唯一对偶图G* G*是连通图 若G是平面连通图，则（G*)*=G m=m*, n=d*, d=n* 若C是平面图G得一个初级回路，S*是G*中与C的各边ei对应的ei*的集合，那么S*是G*的一个割集 G有对偶图等价于G为平面图 每一个平面图都是5-可着色的 如果平面图G有哈密顿回路，则四色猜想成立 若任何一个3-正则平面图的域4-可着色，则任何平面图的域4-可着色 4.5 色数与色数多项式 不断分割即可
items.content_en: Graph Theory Summary Chapter 1: Basic Concepts 1.1 Concepts of Graphs $(V(G), E(G))$ is called a graph. $V(G)$ is a non-empty set called the vertex set, and $E(G)$ is the set of edges between vertices in $V(G)$. A graph is commonly denoted as $G=(V,E)$. We only discuss finite graphs here. $|V|=n$ is called the order of the graph, and $|E|=m$. Some concepts: $e_k=(v_i,v_j)$ $v_i$ and $v_j$ are called adjacent vertices; $e_k$ is incident to both $v_i$ and $v_j$. $v_i$ is the start vertex of $e_k$, and $v_j$ is the end vertex of $e_k$. $v_i$ is the immediate predecessor of $v_j$, and $v_j$ is the immediate successor of $v_i$. Adjacent edges: Two edges that share a common vertex. Directed graph: A graph composed entirely of directed edges. Undirected graph: A graph composed entirely of undirected edges. Mixed graph: A graph containing both directed and undirected edges. Loop: An edge that is incident to only one vertex. Multiple edges: Multiple edges exist between the same pair of vertices. Multigraph: A graph containing multiple edges. Isolated vertex: A vertex that has no incident edges. Degree $d(v)$: The number of edges incident to a vertex. In-degree: The number of incoming edges. Out-degree: The number of outgoing edges. Odd vertex: A vertex with an odd degree. Even vertex: A vertex with an even degree. Simple graph: An undirected graph without loops. $\sum\limits_{v\in{V(G)}}d(v)=2m$. The number of odd-degree vertices in $G$ must be even. The sum of out-degrees in $G$ equals the sum of in-degrees. The number of edges in $K_n$ is $\cfrac12n(n-1)$. In any non-empty simple graph $G$, there must exist vertices with the same degree. Complete graph of order $n$: $K_n$. Complete bipartite graph: $K_{m,n}$. Trivial graph: A graph with $n=1$. Empty graph/null graph: A graph with $m=0$. $(k)$-regular graph: A graph where all vertices have equal degree (equal to $k$). A $(k-1)$-regular graph of order $k$ is a complete graph of order $k$. Weighted graph with positive weights: A weighted graph where all edge weights are positive real numbers. Subgraph: $V'\in V, E'\in E$. Spanning subgraph/generator subgraph: $V'=V, E'\in E$. Induced subgraph: $V'\in V, E'_V = E_V$. Neighbor set: $\Gamma(v)$. Set of immediate successors/external neighbor set: $\Gamma^+(v)$. Set of immediate predecessors/internal neighbor set: $\Gamma^-(v)$. 1.2 Algebraic Representations of Graphs Adjacency matrix It is a symmetric matrix. It can represent loops. It cannot represent multiple edges. Weight matrix It adds weight information to the adjacency matrix. Incidence matrix It is an $n \times m$ matrix. $b_{ij}=\begin{cases}1,&e_j=(v_i,v_k)\in E\-1,&e_j=(v_k,v_i)\in E\0,&otherwise\end{cases}$. It cannot represent loops. It can represent multiple edges. Edge list The edge list is a compressed version of the columns of the incidence matrix. There are two $m$-dimensional vectors $\vec A$ and $\vec B$; the former stores start vertices, and the latter stores end vertices. An optional vector $\vec Z$ stores edge weights. It can represent loops. It can represent multiple edges. Forward star It is a compressed version of the rows of the adjacency matrix, storing the set of immediate successors of each vertex together. There is an $n+1$-dimensional vector $\vec A$ and an $m$-dimensional vector $\vec B$. $d^+(v_i)=A(i+1)-A(i)$. Any value from $B(A(i))$ to $B(A(i+1)-1)$ is an immediate successor of $v_i$. An optional vector $\vec Z$ stores edge weights. It can represent loops. It can represent multiple edges. Backward star Similar to the forward star, it stores the set of immediate predecessors of each vertex in a table. Adjacency list Each entry in the list is of the form $|a|b|c|$: $a$ stores the vertex index, $b$ stores the edge weight, and $c$ stores the address pointer to the next list entry. It can store edge weights. It can represent loops. It can represent multiple edges. Chapter 2: Paths and Cycles 2.1 Connectivity of Graphs In directed graphs: Directed path, directed cycle: As the name implies. No repeated edges: Simple directed path/simple directed cycle. No repeated edges and no repeated vertices: Elementary directed path/elementary directed cycle, abbreviated as path and cycle. In undirected graphs: Path/chain, cycle: As the name implies. No repeated edges: Simple path/simple cycle. No repeated edges and no repeated vertices: Elementary path/elementary cycle. Chord: An edge connecting two non-adjacent vertices on a cycle. Connected graph: For any two vertices in $G$, there exists a path between them. $H$ is not a proper subgraph of any connected subgraph of $G$. Tree: A connected graph with no cycles. Cut edge/cut vertex: An edge/vertex whose removal makes the original graph disconnected. Block: A maximal connected subgraph of $G$ with no cut vertices. Equivalent propositions related to cut vertices: $v$ is a cut vertex of $G$. There exist vertices $u$ and $w$ different from $v$ such that any path $P_{uw}$ from $u$ to $w$ passes through $v$. $V\setminus{v}$ can be partitioned into two vertex sets $U$ and $W$; for any $u\in U$ and $w\in W$, $u$ lies on every path $P_{uw}$. Equivalent propositions related to cut edges: $e$ is a cut edge of $G$. $e$ does not belong to any cycle in $G$. There exist vertices $u$ and $w$ in $G$ such that $e$ belongs to every path $P_{uw}$ between $u$ and $w$. $G\setminus{e}$ can be partitioned into two vertex sets $U$ and $W$ such that for any $u\in U$ and $w\in W$, every path $P_{uw}$ in $G$ passes through $e$. If removing several vertices from graph $G$ results in two connected subgraphs or a single isolated vertex, the set of these vertices is called a vertex cut/separating set $A$. $\mathcal K(G)=\min\limits_{A\in\emptyset}{|A|}$ is called the vertex connectivity. Similarly, for an edge cut set $B$, the edge connectivity is $\lambda(G)$. If $\mathcal K(G)\geq k$, $G$ is called a $k$-connected graph; similarly, a $k$-edge-connected graph. $\mathcal K(G)\leq \lambda(G)\leq \delta(G)$, where $\delta(G)$ is the minimum degree of the vertices. 2.3 Eulerian Paths and Cycles Eulerian cycle/path: A simple cycle/path that traverses all edges. Eulerian graph: A graph that contains an Eulerian cycle. Semi-Eulerian graph: A graph that contains an Eulerian path but no Eulerian cycle. $An Eulerian cycle exists \Leftrightarrow$ the degree of every vertex is even / the out-degree equals the in-degree for every vertex. $An Eulerian path exists \Leftrightarrow$ there are exactly two vertices with odd degree. 2.4 Hamiltonian Paths and Cycles Hamiltonian cycle/path: An elementary cycle in an undirected graph that visits all vertices. Hamiltonian graph: A connected undirected graph that contains a Hamiltonian cycle. Semi-Hamiltonian graph: A connected undirected graph that contains a Hamiltonian path but no Hamiltonian cycle. Some sufficient theorems: If $\forall v_i,v_j$, we always have $d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n-1$, then $G$ contains a Hamiltonian path. If $\forall v_i,v_j$, we always have $d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n$, then $G$ contains a Hamiltonian cycle. If every vertex in a simple graph has degree $\geq \cfrac n2$, then $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle. Let $G$ be a simple graph, and $v_i, v_j$ be non-adjacent vertices satisfying $d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n$. Then $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle if and only if $G+(v_i,v_j)$ has a Hamiltonian cycle. First, define a closed graph: If $d(v_i)+d(v_j)\geq n$, let $G'=G+(v_i,v_j)$, and repeat this process until no such vertex pair exists; the resulting graph is the closed graph, denoted as $C(G)$. A simple graph $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle if and only if its closed graph $C(G)$ has a Hamiltonian cycle. If $C(G)$ is a complete graph, then $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle. 2.6 Shortest Path: Dijkstra's Algorithm 2.7 Critical Path: AOE 2.8 Chinese Postman Problem First, identify the odd-degree vertices, select the shortest few paths to make these odd-degree vertices become even-degree vertices, and then construct an Eulerian cycle. Chapter 3: Trees 3.1 Definitions Related to Trees A connected graph with no cycles is called a tree ($T$). The edges in $T$ are called branches, and vertices with degree 1 are called leaves. If $T$ is a spanning subgraph of $G$ and is also a tree, then $T$ is called a spanning tree/generator tree of $G$, or simply a tree of $G$. 3.5 Huffman Tree The smaller value is placed on the left, the larger value on the right; 0 is on the left, 1 on the right. 3.6 Minimum Spanning Tree Kruskal's algorithm: Continuously add the shortest edges; if a cycle forms, replace it with the next-shortest edge. Prim's algorithm: Select the vertex closest to the already selected region. Chapter 4: Planar Graphs and Graph Coloring 4.1 Planar Graphs Planar graph: A graph that can be drawn on a plane without any intersecting edges. Such a drawing is called an embedding in the plane, and $G$ is a planar graph. One such embedding is called a planar representation of $G$. If $G$ is isomorphic to a planar graph $P$, then $P$ is called a planar embedding of $G$. Face/region: A region that contains no vertices or edges; the edges bounding the region are called its boundary. Euler's formula: For a connected planar graph, $d=m-n+2$. If $G$ has $k$ connected components, then $n-m+d = k+1$. For any general planar graph $G$, we always have $n-m+d\geq 2$. If a connected planar graph $G$ has no cut edges and the boundary of each face has at least $t$ edges, then $m\leq\cfrac{t(n-2)}{t-2}$. 4.2 Maximal Planar Graphs Maximal planar graph: Connected. Has no cut edges. The boundary of each face has 3 edges. $3d=2m$, $m=3n-6$, $d=2n-4$. For a simple planar graph, $m\leq 3n-6$ and $d\leq 2n-4$. There exist vertices with degree less than 6 in any simple planar graph $G$. 4.3 Non-planar Graphs $K_5$ is a non-planar graph, also called $K^{(1)}$. $K_{3,3}$ is a non-planar graph, also called $K^{(2)}$. Graphs obtained by adding some vertices of degree 2 to $K^{(1)}$ and $K^{(2)}$ are called $K^{(1)}$-type graphs and $K^{(2)}$-type graphs, collectively referred to as $K$-type graphs. A necessary and sufficient condition for $G$ to be planar is that $G$ contains no $K$-type subgraph. 4.4 Dual Graph Face $\rightarrow$ vertex, adjacent edges $\rightarrow$ adjacency; the process of finding the dual is called the D process (draw). Properties: If $G$ is a planar graph, then $G$ has a unique dual graph $G^*$. $G^*$ is a connected graph. If $G$ is a connected planar graph, then $(G*)* = G$. $m=m^$, $n=d^$, $d=n^*$. If $C$ is an elementary cycle in a planar graph $G$, and $S^$ is the set of edges $e_i^$ in $G^$ corresponding to each edge $e_i$ on $C$, then $S^$ is a cut set of $G^*$. $G$ has a dual graph if and only if $G$ is planar. Every planar graph is 5-colorable. If a planar graph $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle, then the four-color theorem holds. If the faces of any 3-regular planar graph are 4-colorable, then the faces of any planar graph are 4-colorable. 4.5 Chromatic Number and Chromatic Polynomial Just keep subdividing.

items.content_en: Counter Selection and Read/Write Modes SC1 SC0 Description 0 0 Select counter 0 0 1 Select counter 1 1 0 Select counter 2 1 1 Invalid for 8253Read-Back command for 8254 (see Read operations) RW1 RW0 Read/Write Mode 0 0 Counter latch command (see Read operations) 0 1 Read/Write least significant byte only 1 0 Read/Write most significant byte only 1 1 Read/write least significant byte first, then most significant byte M2 M1 M0 Operating Mode 0 0 0 Mode 0 0 0 1 Mode 1 X 1 0 Mode 2 X 1 1 Mode 3 1 0 0 Mode 4 1 0 1 Mode 5 BCD Description 0 16-bit binary counter 1 Binary-coded decimal (BCD) counter (4 decades) Counter Features Each counter is a single 16-bit presettable down-counter. It can operate in binary or BCD mode. Input, gate, and output settings are determined by the selected mode. Reading from a counter does not interfere with its ongoing count process. Read/Write Operations Write operations: Write a control word into the control register. Load the low-order byte of a count into the counter register. Load the high-order byte of a count into the counter register. Read operations: Simple Read: Two I/O read operations — first for the low-order byte, then for the high-order byte. Counter Latch Command: One I/O write operation to write a control word to the control register, latching the current count into the output latch; then two I/O read operations to retrieve the latched count, similar to Simple Read. Read-Back Command: Available only for the 8254 chip. Operating Modes Software-Triggered Modes (Non-repeating, except where noted) Mode 0: Interrupt on Terminal Count graph TD A[CPU writes count into CR] --> B[Count is transferred to the CE] B --> C[Counting down] C --> D[Output signal when count reaches 0] Gate control: Gate = 1 enables counting; Gate = 0 disables counting. New count handling: A newly written count is loaded on the next CLK pulse and counting continues from this new value. For two-byte counts: writing the first byte pauses counting; writing the second byte loads the new count on the next CLK pulse. Mode 1: Hardware Retriggerable One-Shot Normal operation: The output starts high after mode setup. The output goes low on the CLK pulse following the rising edge of the gate input. The output returns high at terminal count and stays high until the next rising edge of the gate input. Output produces a one-shot pulse of N clock cycles per trigger; it does not repeat automatically. Mode 2: Rate Generator Normal operation: The output starts high. The output goes low for one clock pulse before reaching terminal count. The output then goes high, the counter reloads the initial count, and the cycle repeats. Output is a periodic signal with N-1 clock cycles high and 1 clock cycle low. Mode 3: Square Wave Rate Generator Normal operation: The output starts high. For even counts, the counter decrements by 2 on each falling clock edge; when terminal count is reached, the output state changes and the counter reloads with the full count to restart the cycle. For odd counts, the first clock pulse decrements the count by 1, subsequent pulses decrement by 2; after timeout, the output goes low and the full count is reloaded. The next clock pulse (after reload) decrements the count by 3, and subsequent pulses decrement by 2; the cycle then repeats. If the gate signal goes low while the output is low, the output is immediately set high. New count handling: The current counting sequence is unaffected when a new count is written. If a trigger is received after writing a new count but before the end of the current half-cycle of the square wave, the counter loads the new count on the next CLK pulse and continues counting from there; otherwise, the new count is loaded at the end of the current half-cycle. Mode 4: Software-Triggered Strobe Normal operation: The output starts high. The output goes low for one CLK pulse after reaching terminal count. Gate control: Gate = 1 enables counting; Gate = 0 disables counting. New count handling: A newly written count is loaded on the next CLK pulse and counting continues from this new value. For two-byte counts: writing the first byte has no effect on counting; writing the second byte allows the new count to be loaded on the next CLK pulse. Mode 5: Hardware-Triggered Strobe Normal operation: The output starts high. Counting is triggered by the rising edge of the Gate signal. The output goes low for one CLK pulse after reaching terminal count. Retriggering: If triggering occurs during counting, the initial count is loaded on the next CLK pulse and counting continues until terminal count is reached. New count handling: The current counting sequence is unaffected. If a trigger occurs after a new count is written but before terminal count is reached, the counter loads the new count on the next CLK pulse and continues counting from there. Hardware-Triggered Modes (Non-repeating, but retriggerable) Mode 1: Hardware Retriggerable One-Shot Mode 5: Hardware-Triggered Strobe Lecture 9: Interrupts and 8259 There are 256 total interrupt types: INT 00 to INT 0FFh. Type * 4 equals the physical address of the interrupt vector (the first 1KB stores interrupt vectors, called the Interrupt Vector Table (IVT)). An interrupt vector points to the entry address of the corresponding interrupt service routine (ISR). Interrupt Categories Hardware (external) interrupts: Maskable (from INTR) Non-maskable (from NMI) Software (internal) interrupts: Invoked via the INT instruction. Predefined conditional (exception) interrupts. Hardware Interrupts Maskable interrupt: Trigger: INTR pin, active-high input signal. Type: No predefined type. IF = 1 enables interrupts; IF = 0 disables them. STI sets IF, CLI clears IF. Causes: Interrupt requests from external I/O devices. Procedure: The CPU responds to INTR requests: external I/O devices send interrupt requests to the CPU; the CPU checks the INTR pin on the last cycle of an instruction. If INTR is high and IF = 1, the CPU responds to the request. The CPU sends two negative pulses on the ~INTA pin to the I/O device. After receiving the second ~INTA, the I/O device sends the interrupt type N on the data bus. The CPU executes the ISR for INT N: it reads N from the data bus, pushes the FR onto the stack, clears IF and TF, pushes the CS and IP of the next instruction onto the stack, loads the ISR entry address, and jumps to the ISR. At the end of the ISR, IRET pops IP, CS, and FR in order, allowing the CPU to return to the previous program and resume execution. Software interrupts: INT xx instruction: An ISR is called when the INT xx instruction is executed. For example, int 21h is used for DOS services. The CPU always responds and executes the corresponding ISR, regardless of the IF setting. Any ISR can be invoked via the INT instruction. Predefined conditional interrupts: INT 00: Divide error (dividing a number by zero or resulting quotient is too large). INT 01: Single-step interrupt (if TF = 1, the CPU generates an INT 1 interrupt after executing each instruction, used for debugging). INT 03: Breakpoint interrupt (when the CPU hits a breakpoint set in the program, it generates an INT 3 interrupt for debugging). INT 04: Signed number overflow interrupt (triggered by the INTO instruction; checks the OF flag after an arithmetic instruction). INT 02: NMI interrupt. Procedure: For NMI: The CPU checks for NMI, automatically generates an INT 02 interrupt regardless of IF, and executes the corresponding ISR. For software/internal interrupts: The CPU automatically generates an INT N interrupt and executes the corresponding ISR. There are 256 interrupts in total: 0–4 are dedicated. 5–31 are reserved for system use. 32–255 are reserved for user applications. Interrupt priority: INT > NMI > INTR. Priority of INTR interrupts: Resolved via software polling or hardware checking. Vectored interrupt controllers, such as the 8259 (Programmable Interrupt Controller, or PIC), manage interrupt requests. These are flexible peripheral controller chips capable of handling 64 interrupt inputs, supporting masking, and allowing programming of various priority schemes. Originally sold as separate ICs, they are now integrated into motherboard chipsets and modern processors. Higher-priority interrupts can interrupt lower-priority ones. Lecture 10: BIOS and DOS Programming BIOS INT 10H Programming The INT 10H subroutines are stored in the ROM BIOS (on 80x86-based IBM PCs) and are used to interact with the computer's screen video. Examples include changing character/background colors, clearing the screen, setting the cursor position, and drawing lines on the screen. Different functions are invoked by setting AH to specific values. Scrolling windows: Register Description AH 06h/07h AL Number of lines to scroll BH Display attribute CH Y coordinate of top-left corner CL X coordinate of top-left corner DH Y coordinate of bottom-right corner DL X coordinate of bottom-right corner If AL = 0, the entire window is cleared. Set cursor position: AH = 02h Register Function BH Page number DH Row DL Column Set video mode: AH = 00h In text mode, the screen is treated as a matrix of character rows and columns. For example, AL = 03h selects VGA 80x25 characters with 16 colors. In graphics mode, the screen is treated as a matrix of horizontal and vertical pixels, where each pixel can have a different color. The size of video memory determines the number of pixels and available colors. For example, AL = 13H selects VGA 320x200 pixels with 256 colors. DOS Interrupt 21H Provided by MS-DOS, based on the BIOS-ROM. Once DOS is loaded into memory, INT 21H can be used to perform useful functions such as reading keyboard input and displaying results on the screen. Different functions are invoked by setting AH to specific values. AH = 09H: Output string on screen: Sends a set of ASCII data to the monitor. DX is set to the offset address of the ASCII string to be displayed (assuming DS is the data segment). All characters are displayed until the dollar sign $ is encountered. AH = 4CH: Exit to DOS: MOV AX, 4C00H INT 21H Lecture 11: Serial Data Communication and 8251 Data transmission refers to transferring data from one point to another. A communication channel is the medium used to convey information, such as copper wires, optical fibers, or wireless communication channels. Two Types of Data Transfer Parallel data transfer: Each bit uses a separate line (wire); typically 8 or more lines are used, along with control signals. Advantages: Fast; Disadvantages: Expensive; Used for short-distance communication. Serial data transfer: Uses a single data line to send bits one after another; no dedicated lines for control signals. Advantages: Cheap; Disadvantages: Slow; Used for long-distance communication. Serial Communication Details Data Transfer Rate Symbol rate (a misnomer for baud rate): The number of distinct symbols or pulse changes (signaling events) made to the transmission medium per second in a digitally modulated signal or line code, measured in baud. Each symbol can represent one (binary encoded signal) or several bits of data. Bit rate: The number of bits conveyed or processed per unit of time, measured in bits per second (bit/s or bps). Synchronization Methods Asynchronous serial communication: Transfers one byte at a time. The start of each byte is asynchronous, so each byte requires synchronization between the sender and receiver via a start bit. For example: 1 start bit, 8 data bits per character, 1 parity bit, 2 stop bits. At 100 characters per second, the baud rate is 100*(1+8+1+2) = 1200bps. Synchronous serial communication: Transfers a block of data at a time. The sender and receiver are synchronized at the start of data transfer using sync characters. This includes: Character-oriented synchronous transmission. Bit-oriented synchronous transmission. Communication Modes Simplex: Data flows in only one direction. Example: Printers. Half-duplex: Data can be transmitted in one direction at a time. Example: Walkie-talkies. Full-duplex: Data can flow in both directions simultaneously. Example: Telephones. Error Detection Parity bit: Used in asynchronous serial communication. An extra parity bit is added to the end of each character. Even-parity means the total number of 1s in the data plus the parity bit is even; odd-parity is the opposite. CRC calculation: For vk-bit data and n-bit CRC, CRC is used to detect errors in transmitted data.

items.title: 暑期旅途
items.content: 暑期旅途 2023年的暑假，自六月中旬开始，至八月中下旬的军训，我一度以为这可能是我最长的假期，也是旅游最多的假期了：我于7月与友人前去西藏，看了银河横跨星空、路过赛马比赛、赏了冰川遇了藏羚羊；于7月底去了日本，在福冈拜访了林爷爷，泡了日本温泉，喜欢上了京都这座城市，和奈良小鹿贴贴，并且在归国的飞机上发了烧；于8月重游南京，重访明孝陵，在夫子庙人挤人，又顺路去了扬州游览瘦西湖，并且在旅途中就发烧了。充实又开心，我知道，这将是我此生难忘的一个夏天。 谁知第二年——也就是今年的暑假，我因无小学期，放了足足3个月的假，从6月中到9月中，于是我竟然比去年旅游的次数还要多——这一年暑假也将是此生难忘吧？ 北京 6月前去北京。上海是一座气候舒适但是没什么文化底蕴的城市，北京是一座文化底蕴深厚但是不怎么舒适的城市——感觉这是大多数北京的同学对于北京的看法。兴许是时间的缘故吧，我并未体会到北京的不舒适，仅有的几天停留中，也还没来得及吃厌北京火锅和北京烤鸭。 我是有点嫉妒北京的文化底蕴的，总觉得随便一个地方都能和历史上的某一个事件联系起来，这种与过去连接的感觉非常奇妙。虽然如果从小住在北京，或是在北京住了足够长的时间，应该会对这种感觉越来越不屑吧？ 在北京拜访了几位友人，并且长谈。许久不见，总有说不完的话。与y聊天的那一夜的酒喝到近23:00，地铁停运，在这座陌生的城市里骑了一个钟头共享单车才到旅馆——清北的位置真的是偏远啊！那天晚上还路过了友校： 虽然本不想安排得非常累，但是没想到最后还是有些特种兵。最累的一天反而不是去长城的那一天——那一天早起，8点到八达岭长城的时候已经人满为患。有人抄近路乘缆车到离好汉坡只有一楼之遥的北7楼（没记错的话），我是从北一楼一路爬到了好汉坡，又一路爬到了没什么人的最最末尾北十二楼，在那里与一位大叔分别为对方合影留念，最后在北十一楼下长城。最累的是游览颐和园、圆明园和清北的那一天。颐和、圆明二园本就很大，最后也没有完全兜玩，只是确保那些必看的都去一一参观过。随后去清，不料清在自招活动之类的，未能如愿进校，前去北，leo带我兜了一圈，随后与leo前去王府井参观Apple store和它对面的Huawei store（这就是无可救药的果粉）。那一天走了3万余步，最累。 庆丰包子味道一般，但是看上去很有帝王之气。 崇明 去崇明也是临时起意，起因是身为护士的母亲难得地有了连续两天的休息，就决定前去从未去过但是不远的崇明岛。 一路开车过去的，经过上海长江大桥（可惜上海市长不是江大桥了），我妈有感而发：“这座桥值得50元路费。” 崇明两天主要就逛逛各种森林公园，吃吃便宜又美味的农家乐。农家乐的饭菜真的比商场预制菜好吃一百万倍！（是不是商场里除了烤肉和火锅都是预制菜。。。）海边有很多螃蟹。 看到东滩可以夜公园，想起来之前读到过上海最适合观星的地方是崇明，想以后带着望远镜来看星星。东滩好像是一个扬子鳄保护基地之类的，可惜没见到扬子鳄。 回家的时候意外地发现嘉定的电视塔和电线杆很日本，在车上胡乱拍了一张。 嵊泗 去嵊泗也是临时起意，原因也是身为护士的母亲难得地有了连续两天的休息。一路开车过去，经过东海大桥，我妈有感而发：“这座桥值100元路费。” 到了沈家湾码头，一路乘船去嵊泗，船蛮稳的，不晕。穿上在放奥运会。 嵊泗是一座美丽的小岛，爱上了，加入旅居城市清单了。海边真的很美，好想永远住在海边啊！ 在这里租不到山地自行车，所以只能租电瓶车环岛骑行，非常舒适，只是我还是更喜欢自行车一些。 第二天早起看日出，结果没看到，有山挡着，太阳不是从海里出来的，而是从山后出来的。 海边好多小螃蟹和海蟑螂。 长沙张家界 与Leo一起去的，住在五一广场，也就是市中心，离Apple Store很近，两个无可救药的果粉在长沙Apple store体验vision pro（这已经是我第三次体验vision pro了）。 马王堆汉墓和湖南博物馆都要提前预约，我们临行前才想起，马王堆汉墓去不成了，湖南博物馆在携程上找了一个导游带我们讲解参观，导游水平很高，感觉性格很受。在湖南博物馆看到了辛追夫人，这么看来也不用去马王堆汉墓了。 在长沙呆了两天后，去了张家界。 张家界全是土菜馆，所以我也吃得很开心——美味无比！我爱土菜馆！我爱农家乐！量大管饱又美味！建议交大开满中国各地的农家乐。 张家界很奇妙，或许是阿凡达拍摄地的缘故吧，所以感觉外国人比例甚至可能超过了上海市中心，甚至是可以和交大这样的大学相当。 山真的是一重一重的。 不过我对于张家界的感知也并没有觉得景色非常美，感觉壮观归壮观，但是不过尔尔。不过值得一提的是那里的接驳车系统——原始但是有效！那里的接驳车系统如下：接驳车按照规定的路线行驶，和司机说好你要去哪里，他沿着路线放你下去之后你去找工作人员，工作人员会告诉你接下来乘坐哪一班接驳车并且告知那个司机自己的目的地。这个看上去有点原始的系统竟然出奇地高效！repect respect 我和Leo一直有一个感知：SHSer的走路速度一直比普通人快一些，尤其是对于普通人正常的速度，我们会觉得很难受，有点高不成低不就，再快一点慢一点都会舒服得多。这一点在张家界那里得到了印证：游客中心说要30分钟的路程，我们竟然只走了15分钟，对此颇为惊讶。在金鞭溪那里的时候，由于是平地，我们记了个时，发现2.58km的走路配速竟然是12'11''，还有两段7km的记录，竟然配速也是15'多，真是擅长走路的两个人。 btw，金鞭溪好多🐒。 这只猢狲看上去在深思 在机场回上海候机的时候遇到两个同去上海的人，他们像是科技控股相关公司的员工，与他们相谈甚欢，我和Leo正好专业对口，又是果粉。对方提到想投资安克，正在做调研，安克正是主流苹果配件厂商之一。 日本 重访日本，此次主要目的是带外公外婆出过玩玩——外婆还接到了太外婆的任务，买点酥心糖吃吃：太外婆记得小时候吃到的东洋糖非常甜，想吃吃看。酥心糖是没有买到，但是买了很多软糖硬糖和糕点。买的大福本还担心她咬不动，结果竟然一下子吃了8个，吃得晚饭都吃不下。 此次依次拜访了名古屋-京都-奈良-大阪。填补了一些去年的遗憾吧。 名古屋去年未去过，但感觉大名鼎鼎，去看了看名古屋城。 京都去年的遗憾很多，一一填补：在伏见稻荷大社重买了去年弄丢的狐狸玩具、进去了去年过了参拜时间而没能参观的国宝金阁寺、参观了去年根本没时间去的二条城。我发现我对京都已经开始有点熟悉了，有一夜家人都累了在酒店休息，我独自出去逛，凭我的记忆走到了去年住的酒店。在鸭川旁边坐了很久。京都也是一个以后有机会一定要来旅居的城市！加入旅居列表！ 奈良重访小鹿，它们比去年凶一些，可能是秋天发情期的缘故吧？今年进了春日大社——去年在春日大社门口遇见了P同学，长谈之后竟然过了参观时间。 在大阪的第一天我又一次经过了打烊的黑门市场，但是在最后回国的那一天上午，我终于见到了开门的黑门市场！A5和牛美味。三度经过了去年吃的一家烧肉，可惜此次没机会吃，下次再去。 在日本的几天，我的外公外婆其实不是很吃得惯日本的饭菜，甚至我妈也没有很吃得惯——本以为日本与中国足够近，应该菜品也足够相近的。到头来，我的外公外婆最满意的是两顿弥生轩的日式快餐和一顿一兰拉面。 此次出行也有一些插曲，四人各犯了一次错： 我：把Apple pencil落在京都的酒店，连夜从奈良赶回京都，再回奈良几乎是乘到了JR的末班车。 母亲：约定好在A地点等我，我送疲倦的外公外婆回酒店后回到A点，竟然不见踪影，电话也打不通，此时还暴雨骤降，我只好狼狈地去罗森躲雨。后来知道她只是去逛免税店了，免税店太吵接不到电话。 外婆：上面我送外公外婆回酒店的原因不仅仅是因为他们疲倦，还因外婆的手机落在了酒店。 外公：在机场跟着我们走结果自己走散了，还好距离不远，找到了。 总之还是较为顺利，没出什么大岔子。 以及此次去日本在京都遇到了T同学，去年也在奈良遇到了P同学，真是他乡遇故知啊！ 其他的一些碎碎念 其实主要想讲讲日记。 我是从2018年8月1日开始写日记的，之所以这个日期记得这么清楚，是因为这是我去新加坡马来西亚旅游出发的日子。我为什么要记日记呢？其实是害怕遗忘——我太珍视自己的记忆了——记了日记，我就可以更放心地遗忘了。（其实拍照也是一个道理啊！） 一直以来，我写日记是传统的纸笔写日记的。上了大学之后，写日记是为数不多还需要用到笔的场景，我也因此格外珍惜用纸笔写日记的机会。可是在旅途中，把日记带出去又厚重又不安全，正巧iOS17发布了手记app，我便在旅途中体验体验，在此分享一下自己的感受： 电子日记最令人顾虑的是数据，不过目前绝大多数日记平台都支持导出日记/打印日记了，这是我敢用电子日记的大前提！电子日记的最大优点是记录多媒体：手记app每次都会推荐放在日记里的图片、定位等多媒体，我很喜欢。不仅如此，还有一个记录心情功能，这个功能是我最心水的，我几乎想以后不用纸笔记日记了。 但是它也有痛点：没有iPad版，也就意味着它不能手写，我认为这就失去了日记的感觉——其实用Apple pencil写日记已经让我感到勉为其难了，但是手记只能在手机上打字，因此我放弃了这个计划。 但是我有计划将手记app和纸质日记的优点相结合： 在旅途中，我会选择手记app，不用带出日记本，安全又方便。而且旅途中会有大量照片、定位，正合适手记app。 平时，我会记录纸质日记，但我打算参考手记app的记录心情功能，给自己做一些小便签小贴纸记录每天的心情。
items.content_en: Summer Journey The summer vacation of 2023 started in mid-June and ended with military training in late August. I once thought this would be my longest and most travel-packed holiday: In July, I went to Tibet with a friend, where we saw the Milky Way spanning the sky, passed by a horse racing event, admired glaciers, and spotted Tibetan antelopes; at the end of July, I went to Japan, visited Grandpa Lin in Fukuoka, soaked in Japanese hot springs, fell in love with Kyoto, cuddled with deer in Nara, and even had a fever on the flight back to China; in August, I revisited Nanjing, went to Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum again, got caught in the crowds at Confucius Temple, stopped by Yangzhou to visit Slender West Lake, and also had a fever during the trip. It was a fulfilling and joyful time, and I know this will be a summer I’ll never forget. Who would have thought that the following year—this year’s summer vacation—I had a full 3 months off due to the absence of a short semester, from mid-June to mid-September. As a result, I traveled even more times than last year—will this summer also be unforgettable? Beijing I went to Beijing in June. Shanghai is a city with a comfortable climate but little cultural heritage, while Beijing has profound cultural heritage but is less comfortable—this seems to be the view of most Beijing students. Perhaps it was due to timing, but I didn’t experience the discomfort of Beijing; during my few days there, I didn’t even get tired of eating Beijing hot pot and Peking duck. I’m a little envious of Beijing’s cultural heritage; I always feel that any place here can be linked to an event in history, and this sense of connection to the past is truly wonderful. Of course, if I had lived in Beijing since childhood or for a long enough period, I might have grown indifferent to this feeling. I visited a few friends in Beijing and had long chats with them. It’s always hard to run out of things to talk about after a long separation. I drank until nearly 23:00 with Y that night, and when the subway stopped running, I rode a shared bike for an hour to reach the hotel in this unfamiliar city—Tsinghua and Peking University are really located in remote areas! I also passed by a sister university that night: Although I didn’t plan to make the schedule too tiring, I ended up being quite of a “special forces traveler” after all. The most exhausting day wasn’t the one I went to the Great Wall—I left early that day, and when I arrived at Badaling Great Wall at 8 AM, it was already packed with people. Some people took a shortcut and took the cable car to North Tower 7, which is just one floor away from Hero Slope; I climbed from North Tower 1 all the way to Hero Slope, then continued to North Tower 12 at the very end where there were few people. There, I took a photo with an uncle as a souvenir, and finally descended from North Tower 11. The most tiring day was the one I spent visiting the Summer Palace, Old Summer Palace, and Tsinghua and Peking University. The Summer Palace and Old Summer Palace are both very large, and I didn’t manage to see everything, but I made sure to visit all the must-see spots. Then I went to Tsinghua, but unfortunately, there was a recruitment event going on and I couldn’t enter the campus. I went to Peking University instead, where Leo showed me around. After that, Leo and I went to Wangfujing to visit the Apple Store and the Huawei Store across from it (typical die-hard Apple fans). We walked over 30,000 steps that day—that was the most exhausting part. Qingfeng Baozi tastes average, but it looks quite regal. Chongming My trip to Chongming was a last-minute decision. My mother, who is a nurse, had two consecutive days off for the first time, so we decided to go to Chongming Island, a place we had never been to but was nearby. We drove there and crossed the Shanghai Yangtze River Bridge (too bad the mayor of Shanghai isn’t Jiang Daqiao!). My mom remarked, “This bridge is worth the 50 yuan toll.” We spent two days in Chongming mainly exploring various forest parks and eating cheap and delicious farmhouse meals. Farmhouse food is a million times better than pre-made dishes from supermarkets! (Are all pre-made dishes in supermarkets anything other than grilled meat and hot pot...?) There were lots of crabs by the sea. I saw that Dongtan has a night park and remembered reading before that Chongming is the best place for stargazing in Shanghai. I plan to bring a telescope there to watch the stars someday. Dongtan seems to be a Yangtze alligator conservation base or something similar; unfortunately, we didn’t see any alligators. When we got home, I unexpectedly noticed that the TV tower and utility poles in Jiading looked very Japanese. I snapped a random photo in the car. Shengsi My trip to Shengsi was also a last-minute decision, again because my mother, a nurse, had two consecutive days off. We drove there and crossed the East China Sea Bridge; my mom commented, “This bridge is worth 100 yuan in tolls.” We arrived at Shenjiawan Wharf and took a ferry to Shengsi. The ride was very stable, and I didn’t get seasick. The Olympics were being broadcast on the ship. Shengsi is a beautiful island; I fell in love with it and added it to my list of cities to live in. The seaside is really stunning—I wish I could live by the sea forever! We couldn’t rent mountain bikes there, so we had to rent electric scooters to ride around the island, which was very comfortable, though I still prefer regular bicycles. I got up early the next day to watch the sunrise, but didn’t see it—there were mountains blocking the view, so the sun rose behind the mountains instead of from the sea. There were lots of small crabs and sea cockroaches by the sea. Changsha & Zhangjiajie I went there with Leo and stayed in Wuyi Square, the city center, which is close to the Apple Store. Two hopeless Apple fans tried out the Vision Pro at the Changsha Apple Store (this was my third time trying it). Both Mawangdui Han Tombs and Hunan Museum require advance reservations. We realized this only before leaving, so we couldn’t visit the Mawangdui Han Tombs. For the Hunan Museum, we hired a tour guide through Ctrip to lead us through the exhibits; the guide was very knowledgeable and had a great personality. We saw Lady Xinzhui at the Hunan Museum, so it seemed we didn’t need to go to the Mawangdui Han Tombs after all. After spending two days in Changsha, we went to Zhangjiajie. Zhangjiajie is full of local restaurants, so I enjoyed the food there a lot—it was incredibly delicious! I love local restaurants! I love farmhouse meals! They’re generous, filling, and tasty! I recommend everyone to visit farmhouse meals all over China. Zhangjiajie is quite magical; perhaps because it was the filming location for Avatar, the proportion of foreigners there might even exceed that of downtown Shanghai, and it’s comparable to a university like Jiao Tong University. The mountains here are layered one after another. However, I didn’t find the scenery in Zhangjiajie particularly breathtaking; it was impressive, but nothing extraordinary. One thing worth mentioning is their shuttle bus system—primitive but effective! The shuttle bus system works like this: the buses follow a set route; you tell the driver where you want to go, and after he drops you off along the route, you find a staff member who will tell you which next shuttle bus to take and inform the driver of your destination. This seemingly primitive system is surprisingly efficient! Respect, respect. Leo and I have always noticed that SHSers walk faster than ordinary people; we find the normal walking speed of others uncomfortable, and feel much more at ease when they walk faster or slower. This was confirmed in Zhangjiajie: the visitor center said the journey would take 30 minutes, but we only took 15 minutes, which surprised us. While we were at Jinbianxi, since it was flat ground, we timed ourselves and found that our pace for 2.58km was 12'11'', and we even had two records of 7km with a pace of over 15'. What great walkers we are! By the way, there were lots of monkeys at Jinbianxi. This monkey looked deep in thought. While waiting for my flight back to Shanghai at the airport, I met two people heading to Shanghai as well; they worked for a tech holding company. We had a great chat, and since Leo and I were majoring in relevant fields and were Apple fans, they mentioned they were considering investing in Anker, a leading Apple accessory manufacturer. Japan I revisited Japan, mainly to take my grandparents on a trip—my grandmother even had a mission from her own grandmother to buy some sugar-coated almonds to eat; her grandmother remembered how sweet the Oriental candies she ate as a child were and wanted to try them again. We didn’t buy the sugar-coated almonds, but we bought lots of soft candies, hard candies, and pastries. I was worried my grandmother wouldn’t be able to chew the mochi we bought, but she ate 8 pieces in one go and couldn’t even have dinner afterward. We visited Nagoya, Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka in sequence, making up for some of last year’s regrets. I hadn’t been to Nagoya last year, but it’s quite famous, so I went to see Nagoya Castle. I had many regrets in Kyoto last year, which I made up for one by one: I repurchased the fox toy I lost last year at Fushimi Inari Shrine, visited Kinkaku-ji Temple, a national treasure, which we missed due to closing time last year, and visited Nijo Castle, which we didn’t have time for last year. I found that I was starting to get familiar with Kyoto. One night, when my family was tired and resting in the hotel, I went out alone and, relying on my memory, walked to the hotel where we stayed last year. I sat by the Kamo River for a long time. Kyoto is also a city I definitely want to live in if I get the chance in the future! Added to my list of cities to live in! I revisited the deer in Nara; they were more aggressive than last year, probably because it’s their mating season in autumn. This year, I entered Kasuga Taisha Shrine—last year, I met classmate P at the entrance of Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and after a long chat, we missed the visiting time. On the first day in Osaka, I passed by the closed Kuromon Market again, but on the morning of our last day before returning to China, I finally saw the open Kuromon Market! A5 Wagyu beef was delicious. We passed by a yakiniku restaurant we ate at last year three times, but unfortunately didn’t have a chance to eat there this time; I’ll go next time. During our few days in Japan, my grandparents weren’t very used to Japanese food, and neither was my mom—I thought Japan was close enough to China that the cuisine would be similar. In the end, my grandparents were most satisfied with two meals of Yasai-ken’s Japanese fast food and one bowl of Ippudo ramen. There were also a few mishaps during this trip; each of the four of us made a mistake: Me: I left my Apple Pencil in the Kyoto hotel. I rushed back to Kyoto from Nara overnight and then back to Nara, almost catching the last JR train. Mother: She agreed to meet me at Location A. After taking my tired grandparents back to the hotel and returning to Location A, she was nowhere to be seen, and I couldn’t reach her by phone. It was pouring rain at the time, so I had to take shelter in a Lawson store in a sorry state. Later I found out she had gone shopping at a duty-free store, where it was too noisy to hear her phone. Grandmother: The reason I took my grandparents back to the hotel wasn’t just because they were tired, but also because her phone was left in the hotel. Grandfather: He followed us at the airport but got separated; fortunately, he wasn’t far away and we found him quickly. Overall, the trip went smoothly with no major issues. Also, I met classmate T in Kyoto this time, and classmate P in Nara last year—what a pleasant surprise to meet old friends in a foreign land! Some Random Thoughts Actually, I mainly want to talk about diaries. I started writing a diary on August 1, 2018, and I remember this date so clearly because it was the day I left for a trip to Singapore and Malaysia. Why do I keep a diary? It’s actually to avoid forgetting—I cherish my memories so much—by keeping a diary, I can forget with more peace of mind. (Taking photos works the same way!) Until now, I’ve been writing traditional paper-and-pen diaries. After entering university, writing a diary became one of the few scenarios where I still needed to use a pen, so I cherished the opportunity to write a diary by hand even more. However, taking a diary with me while traveling is bulky and unsafe. Coincidentally, iOS 17 released the Notes app, so I tried it during my trip and would like to share my thoughts here: The biggest concern about digital diaries is data security, but most diary platforms today support exporting or printing diaries, which is the prerequisite for me to use a digital diary! The greatest advantage of digital diaries is recording multimedia: the Notes app always recommends images, locations, and other multimedia to include in the diary, which I like very much. On top of that, there’s a mood-tracking feature, which is my favorite—I almost want to stop using paper diaries in the future. But it does have a drawback: there’s no iPad version, meaning you can’t write by hand, which I think takes away the feeling of keeping a diary—actually, writing a diary with an Apple Pencil already feels forced for me, but since the Notes app only allows typing on a phone, I gave up on this plan. However, I plan to combine the advantages of the Notes app and paper diaries: During trips, I’ll use the Notes app—no need to carry a diary, it’s safe and convenient. Plus, there are lots of photos and locations during trips, which fits the Notes app perfectly. Normally, I’ll write a paper diary, but I plan to follow the mood-tracking feature of the Notes app and make small sticky notes to record my mood each day.

items.title: 没抢到果子首发的经历
items.title_en: My experience of missing the iPhone 16 Pro Max launch sale
items.content: 没抢到果子首发的经历 好笑，时隔一年整，没抢到首发 今年吸取了去年的教训，决定抢贵一点的机型，因为愿意加钱买首发的富哥富姐想必也会无脑冲超级顶配吧？所以我和Bill都筹集了资金，决定一人购置两台iPhone 16 pro max 1t机型 但是事情出现了转机：发布会之后，9/13日之前，我先前去闲鱼进行一些市场调研，发现挂出来的基本上都是256g的机型，也就是iPhone 16 pro max的最低配，令人感到疑惑。可能性有二： 没有人买1t版本，大家都买256g，所以大家都挂256g 没有人有1t的货，所以说1t非常抢手 最终我和Bill决定，我购置一台256g，一台1t，Bill购置两台512，平摊风险 我特地在抢之前熟悉了一下流程。去年是在Apple store直接购买的。今年由于原账号转了美区，美区支付方式没有微信支付宝和储蓄卡，只有信用卡，而我没有信用卡，因此只得作罢。在淘宝Apple Store官方、京东Apple自营店、微信小程序Apple store中。最终选择了微信小程序Apple store，因其与Apple store体验最相似。 13日20时，准时开抢！ 情况如图，Hertz最为fx，竟然进去了不买，只是去逛逛，像是除夕夜去南京路轧闹猛 随后我出状况了，我之前把钱集中到了我的上海银行卡里面，结果发现有限额，而且限额只有5000，我连转都转不出去。最后还是我妈的协助下购置的两台。虽然20:06就登上了，本应07就付款，结果硬生生一台10分一台15分付的款。 与此同时Bill亦出状况了，他给我打电话，我不接。后来发现又是钱的问题，又是颜色的问题，好像也拖得较晚，但比我略早一些。 买是买上了，有没有首发呢？ 去年Leo也是碰到银行卡限额的问题，群里东拼西凑借满了钱，记得是拖到20分上下才付款，结果还是首发，所以应该能抢到吧？ 第二天早上起来一看：预计送货日期10/14-18，心凉了半截 于是乎，直接退货，现在已经是这样了，， 与Bill交流发现他亦未抢到首发，他最后不知怎么抢了3台，看上去都是第二批 我帮他挂了闲鱼，看看能不能赚到钱吧。。。 Bill补充分析： 真是奇怪没想到最热门的是白色，经典咏流传啊！新颜色不过尔尔。 综上所述，银行卡限额真的是罪大恶极！！ 我气急败坏，于昨日前去上海银行解决此问题，打算将日限额提至每日50k，月限额保持每月100k 昨日先前去观看电影《里斯本丸号沉没》，随后就驱自行车前往上海银行嘉定总行 到号之后又等待许久，才得知这张银行卡既没有工资进出，有没有贷款进出，所以5000的限额已经算是很大了。我疑惑、惊讶，感觉银行、款项大、5000元人民币两两都有关系，可三个放在一起就有些好笑。 银行职员为我提出了两条解决方法： 转入另一张无限额的银行卡。可是我的别的银行卡都各有各的用处，不想混在一起搞不清楚，作罢 办一张信用卡，bingo！ 我一直都想办一张信用卡，因为对于国际支付方便一些，正好趁此机会顺水推舟办一张 网上查找后，发现可以学生零额度申请而且支持国际支付的推荐去上海银行，于是穿过马路前往中国银行嘉定总行 微信扫了一个码，按照指示输入相关信息后，眼看临门一脚，发现界面加载不出 在浏览器中打开、在中国银行app内均不行 遂作罢，估计中秋系统升级，过两天再尝试 唉此次抢iPhone 16 Pro Max计划出师不利、诸事不顺、功败垂成
items.content_en: My experience of missing the iPhone 16 Pro Max launch sale How funny — after a whole year, I still missed the launch sale. This year, I learned from last year's lesson and decided to go for a pricier model. Since rich folks willing to pay extra for the launch version would likely go for the top-tier configuration anyway, Bill and I pooled our money and decided to each buy two iPhone 16 Pro Max 1TB models. But then a twist happened: after the launch event, before September 13th, I did some market research on Xianyu and found that almost all listings were for the 256GB model, which is the base variant of the iPhone 16 Pro Max. This was quite puzzling. There are two possible explanations: No one bought the 1TB version, so everyone listed their 256GB models for sale. No one had 1TB units in stock, making the 1TB model extremely hard to get. In the end, Bill and I decided that I would buy one 256GB model and one 1TB model, while Bill would buy two 512GB models, to spread out the risk. I specifically familiarized myself with the purchase process beforehand. Last year, I bought directly from the Apple Store. This year, since my account was switched to the US region, the US region only supports credit cards as payment methods, and I don’t have a credit card, so I had to look elsewhere. I considered the official Apple Store on Taobao, JD.com's Apple flagship store, and the Apple Store mini-program on WeChat. In the end, I chose the Apple Store mini-program on WeChat because its user experience is most similar to the official Apple Store. At 8 PM on the 13th, the sale started on time! As shown in the image, Hertz was acting really weird — he got in but didn’t buy anything, just browsed around, like going to Nanjing Road to join the crowd during Chinese New Year’s Eve. Then I ran into a problem: I had transferred all my money to my Shanghai Bank card, only to find out it had a daily limit of 5,000 yuan, and I couldn’t even transfer more than that. In the end, I relied on my mom’s help to buy the two phones. Although I logged in at 8:06 PM and was supposed to pay at 8:07 PM, I ended up paying for one phone at 8:10 PM and the other at 8:15 PM. Meanwhile, Bill also ran into issues. He called me but I didn’t answer. Later I found out it was another problem related to payment and color options, which delayed his purchase a bit, but he finished earlier than me. So we did manage to buy the phones, but did we get them during the launch sale? Last year, Leo also faced a bank card limit issue. He borrowed money from friends in the group to meet the requirement and paid around 8:20 PM, yet still got the launch version. So maybe we could still qualify? The next morning, I checked: the estimated delivery date was October 14–18, which was a huge disappointment. So I simply returned the phones, and now this is the situation. I talked to Bill and found out he also missed the launch sale. He somehow ended up buying 3 phones, which all turned out to be from the second batch. I listed them on Xianyu for him to see if we can make a profit... Bill’s additional analysis: It’s really strange — I didn’t expect white to be the most popular color; it’s truly a case of “the classic never fades”! The new colors are just meh. In summary, bank card limits are truly the worst culprit!! Furious, I went to Shanghai Bank yesterday to resolve this issue and planned to raise my daily limit to 50,000 yuan and keep my monthly limit at 100,000 yuan. Yesterday, I first watched the movie The Sinking of the Lisbon Maru, then rode my bike to the Jiading headquarters of Shanghai Bank. After getting a number, I waited a long time before learning that since this bank card had no salary or loan transactions, a 5,000 yuan limit was already quite generous. I was puzzled and surprised — I feel there’s a connection between banks, large amounts of money, and 5,000 RMB, but putting all three together is kind of funny. The bank staff gave me two solutions: Transfer money to another unlimited bank card. But my other bank cards all have specific uses, and I don’t want to mix them up and cause confusion, so I declined. Apply for a credit card — bingo! I’ve always wanted to get a credit card because it’s more convenient for international payments. This was the perfect opportunity to take the plunge. After searching online, I found that students can apply for a zero-limit credit card that supports international payments, and Shanghai Bank was recommended. So I crossed the street to the Jiading headquarters of Bank of China. I scanned a QR code, entered the required information as instructed, and was just one step away from success when the page failed to load. It didn’t work either when opened in a browser or through the Bank of China app. So I gave up and figured the system was undergoing an upgrade for Mid-Autumn Festival, and I’d try again in a few days. Sigh, my plan to buy an iPhone 16 Pro Max ended in failure — everything went wrong and I fell short.

items.title: 高光时刻--还可以吧
items.content: 高光时刻--还可以吧 新年快乐🎉🎉 这是我第一次在假期里的苹果发布会，说来好笑，交大竟至今仍未开学 我的直观感受此次发布会无甚惊喜，基本都是常规更新，也有几款产品更新得很烂，真的毫无诚意 iPhone 系列 首先，iPhone16这个外观和颜色真的丑啊！！ 我其实很早之前就看到iPhone16的爆料渲染图了，看到这个设计的时候真的觉得是丑啊。我可以理解为了支持空间视频的功能，两个摄像头不能对角线放置，要水平/竖直放置，但是这个摄像头模块让人感到非常不协调：为什么要把闪光灯单独拉到摄像模块之外呢？如果用iPhone X那样的设计或者用iPhone 12那样的设计，我还是可以理解的，但是为了标新立异弄成这样，真的是可可又悲悲。不过不要低估苹果的畜牧业，我看了这个设计看了半年，竟然已被驯化，觉得这个外观还可以了，真的是果粉可悲的自适应。 其次，这个颜色真的有点奇怪。黑白是常规的颜色，另外三款颜色我认为不比去年（15系列的颜色真的是太好看了！），也是有点标新立异。其实我认为最大的问题在于摄像模块的颜色比周围深，色差较大，给人奇怪的感觉。三款彩色中，我认为绿色最佳，蓝色平平，粉色好丑。Hertz认为配色像垃圾桶，过于廉价。他这么一说真的回不来了。 比较令我惊讶的是iPhone16竟然也给了摄影键，本在惊叹刀钝了，没想到刀法依旧——压感功能是Pro exclusive的。 16Pro让人有点期待，毕竟A18Pro是第二代3纳米芯片，应该能解决去年A17Pro的发热问题，这才是满血3纳米！不过比较好笑，官方介绍里的对比默认对比的竟然是12Pro，一下让人觉得哑然失笑。 别的都是常规升级吧？我有一点没弄清楚，这次全系都有“融合式摄像头”，在标准版能承担广角和长焦的工作，有人看懂是什么意思嘛？还是说仅仅是另一个噱头？感觉标准版的长焦还是需要依靠裁切+算法。 Apple watch 系列 watch ultra只是多了新配色，无聊，不表。 watch x可以聊聊：官方给出的最大卖点是薄，不过私以为对于手表来说其实厚度的感知没有那么大，续航才是对于使用体验更重要的部分。目前的续航，正常用可以一天有点宽裕，但是如果旅游、记录大量运动，那么连一天的续航都没有，我在旅途中都是开低电量模式的，这会牺牲常亮显示、运动监测等功能。诚然，这一代升级了快充，但是谁会出门带一根watch的线呢？虽然第三方有小巧的充电头，但是那种又只能超级慢充，也不舒服。所以我认为走偏了——包括上半年的iPad pro我也觉得是类似的问题，不过那个变薄还比watch x变薄更有道理一些，上述的一些缺点并没有，而且变薄变轻的确舒适。 不过leo主张，现在的watch是比正常的watch厚一些，变薄是有道理的，体验确实会更好，不过让人觉得不如ultra 1。 比较牛的是熄屏显示可以1Hz刷新率了，所以说可以显示秒针了。以及亮面铝金属外壳看上去好看一些了，我一开始还以为是不锈钢。 另一件好笑的是：官方声称watch x边框变薄了，我认为我和绝大多数用户都想看到其相对于789的模具变薄了多少，结果官网只有和3456se对比，真是此地无银三百两。 AirPods系列 先说说好笑的AirPods Max，所有的升级只有新配色和type-C，芯片没换性能无提升——这不是和AirPods pro 2（type- C）一样，悄咪咪上架就行了嘛？我不要新颜色，能不能给我AirPods Max2 AirPods 4我认为不错，降噪效果能有AirPods pro一代的效果（还是从AirPods Max的介绍里推断出来的）、无线充电（普通+手表充电器）、力度感应器（就是不知道能不能调整音量，要是可以的话就完美了，不过以苹果的尿性估计是没有的）。总之就是最强半入耳！感觉是在音质和舒适性上找到了平衡点（不喜欢骨传导/耳夹式，音质差&漏音)。 综上所述 觉得还可以吧，中规中矩，不拉胯，但因为没什么有意思的。今年吸取了去年的经验，决定倒买倒卖iPhone 16 Pro Max 沙漠色 1Tb款，成本13999，最多亏0元，不知道能赚多少。
items.content_en: Highlight Moment -- So-so Happy New Year 🎉🎉 This is my first Apple event during a holiday. Funny enough, Jiaotong University still hasn’t started classes yet. My immediate impression of this event is that there were no major surprises; most updates were routine, and a few products had terrible upgrades with zero sincerity. iPhone Series First off, the design and colors of the iPhone 16 are really ugly!! I saw the leaked renders of the iPhone 16 quite a while ago, and I truly thought the design was hideous. I can understand that to support spatial video functionality, the two cameras can’t be placed diagonally and must be arranged horizontally or vertically. But this camera module looks extremely uncoordinated: why is the flash separated from the camera module? If they used a design similar to the iPhone X or iPhone 12, I could accept it. But doing this just for the sake of being different is really sad. However, don’t underestimate Apple’s ability to condition users — after seeing this design for half a year, I’ve been tamed into thinking the look is acceptable. Truly a tragic case of fan loyalty leading to adaptation. Secondly, the colors are a bit strange. Black and white are standard colors, but I think the other three colors aren’t as nice as last year’s (the colors of the 15 series were really gorgeous!). The biggest issue is that the color of the camera module is darker than the surrounding area, creating a noticeable color difference that looks odd. Among the three colored models, I think green is the best, blue is mediocre, and pink is ugly. Hertz said the color scheme looks like a trash can and feels too cheap. Once he said that, I couldn’t unsee it. To my surprise, the iPhone 16 also got a camera button. I was amazed at how predictable Apple’s moves are — the haptic feedback feature is still exclusive to Pro models. The 16 Pro is somewhat promising; after all, the A18 Pro is a second-generation 3nm chip that should resolve the overheating issues of the A17 Pro from last year. This is the true full-power 3nm chip! It’s funny though that the official comparison in the presentation uses the 12 Pro as the benchmark, which is quite amusing. Are the other upgrades all routine? There’s one thing I don’t understand: all models this time have a “hybrid camera” that can handle wide-angle and telephoto tasks on the standard version. Does anyone know what this means? Or is it just another marketing gimmick? I feel like the telephoto capability on the standard version still relies on cropping and algorithms. Apple Watch Series The Watch Ultra just got new colors — boring, so I won’t cover it. Let’s talk about the Watch X: the main selling point the official team highlights is its thinness. However, in my opinion, the thickness of a smartwatch isn’t that noticeable to users; battery life is a far more important factor for the overall experience. Currently, the battery can last a full day with moderate use, but if you’re traveling or tracking a lot of workouts, it won’t even last a day. I always use low-power mode when traveling, which disables features like the always-on display and workout tracking. True, this generation supports fast charging, but who would carry a Watch charger when going out? Although third-party manufacturers make compact chargers, they only support slow charging, which is inconvenient. So I think Apple took a wrong turn here — I had a similar view of the iPad Pro released earlier this year; at least its thinner design makes more sense, as it doesn’t have the above flaws, and being thinner and lighter is indeed more comfortable. However, Leo argues that the current Watch is thicker than normal models, so making it thinner is justified and does improve the experience. Still, he thinks it’s not as good as the Ultra 1. The coolest update is that the always-on display can now refresh at 1Hz, so the second hand can be displayed. Also, the shiny aluminum casing looks nicer; I initially thought it was stainless steel. Another funny thing: the official team claimed the Watch X has a thinner bezel. I, and most users, want to see how much thinner it is compared to the 7/8/9 models, but the official website only compares it to the 3/4/5/6/SE models. Talk about trying to hide something! AirPods Series Let’s start with the hilarious AirPods Max: the only upgrades are new colors and a USB-C port; the chip hasn’t changed and performance remains the same. Why not just quietly release an AirPods Max 2 instead of rebranding the old model with new colors? I don’t want new colors — give me an AirPods Max 2! I think the AirPods 4 are great: their noise cancellation is comparable to the first-gen AirPods Pro (I inferred this from the AirPods Max description), they support wireless charging (compatible with regular chargers and Watch chargers), and they have force sensors (I just wonder if volume can be adjusted; if so, they’d be perfect, but given Apple’s track record, that’s unlikely). In short, they’re the best semi-in-ear headphones! They strike a great balance between sound quality and comfort (I dislike bone-conduction and ear-hook designs due to poor sound quality and sound leakage). Conclusion I’d say it’s so-so — average, not bad, but nothing interesting. Having learned from last year’s experience, I decided to resell my iPhone 16 Pro Max in Desert Titanium with 1TB storage. The cost was 13,999 yuan, and I stand to lose at most 0 yuan. I wonder how much profit I’ll make.

items.title: 影评：《姥姥的外孙》
items.title_en: Movie Review: How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies
items.content: 永恒的难题 今天去看了姥姥的外孙 这是一部铺垫得很慢的电影。电影前半段我几乎以为是一部喜剧片，没想到这竟然只是糖衣，前后的呼应竟更让人唏嘘不已。 印象最深刻的镜头是几组火车的镜头。安乘着火车和大舅一家陪同外婆去烧香祈福，又一同乘回来；铁轨穿过繁忙但不繁华、热闹但不喧闹、市井但不低俗的郊区小镇；尤其是最后得知外婆为自己存款时，安愣住了，向后的火车的喧嚣遮盖了他杂乱的思绪，他恍惚看见小时外婆“轻易”的约定，向后的火车声音却变得平静，安回到此时此刻。铁轨上的天空，树梢之间，有彩虹。 从最后一次化疗后的剧情，真正让人落泪不止。 老人需要什么？老人需要陪伴。老人害怕什么？老人害怕孤独。老人爱自己的孩子，老人恨自己的孩子。老人又变回了孩子。安用手机给外婆看弱智美颜特效，安陪外婆打牌，安安慰深夜痛哭的外婆，安给临终的外婆唱安眠曲。 这个时代太快，让人不愿承认但又不得不承认，代沟就是在越来越大，后辈和长辈的话题真的越来越少，无非是新闻、饭菜、小时故事。诚然可悲，但又无可奈何。但是我依旧想多与长辈沟通，我想认识更加立体的自己的长辈，ta们作为一个真实的人，而不是相对于自己的一个身份。 我也很害怕我会变心。小孩子的心思很简单：我要孝顺，我希望所有人都好，就像电影中的彩虹说：“我长大要当医生为姥姥治病。”但是现实的种种风尘斑驳了赤字之心。大舅最后才想起来，自己夜不能寐的原因。我是独生子女家庭，相比大家庭子女之间地位的矛盾，独生子女家庭的矛盾更在于放不下孩子、也需要孩子的父母，和想为自己往前飞却又希望回头带着父母一起往前的瞻前顾后。父母曾经是一切——但是所有孩子都会背叛父母，父母不是一切；所有的父母也不得不接受这份背叛，让孩子向前飞。 长辈、后辈、友谊、利益、事业、爱情，我们迷失在其中，我们忘了一些誓言，但是总有人记得，但或许没人理得清这些关系吧？对这些关系做任何的比较或许都是一种痛苦。安不要再问外婆最爱的人是谁了，安对外婆说自己最爱的人是外婆。
items.content_en: The Eternal Dilemma I watched How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies today. This is a movie with a very slow build-up. In the first half, I almost thought it was a comedy, but it turned out to be just a sugar-coated exterior; the echoes between different parts of the film are even more heart-wrenching. The most memorable scenes involve trains. An takes the train with his eldest uncle’s family to accompany his grandma to pray for blessings, and they return together on the same train. The railway line runs through a suburban town that is busy yet not flashy, lively yet not noisy, and down-to-earth yet not vulgar. Especially when An learns that his grandma had saved money for him, he is stunned; the roar of the train moving backward drowns out his chaotic thoughts. He vaguely recalls the easy promise his grandma made when he was a child, and the sound of the train gradually fades into calm as he returns to the present moment. Above the railway tracks, among the treetops, there is a rainbow. The plot after the last round of chemotherapy truly brings tears to one's eyes. What do the elderly need? They need companionship. What do they fear? They fear loneliness. The elderly love their children, and they resent them too. Eventually, the elderly become like children again. An shows his grandma a silly beauty filter effect on his phone, plays cards with her, comforts her when she cries late at night, and sings her a lullaby as she lies on her deathbed. This era moves too fast; we reluctant to admit it, yet we have to. The generation gap is widening, and the topics between younger and older generations are dwindling to mere news, meals, and childhood stories. It is indeed sad, but there is nothing we can do about it. Still, I want to communicate more with my elders; I want to get to know the more three-dimensional versions of them as real people, rather than just seeing them as roles relative to myself. I also fear I might lose my original intentions. A child’s mind is simple: they want to be filial and hope everyone is well, just like Rainbow in the movie says, "When I grow up, I want to be a doctor to cure grandma’s illness." But the harsh realities of life tarnish this pure heart. It is only at the end that the eldest uncle realizes why he couldn’t sleep at night. In a one-child family, compared to the status conflicts among siblings in large families, the main conflict lies in parents who cannot let go of their child while still needing the child’s care, and children who want to move forward in life but also wish to look back and take their parents along. Parents used to be everything — but all children will eventually betray their parents; parents are not everything. All parents have to accept this betrayal and let their children fly forward. Elders, juniors, friendship, interests, career, love — we get lost in these, forgetting some promises along the way. But someone always remembers; perhaps no one can fully untangle these relationships anyway. Making any comparisons between these relationships might only bring pain. An no longer asks his grandma who she loves the most; he tells her that the person she loves most is herself.

items.content: 前言 v1.0 写这一份上中腔词典的原因是一时兴起。其实很难说我这里所说的“上中腔”的具体定义是什么。说是上中腔，但又主要是大师班的同学常用，但别的班也有一批同学会用。说是大师班的同学常用，但又主要是大师班的男生在用，女生们也会用其中的一些表述，但不多。为了简单起见，还是称其为上中腔好了。写这份东西写主要是图一乐，回顾一下以前的一些已经成为典故的趣事，不可当真。用上中腔的表述来说，这份东西其实非常🌭，ydfx。编写这份东西的时候，毛哥和Nababa同学给我提供了很多帮助，他们是我的第一批读者，帮助我扩充了一些词条，也回忆了有意思的故事，其中Nababa同学还帮我写了一些我不是很熟悉的词条。感谢zjh同学，在发布前夕又补充了大量词条。也感谢myj，sty同学，从他们那里我也了解到更多的一些我不熟悉的词条和它们的词源典故。以下的词条的例句来源于我与同学的聊天记录，感谢这些聊天记录！这些必然包含着我的片面性与局限性，欢迎扩充更多词条以及修订词条！ v1.1 修订、增补了一些词条。由于微信显示不出\dagger，\ddagger和\star符号，在微信公众号中改成了粗体、斜体和下划线。也欢迎下载原文档查看。感谢Nababa同学和try同学的批评指正以及提供的资料。 关于到底什么是“上中腔”，try同学认为这是九班腔，又因高三重分班后在大师班内广泛传播，随后又平行班也沾染了一些这种腔调。认为有一定道理，不知大家怎么看。感觉这确实很难定义，但确实有这么个东西。它可以是上中腔、九班腔甚至只是我身边的人的口癖。感觉这份东西还是非常主观啊！嗨不过也是写这好玩儿而已。只是一份🌭词典罢了 估计也就到1.1就差不多了吧。如果这份东西还能再写一个1.2就真的🌭又fx了。 【词源】来源于公众号“数学是思维的体操”。该公众号管理者是平几吧成员，曾请郭fj同学帮忙做平面几何题。后此公众号的名号经郭fj而在⑨班传播，因名字魔性遂成梗。 后面由于音近，有呕人变“体操”为“蕊尻”，更加发笑。 【变体】数学是思维的蕊尻 无头苍蝇$^\dagger$ 【释义】做出无脑行为的人 【词源】同来源于在郭fj同学的纯几何杯赛”大司马杯“号召中，提到：“笛卡尔的茅厕吸引了许多无头苍蝇”。 5. 模仿老师 像像我和你讲/说 【释义】发语词，用开玩笑语气表示通知或者规劝对方 【词源】吴jy老师说话有时有些口吃，她本身口头禅是“像我和你讲”，但应口吃就成了“像像我和你讲” you cross the line$^\dagger$ 【释义】你越界了 【词源】李p老师布置的一张flyer，一组使用高超PS技巧P出来了杰哥帮助同学买东西、解决住宿问题，最终被发现后被批越界 whip$^\dagger$ 【释义】鞭打 【词源】李p老师为了解释whip这个词的意思，在教室里展示whip 小f同学 6. 其他 be$^\star$ 【释义】上海话中的“be”发音的语气词，常与weisa连用，也可写作“beh” 【词源】高一时，钟zj同学在周日晚自修补先修课作业，在教室大喊一声：“be，什么是线性有关？” dismiss$^\star$ 【释义】拒绝，抛弃，绝交，用于开玩笑语气 【例句】她已经被我dismiss 保守估计98分$^\dagger$ 【释义】表示自己在虚张声势 【词源】rui同学在某场历史考试结束之后大喊大叫：“保守估计98分”。 【变体】保守估计 【例句】今天保守估计基金能挣500 刺痛 【释义】表示一些事情使心情受到负面影响 【例句】比如说提起我的高数失败，就是一种刺痛。 “董”相关$^\dagger$ 【释义】董jq老师衍生出来的一系列词语，例如“不董装董”、“董装不董” 【词源】高一时董jq老师神出鬼没。有时有人进班级或在后门窥视，让人疑心是董老师，因此称其“不董装董”，自此衍生出来一系列词语 胡椒$^\dagger$ 【释义】匿名的显得很牛的人 【词源】春考之后，英语大佬曹yw同学在英语群里以胡椒的匿名id问老师能不能不做英语作业了。 基里巴斯$^\dagger$ 【释义】时空错乱，倒时差 【词源】Cosmo同学在数学考前复习语文，语文考前复习数学，时空错乱，像是生活在横跨日界线的基里巴斯一样 看看你的$^\star$ 【释义】看看对方的情况 【例句】[发送了一张图片，是一个量表]看看你的！ 口区$^\dagger$ 【释义】表示恶心 【词源】“呕”这个字拆开来，来源于孙m同学，rui同学最爱用，后来风靡开来了 【变体】呕（先有的“口区”，再有的“呕”） 蓝奶酪${^\dagger} {^\ddagger}$ 【释义】味道恶臭的物品。 【词源】来自高二地理课张yt发现所坐座位有恶臭，经沈ty研究恶臭来源为龚zr的自制酸奶，故用同为恶臭奶制品的蓝奶酪代指。 某巨$^\dagger$ 【释义】对厉害的人的尊称 【例词】郭巨 谬误 【释义】表示用轻松的语气对某人的批评，常与完全连用 【例句】我又发现了一些小谬误。 你好$^\star$ 【释义】表示接下来说的内容将以一种戏剧化或者夸张化的语气，常与“同学”、“请”连用 【例句】你好，请飞来北京看。 脑控 【释义】嘲讽对方做了一些比较荒谬的事情 【词源】原出处已散逸，或许来源于廖凯原的《轩辕反熵运行体系》，或许来源于网上关于脑控的发笑阴谋论 脑死亡$^\star$ 【释义】做了一些荒谬或者略微有点愚蠢、没有逻辑的事情，可以形容自己或者别人，贬义。常与热狗连用。 【词源】来源于《破道计划》（郭xj著）“所有人眼前一黑，全部倒下，他们的大脑承载了本不该承载的东西，全部陷入了脑死亡。” 【变体】nsw、脑死亡一次、nsw吧、脑死、眼前一黑，陷入脑死亡 【例句】我今天早上11:15起床已经nsw！ Odeur$^\dagger$ 【释义】匿名者 【词源】网课期间，沈ty同学以Odeur的化名出没于各个腾讯会议会议室 然而 【释义】表示转折 【例句】然而：我可悲。 热狗$^\star$ 【释义】表示做事不太聪明又有点可爱发笑，可作为名词、形容词、副词、语气词使用 【词源】高一义卖高sm同学提议可以卖热狗，后虽热狗因卫生原因被否，但是高sm同学读“热狗”的口音流传了下来 【变体】热狗人，🌭，🌭吧，小热狗以及众多表情包的形式 【例句】这也是为什么有小热狗喜欢iPad mini。 请$^\star$ 【释义】发语词，表示接下来说的内容将以一种戏剧化或者夸张化的语气，有时用来表达比较轻松语气的请教，常与同学、你好连用 【例句】请你加速！ 事实上 【释义】in fact，也不知为何常被拿来发语，语言非常欧化呐 【例句】事实上我后天早上说不定也要从交大出发。 同学$^\star$ 【释义】表示接下来说的内容将以一种戏剧化或者夸张化的语气，常与请、你好连用、注意 【例句】同学，你有些发笑。 tsosnymud$^\dagger$ 【释义】“操死你妈的”用外国人口音读出来 【词源】来源于章jh同学对“操你妈的”进行加强，并且用更顺口的语气说出来。 完全 【释义】表示夸张化的否定 【例句】完全错误！ 显然$^\star$ 【释义】表示夸张化的语气 【例句】我显然追求最佳显示效果。 一次$^\star$ 【释义】用于自嘲，常与发笑、热狗连用 【例句】🌭一次 智慧 【释义】常用于自夸，其否定形式常常表示轻松语气的批评 【例句】我是智慧的。 【例句】大不智慧！ 中情局$^\dagger$ 【释义】偷看英语默写答案 【词源】高一时钟zj同学作为英语课代表，是及时雨中的普罗米修斯，他从老师或者隔壁同学那里盗来答案，史称中情局。 注意$^\star$ 【释义】表示提醒对方说错话或者做事荒谬，常与“智力”连用 【例句】注意！到虹桥只需1h5min。
