items.content_en: The fxlego Compendium v1.0 The reason I wrote this dictionary of Shangzhong Speak was on a whim. Honestly, it's hard to say what the exact definition of "Shangzhong Speak" is here. It's called Shangzhong Speak, but it's mainly used by students in the Master Class — though a good number of students from other classes use it too. It's called Shangzhong Speak, but it's mainly the boys in the Master Class using it; the girls use some of these expressions as well, but not much. For simplicity, let's just call it Shangzhong Speak. The main reason for writing this was just for fun, to look back on some amusing anecdotes that have become lore. Don't take it seriously. To put it in Shangzhong Speak, this thing is actually very 🌭, ydfx. When compiling this, Brother Mao and fellow student Nababa helped me a lot. They were my first readers, helped me expand several entries, and recalled interesting stories. Nababa also helped me write some entries I wasn't very familiar with. Thanks to fellow student zjh, who added a large number of entries on the eve of publication. Thanks also to myj and sty, from whom I learned about even more entries I didn't know and their etymological origins. The example sentences below come from my chat records with classmates. Thank you for those chat records! This inevitably reflects my own blind spots and limitations. Feel free to expand and revise the entries! \dagger denotes outdated or rarely used entries, \ddagger denotes entries with strongly offensive meanings or origins, \star denotes commonly used entries Pinyin Abbreviation Table Abbreviation Chinese Variant buc Not bad bc (Not bad) bd Don't understand bzd Don't know ee Uh-uh fx Laughing fxfx (Laughing laughing) ydfx (Kind of laughing) hb Alright hd Okay hod (Hou de (variant of hao de)) hyys Very interesting ii Hey hey jwyj After my research juj Refuse kb Pathetic kbkb (Pathetic pathetic) ydkb (Kind of pathetic) kknd Let's see yours kyd That works kyx Take a look nsw Brain dead nk Mind control / Nanjing nkr Mind control person mxd Didn't expect qnjs Please introduce sd Yes bsd (Not really) szyd That's right tina Oh my god tn (Oh my god) ylrc So that's how it is xm Jealous zssm What is this 2. Fake Classical Chinese Pronoun + 母 (Mother) ^\star 【Definition】 xx's mother 【Variant】 Your mother, my mother 【Example】 Alright, how old is your mother this year? Degree word + 佳**^\star** 【Definition】 Used for evaluating things; instead of saying "good" or "bad," one says "佳" (excellent/superior) 【Variant】 Not excellent, extremely excellent, most excellent, fairly excellent 【Example】 Oh dear, the weather outside is indeed not excellent. 何处 【Definition】 Where (formal/classical) 【Example】 Where exactly we'll meet then can be discussed further. 亦**^\star** 【Definition】 Also (formal/classical) 【Example】 But they also use Apple. 可/不可**^\star** 【Definition】 Can / cannot 【Example】 kb (kind of pathetic), if there's PE class, then it cannot be. 3. Big Words for Small Things 部署 (Deploy) 【Definition】 To plan, prepare, and implement 【Example】 Oh, after you wake up tomorrow morning, deploy the payment collection. 【Example】 And my roommate is still deploying the plane tickets for the Japan trip today. 会面**^\star** 【Definition】 To meet up 【Example】 Where exactly we'll meet then can be discussed further. 昏聩 (Senile / Befuddled) 【Definition】 To be out of one's mind, doing absurd or foolish things 【Example】 Shufen was quite befuddled this morning. 拒绝**^\star** 【Definition】 Interjection used to express refusal, but not in a formal tone — rather a slightly euphemistic way of declining. Often used with the WeChat [fist] emoji 【Example】 Refuse to go to Guoquan Road. 通过**^\star** 【Definition】 To express approval 【Synonym】 Support 【Example】 Alright alright, approved, accepted. 污名化 (Stigmatize) 【Definition】 Used to reject the other party's criticism of oneself, often used together with "refuse" and "forbid." Sometimes also used to acknowledge that one's own criticism was inappropriate 【Etymology】 A common expression of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs 【Example】 Okay, you're right, stigmatizing once. 研究**^\star** 【Definition】 To look into something 【Variant】 Research it, after my research 【Example】 So let me research whether you have any interest in getting into this. 支持**^\star** 【Definition】 To express approval 【Synonym】 Approve 【Example】 Firmly supported. 4. Math-Related 笛卡尔的茅厕**^\dagger** 【Definition】 Analytic geometry 【Etymology】 Descartes is the founder of analytic geometry. In classmate Guo fj's pure geometry competition "Dà Sīmǎ Cup" call-to-arms, it was mentioned: "Descartes' toilet attracted many headless flies." 号角已经吹响**^\dagger** 【Definition】 To begin 【Etymology】 Also from the "Dà Sīmǎ Cup" call-to-arms: "The horn of the Dà Sīmǎ Cup has sounded." 无头苍蝇**^\dagger** 【Definition】 People who act brainlessly 【Etymology】 Also from in classmate Guo fj's pure geometry competition "Dà Sīmǎ Cup" call-to-arms, where it was mentioned: "Descartes' toilet attracted many headless flies." 5. Teacher Impressions 像像我和你讲/说 【Definition】 Opening phrase used jokingly to inform or advise the other person 【Etymology】 Teacher Wu jy sometimes stutters. Her catchphrase was originally "像我和你讲" (Like, let me tell you), but due to her stutter it became "像像我和你讲" (Like like let me tell you) you cross the line**^\dagger** 【Definition】 You crossed the line 【Etymology】 From a flyer assigned by Teacher Li p. A group used advanced PS skills to edit in Jiege helping classmates buy things and solve housing problems, which was eventually discovered and criticized as crossing the line. whip**^\dagger** 【Definition】 To whip 【Etymology】 Teacher Li p, to explain the meaning of the word "whip," demonstrated a whip on classmate Xiao f in the classroom. 6. Miscellaneous be**^\star** 【Definition】 A Shanghai dialect interjection pronounced "be," often used with "weisa." Can also be written as "beh" 【Etymology】 In sophomore year (wait, freshman year?), classmate Zhong zj was doing makeup work for the pro-seminar during Sunday evening self-study, and shouted in the classroom: "Be, what is linear dependence?" 保守估计98分**^\dagger** 【Definition】 Used to express bravado/boasting 【Etymology】 Classmate rui shouted loudly after a physics exam: "Conservatively estimated at 98 points." 刺痛 (Sting) 【Definition】 Used to express that certain things negatively affect one's mood 【Example】 For instance, bringing up my failure in advanced mathematics is a sting. tsosnymud**^\dagger** 【Definition】 "操死你妈的" (f*ck your mother) pronounced with a foreign accent 【Etymology】 Originated from classmate Zhang jh, who intensified "操你妈的" (f*ck your mother) and said it in a smoother tone. "董"-Related**^\dagger** 【Definition】 A series of words derived from Teacher Dong jq, such as "不董装董" (not understanding but pretending to understand) and "董装不董" (understanding but pretending not to understand) 【Etymology】 In freshman year, Teacher Dong jq would appear and disappear unpredictably. Sometimes people would enter the classroom or peek through the back door, making others suspect it was Teacher Dong. This was called "不董装董" (not Dong but pretending to be Dong), and from this a series of words developed. 胡椒 (Pepper)^\dagger 【Definition】 An anonymous person who seems very impressive 【Etymology】 After the spring exam, English ace Cao yw asked the teacher in the English group chat using the anonymous ID "Pepper" whether he could skip English homework. 基里巴斯 (Kiribati)^\dagger 【Definition】 Temporal confusion, jet lag 【Etymology】 Classmate Cosmo studied Chinese before the math exam and math before the Chinese exam — time and space utterly scrambled, as if living in Kiribati, which straddles the International Date Line. 看看你的**^\star** 【Definition】 Let's see what your situation is 【Example】 [Sent an image, a scoring scale] Let's see yours! 口区**^\dagger** 【Definition】 Expressing disgust/nausea 【Etymology】 The character "呕" (vomit) split into its two components 「口」 and 「区」. Originated from classmate Sun m; classmate rui loved it the most, and it later caught on widely 【Variant】 呕 (the original "口区" came first, then "呕" followed) 蓝奶酪 (Blue Cheese)^\star 【Definition】 An item that smells foul 【Etymology】 From a sophomore year geography class where Zhang yt discovered a foul smell at the seat they were sitting in. Through Shen ty's investigation, the source was determined to be Gong zr's homemade yogurt. Hence, blue cheese — a similarly foul-smelling dairy product — was used as a substitute reference. 某巨**^\dagger** 【Definition】 A respectful title for very capable people 【Example word】 Guo-giant (Guo ju) 谬误 (Fallacy) 【Definition】 Used to criticize someone in a lighthearted tone, often used with "完全" (completely) 【Example】 I've discovered some little fallacies again. 你好 (Hello) 【Definition】 Indicates that what follows will be said in a dramatic or exaggerated tone, often used with "同学" (classmate) or "请" (please) 【Example】 Hello, please fly over to Beijing to see this. 脑控 (Mind control) 【Definition】 Used to mock someone for doing something quite absurd 【Etymology】 The original origin has been lost; perhaps from Liao Kaiyuan's "Xuanyuan Anti-Entropy Operational System," or perhaps from online conspiracy theories about mind control that are laughable. 脑死亡**^\star** 【Definition】 Doing something absurd, slightly foolish, or illogical — can be used to describe oneself or others. Derogatory. Often used with "hot dog." 【Etymology】 From "Project Breakthe Way" (authored by Guo xj): "Everyone's vision went black, and they all collapsed. Their brains had borne things they shouldn't have borne, and all fell into brain death." 【Variant】 nsw, brain death once, nsw ba, brain death, vision blackened, falling into brain death 【Example】 Waking up at 11:15 this morning is already nsw! Odeur**^\dagger** 【Definition】 An anonymous person 【Etymology】 During online classes, classmate Shen ty appeared in various Tencent Meeting rooms under the alias Odeur. 然而 (However) 【Definition】 Expresses contrast / transition 【Example】 However: I am pathetic. 热狗 (Hot dog)^\star 【Definition】 Expresses doing something not too smart yet rather endearing and laughable. Can be used as a noun, adjective, adverb, or interjection 【Etymology】 In a freshman year charity sale, classmate Gao sm proposed selling hot dogs. Although the hot dog idea was later rejected for hygiene reasons, Gao sm's way of pronouncing "热狗" (hot dog) stuck around 【Variant】 Hot dog person, 🌭, 🌭 ba, little hot dog, and many emoji forms 【Example】 This is also why a little hot dog likes the iPad mini. 请 (Please) 【Definition】 Opening phrase indicating that what follows will be said in a dramatic or exaggerated tone. Sometimes used for lightly-toned requests for advice. Often used with "classmate" and "hello" 【Example】 Please accelerate! 事实上 (In fact) 【Definition】 in fact — don't know why it's often used as an opening phrase anyway, the language is very Europeanized 【Example】 In fact, I might also be setting off from Jiaotong University the day after tomorrow morning. 同学 (Classmate) 【Definition】 Indicates that what follows will be said in a dramatic or exaggerated tone. Often used with "please" and "hello," and can also be used for "attention" 【Example】 Classmate, you're a little laughable. 完全 (Completely) 【Definition】 Used for exaggerated negation 【Example】 Completely wrong! 显然 (Obviously) 【Definition】 Used for an exaggerated tone 【Example】 I obviously pursue the best display effect. 一次 (Once) 【Definition】 Used for self-deprecation, often used with "laughing" and "hot dog" 【Example】 🌭 once 智慧 (Wisdom) 【Definition】 Often used for self-praise. Its negative form often expresses a lighthearted criticism 【Example】 I am full of wisdom. 【Example】 Greatly unwise! 中情局**^\dagger** 【Definition】 Sneaking a look at English dictation answers 【Etymology】 In freshman year, classmate Zhong zj served as the English class representative, a "Prometheus" among the "Timely Rain" — he stole answers from the teacher or neighboring classmates, earning the nickname "CIA." 注意**^\star** 【Definition】 Indicates calling out the other party for misspeaking or doing something absurd. Often used with "智力" (intellect) 【Example】 Attention! It only takes 1h5min to get to Hongqiao.

items.title: 9 3/4车站和驯龙高手
items.title_en: Platform 9¾ and How to Train Your Dragon
items.content: 9 3/4车站和驯龙高手 今天由于一些机缘巧合，在交大玉兰苑二楼体验到了Vision Pro，随便写一点感受， 戴上Vision Pro的其实有点麻烦的，有点笨重，我用的是单环的绑带，要束得比较紧。耳朵也一下子不知道是要盖在绑带下面还是不要盖在绑带下面。鼻子下面是会有一点点漏光的，没有那么贴合，佩戴的过程中，那块贴面的磁吸零件也经常松动（可能因为那块贴面的零件并不是量身定做的吧？）带上Vision Pro，我的第一感觉是与带着眼镜的观感无异。再定睛一看，会感觉有点“花”，怀疑是被各种人戴了之后摄像头上有点油渍没有擦掉吧（这其实和普通的眼镜也是一个道理）。再仔细体验，觉得确实暗部会比实际的亮度更低一些，细节不太清楚，有点糊作一团（这也可能是我加入的镜片和我实际的度数不太一致的缘故）。但是即使有这么多问题，戴上去的感觉还是震撼的，身临其境的感觉会让你忘记以上的缺点。甚至之前被诟病的“视角小”的问题我觉得也没有那么严重，因为本来视线的边缘就是模糊的，问题不是很大。让我感到有点吃力的是Vision Pro的重量。这次因为是体验，所以没有用双环的绑带，脖子感觉快要断掉了。我的面部确实也压得有点难受。而且眼睛离屏幕这么近，又要用视线来控制焦点，眼睛也是有点累的。 但是不得不说，VisionOS已经打磨得比较好了。记得《乔布斯传》中有一位苹果高管对于iPad的描述。ta在那里使用iPad，旁边一个素不相识的小孩看到了也很感兴趣，ta于是把iPad借给了那个小孩，那个小孩拿到iPad，不需要任何的使用手册，就很轻易地上手了iPad。我认为Vision Pro也是类似的体验，ta的交互中能够找到来自iPhone的Home键、手势操作的影子，用户完全不会有面对一个界面不知所措的感觉。符合直觉的设计是好设计。 体验了几个App。一个是看那个机械零件。那位引导我的店员说其实可以走进这个零件看内部构造，但是我不敢，我觉得会一头撞进去。真的有一种9 3/4车站的感觉。那个零件是可以用手拆开的，让我感到惊讶的是甚至可以用手来将它翻转。认为这个手部识别应该会比较难，这确实是比较让我惊喜的一点。也体验了那个知名的与恐龙面对面的App。恐龙走出屏幕的时候，我真的很害怕，竟然一下子蹲了下来。我小心翼翼地想像驯龙高手里面的Hiccup用手去摸龙的额头，但是它咬了我一下，我害怕得把手缩了回去。太真了。还体验了iMAX看电影，看了几段试看片段。哇那个真的是太爽了，真的想在电影院一样。但是我试图像宣传片里的一样把银幕放到湖的上面，我自己好坐在湖边看，但是来不及研究出应该怎么操作。不过我还是体验了几个环境的场景。看了雪山、沙漠、湖边、月球。真的非常震撼。最后体验的app是淘宝。没想到国内厂商已经这么快就适配了Vision Pro。打开淘宝，说实话也都是几个我比较熟悉的商品：大疆mini 4，索尼A7C2等等（怀疑被算法了，这不是我一直念叨想要的嘛）点进去，是可以把立体的商品拿出来看的。感觉这个真的会重塑线上购物的体验。 感谢trt告知了我这个活动，真的很难得。这应该是那一个幻想中的美好未来的一部分吧？不知这个产业以后会变成什么样。
items.content_en: Platform 9¾ and How to Train Your Dragon Today, due to a series of coincidences, I got to try the Vision Pro at the second floor of Yulan Garden on Jiaotong University campus, and I’ll jot down a few thoughts. Putting on the Vision Pro is actually a bit of a hassle — it’s quite bulky. I used the single-strap version, which needs to be tightened quite firmly. I also wasn’t sure whether my ears should be covered by the strap or not. There’s a little light leakage under the nose since it doesn’t fit perfectly, and the magnetic face-contact part often loosens during wear (maybe because this face-contact piece isn’t custom-made for me?). My first impression of wearing the Vision Pro was that it felt no different from wearing regular glasses. But upon closer inspection, the image looked a bit blurry; I suspect there were oil stains on the cameras after being used by many people (this is similar to what happens with ordinary glasses). After further use, I noticed that the dark areas appeared dimmer than they actually are, and details weren’t very clear, looking rather blurry (this might also be because the lenses I added didn’t match my prescription exactly). But even with all these issues, the experience was still stunning — the sense of immersion made me forget about these flaws. I even found the previously criticized issue of a narrow field of view to be less severe, since the edges of our vision are naturally blurry anyway, so it wasn’t a big problem. What I found really taxing was the weight of the Vision Pro. Since this was just an experience session, I didn’t use the dual-strap version, and my neck felt like it was about to break. My face was also pressed uncomfortably. Plus, with my eyes so close to the screen and having to use my gaze to control focus, my eyes got tired too. But I have to say, VisionOS has been polished quite well. I remember a description of the iPad in Steve Jobs by an Apple executive: the person was using an iPad, and a stranger child nearby showed interest; so they lent the iPad to the child, who could easily figure out how to use it without any manual. I think the Vision Pro offers a similar experience — its interactions incorporate elements reminiscent of the iPhone’s Home button and gesture controls, so users won’t feel lost when facing the interface. Intuitive design is good design. I tried a few apps. One was an app showing a mechanical part. The staff member guiding me said I could walk inside the part to see its internal structure, but I didn’t dare — I thought I’d bump my head into it. It truly felt like Platform 9¾! The part could be disassembled by hand, and to my surprise, I could even flip it with my hands. I thought hand recognition would be quite difficult, so this was a pleasant surprise. I also tried the popular app where you face a dinosaur. When the dinosaur stepped out of the screen, I was really scared and immediately crouched down. I carefully tried to mimic Hiccup from How to Train Your Dragon and touch the dragon’s forehead, but it bit me, so I quickly pulled my hand back — it was so realistic! I also tried watching a movie on iMAX, viewing a few preview clips. Wow, it was amazing — it felt just like being in a cinema. I tried to follow the promo video and place the screen over a lake so I could sit by the lake and watch, but I didn’t have time to figure out how to do it. I also experienced several environment scenes: snowy mountains, deserts, lakesides, and the moon. They were truly breathtaking. The last app I tried was Taobao. I didn’t expect domestic developers to adapt for the Vision Pro so quickly. When I opened Taobao, I saw mostly products I was familiar with: DJI Mini 4, Sony A7C2, etc. (I suspect the algorithm recommended them since these are the ones I’ve been asking for!). When I clicked on a product, I could view its 3D model. I think this will truly revolutionize the online shopping experience. Thanks to trt for telling me about this event — it was really rare. Is this part of that wonderful future we once imagined? I wonder what the industry will look like in the future.

items.title: Ars Longa, Vita brevis
items.content: Ars Longa, Vita brevis 现在已经很晚了，刚刚和一位朋友打了电话煲了电话粥，所以现在事实上已经是6月5日1:00多了，即使如此，我还是觉得有必要趁我的感受没有消失前写下我看完《坂本龙一：杰作》之后的感受。 我是什么时候知道坂本龙一的呢？高三的时候，我做作业喜欢听钢琴曲。我的钢琴曲都选自Apple music每周更新的钢琴休憩小站的歌单，其中就有坂本龙一的《OPUS》和《energy flow》。OPUS是我在这个歌单中挑出来单曲循环过的音乐之一，我能听出它的非同寻常。“坂本龙一”这个日本名字就进入了我的记忆。又是“龙”，又是“一”的，听上去就是一个大师嘛。我后来才知道，他确实是一位大师。 后来，我发现坂本龙一确实久负盛名。在一些视频中，我了解到了他的名作《Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence》。我很庆幸我对于美是有敏锐的感受的，我看一个介绍他的视频中的很多音乐中，给我留下最深印象的就是《Merry Christmas， Mr Lawrence》。但是我真正了解他反而是在他去世前不久。2021，2022年的时候，我在B站上找过大量有关于他的视频进行了解，看了纪录片《坂本龙一：终曲》，我发现他不是那种老态龙钟的保守的音乐大师，而是颇为先锋。不仅在年轻的时候，他在YMO他做过很多尝试，甚至到他步入中老年之后，也试着去创新，去写出《async》这样的先锋作品，这让我对他既是愈发感兴趣，又是愈发敬佩。我也尝试去听他的音乐，有些先锋音乐、实验音乐不适合作为常听的娱乐性的或者说仅仅是让我专注下来的bgm，只适合作为一种新奇的体验，但从中我能够感到坂本龙一对于音乐本质的独到理解与不断的探索。 只是我开始了解他没多久，他就离世了。 《坂本龙一：杰作》是他留给我们最后的礼物。 在5/31，我发现《坂本龙一：杰作》上院线了。我认为我一定要去看，而且我也认为我应该一个人去看。我谁都没有约。 是6月4日20:00-21:43的票。我很担心自己能不能看完的，因为担心自己没有这个耐心，但是随着乐音渐强，我代入了这种情绪化的氛围，我就知道自己一定能听下去，我本来以为或许自己会包场，因为感觉这种形式能接受的人很少吧？但是实际上没有包场，全场一共9位观众。坐在我前面的我能看到的4位观众中，1位看微信看得睡着了，1位在看微信，2位在刷短视频。手机的屏幕很亮很刺眼，我尽量压低身子，希望他们的座位挡住屏幕的光。不知道他们有没有享受这一段旅程。电影院运作的噪音很大，这对于这样一场音乐会而言是很严重的影响，但无妨。 前几周刚好连续看了坂本龙一的两本自传《我还能看到几次满月升起》和《音乐即自由》，同时我也不是什么专业的音乐人，所以我看这部作品的时候，我在想的是，坂本龙一在演奏时会想什么呢？镜头一直给坂本龙一的脸特写，我可以看到他最细微的表情，我尽力地去揣度他的想法。 《BB（Bernardo Bertoilucci）》是他这次演奏会的第二首音乐。我第一次知道，原来BB指的是Bernardo Bertoilucci。贝托鲁奇是坂本龙一敬爱的前辈，为他的电影配乐，尽管有许多起伏与碰撞，但能为自己心目中的大师的作品配乐，坂本龙一想必是非常幸福的。而看到两位大师合作，那种惺惺相惜，是如此让人动容。整个音乐会有两首音乐都是贝托鲁奇的电影配乐。一首是《The Last Emperor》，一首是《The Sheltering Sky》。《The Last Emperor》是坂本龙一是贝托鲁奇的第一次合作，而《The Sheltering Sky》的合作或许是对于坂本龙一影响最大的一次。事实上“我还能看到几次满月升起”就摘自《遮蔽的天空》，这句话坂本龙一直到晚年也一直在回味，甚至喃喃自语。已经30年了。 我也是第一次知道“Andata”的中文是的“离去”。我对于《Andata》的旋律相对而言较为熟悉，但知道了它的含义之后，又对它的那种空落感的认识更加具象化。这次是纯钢琴演奏，因此没有原曲中应该是电子合成音的那一部分。但却是觉得那部分电子合成音或许更有那种空落之感。坂本龙一青年时自杀的女友离去了、他未曾见到最后一面的父亲离去了、带他进入电影配乐的大岛渚离去了、他心目中的大师贝托鲁奇离去了、他的挚友大卫·鲍伊离去了、YMO的高桥幸宏也先他一步离去了，现在他自己也要离去了。 再下一首让我印象深刻的音乐就是《Aubade2020》（《晨曲2020》）。我认为这或许是坂本龙一的《朝花夕拾》？这或许是整场音乐会最轻快的的旋律了，其中的欢乐莫不是他幼时特殊幼儿园中学钢琴的经历，莫不是他第一次作出《小白兔之歌》的感受？这种快乐是轻快的。我认为这其实与后面一首《Ichimei-Small happiness》（《一命：渺小的幸福》）相对照。这首音乐不快乐，有种物哀之感，但很幸福，应该是他此刻的感受吧？鲜花在谢的时候是幸福的，红叶在飘落的时候是幸福的，最终土地上还会长出新的苗来。 《Tong Poo》(《东风》)是坂本龙一年轻时的名作，我想他这应该是在回想YMO时期，那段他探索民族音乐的时期吧？在YMO的经历，让坂本龙一走向了国际化。最后因为与细野晴臣和高桥幸宏观念不合最终解散。解散之后YMO有两次重聚，一次是商业性的，几个人还处于矛盾的状态，不太愉快，但是第二次是自发的，年岁的增长让三位也更加平和包容，时隔多年为YMO画上了一个完美的句号。 《20180219（w/prepared piano》（《预制钢琴》）前，坂本龙一手动改装琴弦，赋予了钢琴特殊的音色。这种音色让我回想起坂本龙一在福岛海啸之后去拜访福岛，找到的那架破烂钢琴的音色，或许也正是从中获得灵感吧？wrepared指的应当也是wreck- prepared吧？感觉这种改装钢琴的手法非常实验性，但是做出来的效果却出人意料的动听和谐。 倒数第二首诗另外一首电影配乐《Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence》。这首音乐在他的音乐生涯中也有这举足轻重的地位。他因为这首音乐，去了奥斯卡现场，见到了贝托鲁奇，才有了后面的电影配乐的那一半故事。但是坂本龙一对于这首音乐的态度很矛盾，也是到了晚年才释怀。他起先一直不愿意谈这首音乐，因为厌倦这首音乐成为他的公众形象（其实这也有点叛逆），但他去听别人的音乐会，理解了听不到自己想听的音乐的难受，因此开始不忌讳在自己的音乐会上面演奏这首音乐，也算是最终和解吧。我事先没见过演奏单，也一直在想坂本龙一是否会把这首音乐放进他留下来的最后的礼物呢？我一直等，听到了《The Last Emperor》中《Where is Armo》的开头差点以为是《Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence》。我听到最后都已经觉得，或许这最后一次他想为了自己演奏，不弹这首了吧，没想到这一首音乐的旋律最终还是浮现了出来，他想必是彻底和解了，他最后一次为世界弹了一遍《圣诞快乐，劳伦斯先生》。他会不会想起大卫·鲍伊，想起在奥斯卡遇到贝托鲁奇，想起北野武油腻但纯真的脸。这是他唯一一首微笑着演奏的音乐。 最后一首音乐是《OPUS》，这是我第一次知道坂本龙一这个名字的媒介，却也是坂本龙一的落幕。我事先是知道这首音乐 是最后一首音乐，但是没想到是以一种如此伤感的形式：弹着弹着，脚步声响起，琴声依旧，琴键上的手消失了，琴键却兀自地弹着。字幕提醒着我们“斯人已逝，乐音不止”。 全片的最后一幕是Ars Longa, Vita brevis（艺术千秋，人生朝露），这句话也在他的《你还能看到多少次满月升起》里出现过，这是坂本龙一的墓志铭，恰如其分。
items.content_en: Ars Longa, Vita brevis It's already very late now. I just had a long phone call with a friend, so in fact it’s already past 1:00 AM on June 5th. Even so, I feel it’s necessary to write down my thoughts after watching Ryuichi Sakamoto: Coda before my feelings fade away. When did I first hear of Ryuichi Sakamoto? In my senior year of high school, I liked listening to piano pieces while doing homework. All my piano tracks came from the weekly updated Piano Lounge playlist on Apple Music, which included Sakamoto’s OPUS and energy flow. OPUS was one of the tracks I looped repeatedly from that playlist; I could tell it was extraordinary. The Japanese name “Sakamoto Ryuichi” thus entered my memory. With “Ryu” (dragon) and “Ichi” (one) in it, it sounded like the name of a master. I later learned that he indeed was a master. Later, I discovered that Ryuichi Sakamoto was truly renowned. Through some videos, I learned about his famous work Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence. I’m glad I have a keen sense of beauty: among the many pieces of music in a video introducing him, the one that left the deepest impression on me was Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence. But I really got to know him only shortly before his death. In 2021 and 2022, I searched Bilibili for numerous videos about him and watched the documentary Ryuichi Sakamoto: Coda. I found he wasn’t a conservative, aged music master, but rather quite avant-garde. Not only did he make many experiments in YMO during his youth, but even in his middle and old age, he tried to innovate and create avant-garde works like async. This made me increasingly interested in and admiring of him. I also tried listening to his music; some avant-garde and experimental pieces aren’t suitable as regular entertainment or background music to help me focus—they’re only fit for a novel experience. Yet through them, I could sense Sakamoto’s unique understanding of the essence of music and his continuous exploration. But not long after I started learning about him, he passed away. Ryuichi Sakamoto: Coda is the last gift he left for us. On May 31st, I found out that Ryuichi Sakamoto: Coda had been released in theaters. I felt I absolutely had to watch it, and I also thought I should go alone. I didn’t make any plans with anyone. The ticket was for 8:00–9:43 PM on June 4th. I was worried I wouldn’t be able to finish watching it, as I doubted I had the patience. But as the music grew louder and I immersed myself in the emotional atmosphere, I knew I would definitely keep listening. I originally thought I might have the whole theater to myself, as I assumed few people would appreciate this format. But in reality, there were 9 audience members in total. Among the 4 people I could see sitting in front of me, 1 fell asleep while using WeChat, 1 was using WeChat, and 2 were scrolling through short videos. The screens of their phones were very bright and glaring; I tried to lower my body, hoping their seats would block the light from the screens. I wonder if they enjoyed this journey. The noise from the cinema’s operation was quite loud, which was a serious disruption to such a concert, but it didn’t matter. A few weeks prior, I had read Sakamoto’s two autobiographies, How Many More Full Moons Can I See? and Music Is Freedom, back-to-back. Since I’m not a professional musician, when watching this film, I wondered what Sakamoto was thinking while playing. The camera kept focusing on his face, allowing me to see his subtlest expressions; I tried my best to guess his thoughts. BB (Bernardo Bertolucci) was the second piece performed at this concert. I learned for the first time that BB stood for Bernardo Bertolucci. Bertolucci was a senior Sakamoto admired greatly; Sakamoto composed music for his films. Despite many ups and downs and conflicts, being able to compose for the works of a master he looked up to must have made Sakamoto very happy. Seeing the collaboration between the two masters was truly touching. Two pieces at the concert were film scores by Bertolucci: The Last Emperor and The Sheltering Sky. The Last Emperor was Sakamoto’s first collaboration with Bertolucci, and the collaboration on The Sheltering Sky perhaps had the greatest influence on Sakamoto. In fact, the phrase “How many more full moons can I see?” is taken from The Sheltering Sky; Sakamoto reminisced about it and murmured it to himself even in his later years. It had been 30 years already. I also learned for the first time that the Chinese translation of “Andata” is “departure”. I was relatively familiar with the melody of Andata, but after learning its meaning, my understanding of its sense of emptiness became more concrete. This time it was a pure piano performance, so the part that should be electronic synthesizer sounds in the original version was absent. Yet I felt those electronic synthesizer parts might have conveyed an even stronger sense of emptiness. Sakamoto’s girlfriend who committed suicide when he was young left him; his father, whom he never met in person, left him; Nagisa Oshima, who introduced him to film scoring, left him; his master Bertolucci left him; his close friend David Bowie left him; Haruomi Hosono of YMO also passed away before him, and now he himself was about to leave. The next piece that left a deep impression on me was Aubade 2020 (“Morning Song 2020”). I think this might be Sakamoto’s Reminiscences of the Past? This was perhaps the liveliest melody of the entire concert. The joy in it surely stemmed from his experience learning piano at a special kindergarten in childhood and the feeling of creating Song of the Little Rabbit for the first time. This joy was light-hearted. I think this actually contrasts with the next piece, Ichimei – Small Happiness. This piece isn’t joyful; it has a sense of mono no aware, but it’s happy—this must be how he felt at that moment. Flowers are happy when they wither, autumn leaves are happy when they fall, and new sprouts will eventually grow from the soil. Tong Poo (“East Wind”) is a famous work from Sakamoto’s youth. I think he was recalling his YMO period, when he explored ethnic music. His experience in YMO helped Sakamoto go global. Eventually, the group disbanded due to disagreements with Haruomi Hosono and Ryuichi Sakamoto over creative concepts. After the disbandment, YMO reunited twice: the first time was commercial, and the members were still at odds, making it an unpleasant experience; the second reunion was spontaneous, and as they grew older, the three of them became more peaceful and inclusive, drawing a perfect conclusion to YMO after many years. Before performing 20180219 (w/prepared piano), Sakamoto manually modified the piano strings to give the instrument a special timbre. This timbre reminded me of the sound of the broken piano Sakamoto found when he visited Fukushima after the tsunami; perhaps he drew inspiration from it? “Prepared” here likely refers to “wreck-prepared”. I found this method of modifying the piano very experimental, but the resulting sound was surprisingly pleasant and harmonious. The penultimate piece was another film score, Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence. This piece holds a pivotal place in his musical career. Thanks to this piece, he went to the Oscars, met Bertolucci, and thus began the second half of his film scoring story. However, Sakamoto had a contradictory attitude toward this piece and only let it go in his later years. He initially refused to talk about it, tired of it becoming his public image (which was also a bit rebellious). But when he attended other people’s concerts and understood how painful it was to not hear the music one wanted to hear, he stopped hesitating to perform this piece at his own concerts—this was a final reconciliation. I hadn’t seen the program beforehand and kept wondering if Sakamoto would include this piece in his last gift to us. I waited, and when I heard the opening of “Where is Armo” from The Last Emperor, I almost thought it was Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence. By the end, I even thought he might choose to play for himself this time and skip this piece. Unexpectedly, the melody of this piece finally emerged; he must have fully reconciled with it. He played Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence for the world one last time. Did he recall David Bowie, his meeting with Bertolucci at the Oscars, or the greasy yet innocent face of Takeshi Kitano? This was the only piece he played with a smile. The last piece was OPUS—the medium through which I first learned Sakamoto’s name, and also Sakamoto’s finale. I knew beforehand that this was the last piece, but I didn’t expect it to be in such a sad form: as he played, footsteps sounded, the music continued, the hand on the keys disappeared, but the keys kept playing on their own. The subtitles reminded us, “Though the man is gone, the music remains.” The final scene of the film is Ars Longa, Vita brevis (Art lasts forever, life is but a fleeting moment)—a phrase that also appears in his book How Many More Full Moons Can I See?. This is Sakamoto’s epitaph, and it fits perfectly.

items.title: Ride, ride through the day
items.content: Ride, ride through the day 我能接受的最快的还算能享受的速度是自行车的速度。 在读大学以前，我很少骑车。出行无非三种方式：步行、乘父母的车、乘公交。乘公交的时光是漫长的，总需要一样东西来分散注意力，打磨时光。对我而言，那常常是手中的Kindle和耳朵里的AirPods。公交车是颠簸的，有一股怪味，窗缝和座位底下总感觉很脏，车门打开时候嘎吱嘎吱的。地铁稍微稳一点，但是隆隆的运行声让我总要带上降噪耳机，即使我不想听音乐。在公交上，我能感受到阅读和欣赏音乐的快乐，但是我不享受这段单调、重复、死板的旅程。 乘父母的车比乘公交舒服一些。至少有一整面的窗户是留给我的，我可以看看路边的景色。可这景色往往是单调的——在这个车速限制的观察的宏观尺度上、在城市里，我看到的几乎只有千篇一律的楼和不断重复的路灯、路牌、和路上的标线。对我而言，享受的纯粹的车程可能只有那种空旷、笔直、怪石环绕的无人公路或是溪边的人小路。感觉山石和水流是少数不多在宏观的尺度之下还能欣赏的东西了。平时乘车唯一的享受之处在于与家人的聊天，但这也不属于旅途的享受的范畴了。 但是每次步行就很享受。步行足够慢，慢到我可以看清路途中的一切细节；步行足够随意，我想停便停、想快便快、想慢便慢；步行足够放松，我可以肆意挥霍自己的注意力；步行足够真实，我可以去触碰大地，听落叶的声音，嗅即将下雨的味道。步行是生活；步行是探索；步行是欣赏；步行是作诗。 高中毕业之后，第一个新的交通体验是亲自开车。我的母亲很惊讶我没有像刻板印象中的男孩一样喜欢车这类所谓“阳刚”的东西。我没有很喜欢开车的感觉。我认为开车的感觉甚至比乘车还糟糕。除了不能好好看看身边的景，甚至注意力都被分开了——“看”就几乎只够实现最功利的目的了。 第二个新的交通体验是自行车。我上大学前自行车骑得不多，高中毕业后用从自己成功从SHS骑共享单车骑40km回家的经历换来了一辆入门的山地车giant-atx720。大学这一个学期，我骑的里程可能比我人生的前18年加起来都要多。我很享受骑行。骑行其实和步行很像——过了两三天后也还记得很多那段路的细节。在闵行骑车时每次都是绿灯，出了闵行就一直等红灯。过了一座桥后远远看到一座寺庙的大雄宝殿，在地图上查看发现是法华禅寺。非机动车道上奔波的除了疾驶的外卖小哥还有从工具箱里掉了一只扳手出来的维修工人。电瓶车的侧面伸出一个毛茸茸的头和一条兴奋地晃着的小尾巴，在等红绿灯时，那只小狗跳下了车，车上的老爷爷和隔壁车的老奶奶告诉它还没到，回去，它就回去了。看到嘉定新城一片风景秀丽的河边步道，旁边是红色的黄色的树，那是在嘉定城市规划馆旁边。馆对面还有一家养乐多工厂，以前我的太外婆经常送给我养乐多，一板一板的。骑着骑着，耳机里随机到了Queen的《Bicycle Race》。在骑过苏州河的时候，那个地方离虹桥很近，看到了4，5架飞的很低的飞机，就直直地在头顶掠过，连航空公司的名字都能看到。有幸拍下了几张照片，再往前骑一点是一帮在等着看飞机降落的年轻人。 很喜欢这张 《中国东方航空》 但是我最近意识到骑行的享受较步行已经有所下降了。我是在一天晚上意识到这件事的。那天晚上图书馆闭馆，和一个偶然遇到的高中同学一起回去。她没找到共享单车，所以我们一同走回去。在教超旁边，我看到一颗树，那棵树很粗，看上去年龄比旁边的行道树大了不少。一般而言，人感知到一件事往往能够快速唤醒一个人沉睡的回忆的。对我而言，最灵敏的是嗅觉，但是嗅觉稍纵即逝，往往我还没有想起那一段回忆就消逝了，空留感受的余音和美丽的遗憾。但是视觉是真切的，那棵粗得不一般的树让我立刻想到了小学上学路上和祖父一同依据树干粗细“钦定”的树老大、老二、老三和老四。我骑行的时候从未注意过这棵树。 步行、骑行。对于很多人来说，通勤是种折磨。是啊，谁愿意一大早起来挤在狭小的车厢内呢？步行作为通勤的方式可能在现在已经不太实际了，但是骑行还是可以作为一种折中的办法吧？我不愿意每一段路程都要想办法消磨时间，我还是希望多几段可以享受的旅程的。
items.content_en: Ride, ride through the day The fastest speed I can accept and still enjoy is the speed of a bicycle. Before college, I rarely rode a bike. My travel options were limited to three: walking, taking my parents' car, or riding the bus. Bus rides are long, so I always needed something to distract me and pass the time. For me, that was often my Kindle in hand and AirPods in my ears. Buses are bumpy, have a strange smell, and the gaps in the windows and under the seats always feel dirty; the doors make a creaking sound when they open. The subway is a bit smoother, but its rumbling noise forces me to wear noise-canceling headphones even when I don’t want to listen to music. On the bus, I can enjoy the pleasure of reading and listening to music, but I don’t relish this monotonous, repetitive, and rigid journey. Taking my parents' car is more comfortable than taking the bus. At least I have an entire window to myself to admire the scenery along the road. But this scenery is often dull — at the macroscopic scale allowed by speed limits in the city, all I see are identical buildings, repeating streetlights, signs, and road markings. For me, the only truly enjoyable rides are on empty, straight country roads surrounded by strange rocks or narrow paths beside streams. It seems that mountains, rocks, and flowing water are among the few things still worth appreciating at a macroscopic level. The only enjoyable part of riding in a car is chatting with family, but that doesn’t count as part of the journey’s enjoyment. But I always enjoy walking. Walking is slow enough for me to notice every detail along the way; it’s flexible enough for me to stop when I want, go fast or slow as I please; it’s relaxing enough for me to freely allocate my attention; and it’s real enough for me to touch the ground, hear the sound of falling leaves, and smell the scent of impending rain. Walking is life; walking is exploration; walking is appreciation; walking is poetry. After graduating from high school, my first new transportation experience was driving a car myself. My mother was surprised that I didn’t like cars, those so-called “masculine” objects that boys in stereotypes are supposed to love. I don’t particularly enjoy driving; in fact, I find it even worse than being a passenger. Not only can’t I properly enjoy the scenery around me, but my attention is also distracted — “seeing” is reduced to fulfilling purely utilitarian purposes. My second new transportation experience was riding a bicycle. I didn’t ride a bike much before college. After graduating from high school, I earned an entry-level mountain bike, a Giant ATX720, by successfully riding a shared bike 40km home from SHS. This semester in college, the distance I’ve ridden may exceed the total I covered in the first 18 years of my life. I really enjoy cycling. Cycling is actually quite similar to walking — I still remember many details of a route days after riding it. When riding in Minhang, I always hit green lights; once I leave Minhang, I keep waiting for red lights. After crossing a bridge, I saw the main hall of a temple in the distance; checking on the map, I found it was Fahua Zen Temple. Besides delivery riders speeding by, the non-motorized vehicle lane also has repair workers who drop a wrench out of their toolboxes. A fluffy head and an excited wagging tail stick out from the side of an electric scooter; while waiting for the light to turn green, the puppy jumps off the scooter, and the old man on the scooter and the old lady in the next vehicle tell it to go back since it’s not time yet, and it obeys. I saw a scenic riverside path in Jiading New City, with red and yellow trees nearby; it’s next to the Jiading Urban Planning Museum. Across from the museum, there’s also a Yakult factory; my great-grandmother used to give me Yakult in packs. As I rode along, my earbuds randomly played Queen’s Bicycle Race. When crossing the Suzhou River, a place close to Hongqiao, I saw 4 or 5 planes flying very low overhead, so close that I could even read the airline name. I was lucky enough to take a few photos; a little further ahead, there was a group of young people waiting to watch the planes land. I really like this one. China Eastern Airlines However, I recently realized that the joy I get from cycling has declined compared to walking. I realized this one evening. That night, the library closed, and I went back with a high school classmate I ran into by chance. She couldn’t find a shared bike, so we walked back together. Next to the convenience store, I saw a tree — it was very thick and looked much older than the other street trees around it. Generally, perceiving something can quickly awaken dormant memories. For me, the most sensitive sense is smell, but it fades quickly; often, the memory disappears before I can recall it, leaving only a lingering feeling and a beautiful regret. But vision is concrete: that unusually thick tree immediately made me think of the “top four trees” I and my grandfather designated based on trunk thickness on my way to primary school. I never noticed this tree while cycling. Walking and cycling. For many people, commuting is a torment. Indeed, who wants to wake up early and squeeze into a cramped carriage? Walking may no longer be a practical commuting option today, but cycling could serve as a compromise. I don’t want to spend every journey trying to kill time; I still hope for more journeys I can truly enjoy.

items.title: 法大悲 repo
items.content: # 法大悲 repo 有幸抢到了法大悲的票 于是在12月15日的交大金课工程学导论课下课后翘了晚上18:30的数学分析习题课前去上海文化广场观看 乘地铁紫竹高新区-->上海南站-->陕西南路 坐一号线的时候还有一个地铁迷兴奋地跑过来拍照，说这部地铁是上海一号线第一辆列车 感觉很好运 因为好久没有听音乐剧了，打算在路上重听一下10周年版的大悲，然后发现自己的耳朵进化了，已经听得出AirPods 2无法承受这种宏大的交响乐了，在地铁上后悔没有把大馒头4带出来。 在上海南站换乘的时候听到《The Confrontation》已经听得头皮发麻了，非常期待！！ 从陕西南路出来发现是环贸iapm，高考后莫名其妙对这里非常熟，打卡圣诞Apple store 晚饭在一家深井陈记烤鹅吃了雪菜牛肉饭，一直很喜欢吃这道菜，很鲜。 没有给饭拍照（哎这次就是没想到应当多拍点照片）因为外面打光很好，想给自己拍张照 发现反光不够好 走到上海文化广场，路边的旗，， 进去了，人很多，见到一个女孩子拿着徕卡相机（不是镜头，是镜头+相机），感觉她很富有 看到上海电视台也在有那里采访，趁没有人偷偷拍了一张大海报（的一部分 买了一些纪念品：纪念册和CD 可以给大家看看纪念册里面，很精美！sukisuki 在进场的时候还偶遇xys小姐，小小震撼，，和她大眼瞪小眼 记得第一次看10周年的时候还有点无聊，因为确实10周年仅仅是一个音乐会，表演的部分不是很多，自己还没有定力只听音乐不做别的事情，眼睛没事情做。这一次看现场还是完全不懂的法语，隐隐约约有点担心自己会不会感觉无聊，， 但其实当《Prologue》的旋律一开始的时候，我就知道不可能会感到无聊，现场的声音和耳机里的声音是不好比的，每一个音符使灵魂震颤，'Pitié,pitié'一开口，我一下子很恍惚，真的不敢相信自己能在现场听到 我全程都很亢奋，尤其是《The Confrontation》、《Do you hear the people sing》、《One day more》 《Master of the house》很欢乐，《Beggars at the feast》大家真的在拍手 小珂赛特和伽弗洛什都很可爱，，喜欢《橱窗里的娃娃》，甜甜的小女孩谁不爱 冉阿让说“你命令我不要死，我会努力尝试”的时候真的热烈盈眶 不过也有一些缺点，忘记哪一段高潮的时候设备爆音了，一下子出戏了 第二幕的时候很多地方不该拍手，但是观众在乱拍手，导致几首歌之间的衔接被打断了 不过总体来说，真的远胜录像版本，毕竟大悲所有的版本里面，现场版是最好的！ 录了两段encore： 唱了两遍《finale》，唱第二遍的时候感觉演员是想台下的观众一起唱吧，可惜大家实在是不会说法语 其实有点可惜没有唱《Do you hear the people sing》，不知道是不是政治原因，感觉那个更适合大合唱 落幕！ 像梦一样的晚上 回来路上真的很上头，想重看10周年25周年电影和书了，于是在地铁上就下载了电子书，关掉《麦田里的守望者》，开始看《悲惨世界》 在地铁上还是只能拿AirPods pro 2听大悲，很难受，一回到寝室就使用大馒头听。大馒头4确实很牛！头戴式耳机的声场优势在这种交响乐上真的体现得淋漓尽致。 ww还想再看 哎可惜这次没拍什么照片，还没有养成随时随地用影像记录生活的好习惯
items.content_en: # Les Misérables (French production) review I was lucky enough to snag tickets for Les Misérables. So after the Introduction to Engineering class at Jiao Tong University on December 15th, I skipped my Mathematical Analysis exercise class at 18:30 and went to Shanghai Culture Square to watch the show. I took the subway from Zizhu High-tech Zone to Shanghai South Station, then to Shaanxi South Road. While riding the Line 1, a fellow subway enthusiast excitedly came over to take photos, saying this train was the first one on Shanghai's Line 1. I felt really lucky. Since it had been a while since I last watched a musical, I planned to re-listen to the 10th-anniversary version of Les Misérables on the way. I then realized my ears had evolved—I could tell that AirPods 2 couldn’t handle such grand symphonic music. I regretted not bringing my Big Muffin 4 with me on the subway. When I heard The Confrontation while transferring at Shanghai South Station, I was already thrilled; I couldn’t wait to see the show!! Upon exiting at Shaanxi South Road, I found myself at IAPM mall. I somehow became very familiar with this place after the college entrance exam, so I stopped by the Christmas-themed Apple Store to check it out. For dinner, I had shredded vegetable and beef rice at Shenjing Chenji Roast Goose. I’ve always loved this dish—it’s incredibly savory. I didn’t take a photo of the meal (sigh, I didn’t think to take more pictures this time) because the lighting outside was great, and I wanted to take a selfie. I noticed the reflection wasn’t ideal. Walking to Shanghai Culture Square, I saw the flags by the roadside: I went inside—there were so many people! I saw a girl holding a Leica camera (not just the lens, but the whole camera set). She looked very wealthy. I also saw Shanghai TV doing an interview there. While no one was looking, I secretly took a photo of part of the large poster: I bought some souvenirs: a commemorative album and a CD. Let me show you what’s inside the commemorative album—it’s really exquisite! sukisuki When entering the venue, I even ran into Miss XYS—what a surprise! We just stared at each other. I remember I found the 10th-anniversary version a little boring back then, because it was essentially just a concert with few performance segments. I lacked the discipline to focus solely on the music with nothing else to do, and my eyes had nothing to occupy them. This time, watching the live show with zero knowledge of French, I was vaguely worried I might get bored... But as soon as the melody of Prologue started, I knew I wouldn’t be bored at all. The sound in person is incomparable to that from headphones—every note made my soul tremble. The moment 'Pitié, pitié' was sung, I was completely stunned; I couldn’t believe I was hearing it live. I was excited throughout the entire show, especially during The Confrontation, Do you hear the people sing, and One day more. Master of the house was so joyful, and everyone really clapped along during Beggars at the feast. Little Cosette and Gavroche were so adorable; who wouldn’t love the sweet little girl in The Doll in the Window? When Jean Valjean said, “You order me not to die, and I will try my best,” I was moved to tears. There were a few flaws though: I forgot which climax had audio distortion, which broke the immersion for a moment. During Act 2, there were many parts where clapping wasn’t appropriate, but the audience clapped randomly, disrupting the transitions between songs. Overall, though, the live version is far superior to recorded versions. After all, among all versions of Les Misérables, the live version is the best! I recorded two encores: They sang Finale twice. During the second rendition, it felt like the actors wanted the audience to sing along, but unfortunately, no one knew French. It’s a shame they didn’t sing Do you hear the people sing; I wonder if it was due to political reasons. That song is perfect for a chorus! Curtain call! A dreamlike evening. On the way back, I was still buzzing with excitement and wanted to rewatch the 10th and 25th-anniversary movies and read the book. So I downloaded the e-book on the subway, put away The Catcher in the Rye, and started reading Les Misérables. I still had to use AirPods Pro 2 to listen to Les Misérables on the subway—it was frustrating. As soon as I got back to my dorm, I switched to using Big Muffin. Big Muffin 4 is truly amazing! The soundstage advantage of over-ear headphones really shines when listening to symphonic music like this. I definitely want to watch it again. Sigh, it’s a pity I didn’t take many photos this time; I haven’t developed the habit of recording life through images anytime, anywhere.

items.title: 看星星
items.content: 看星星 很巧，很多很喜欢的作品都是星际题材：星际争霸、星球大战、星际牛仔……无数的星星各有各的神秘与朦胧，对于我而言，星星对我的吸引不仅仅在于对未知的好奇，更因其因人类认知的永远无法企及全部星星的崇高与悲壮。 我是什么时候开始看星星的呢？应当是高一学期初那几个夜晚。当时和Bill臭味相投，已经忘了是什么契机，发现上中竟然能看到很多星星，于是乎每天晚上晚自修结束一起去上中操场，躺在软软的草地上面，一颗一颗地认星星，最后爬起来的时候发现屁股和背全都湿掉了。当时就和他聊，说多少年后，这一段一起看星星的时光可能会模糊朦胧，可能会分不清楚究竟是梦还是真实，但绝对不敢把这段时光忘掉，因为这一段时光太珍贵了。从2020年10月的天空开始几个月的天空当时都十分熟悉。火星、木星、土星、牛郎、织女、天津一、天津四、毕宿五、五车二、五车三、天狼、北落师门、还有整个参宿。这些只在书上看到的名字突然在现实世界有了一个实体。这就好比我抬起头，第一次发现那崇高的未知世界的大门竟然有一道缝，缝里洒出来一束光，我进不去那个世界，却可以沐浴在光芒之中。 后来大操场翻修了，在高中期间再也没开，我和Bill也停止了看星星。很久不看星星，对于星空也陌生了。高三那年的中秋节，我和我的母亲半夜出去散步，想找一个好地方赏月，无奈到处都是灯光，钠灯的晕影无情地遮盖了月之皎洁。后来不知是谁想出对策，可以去楼顶赏月。我们到了楼顶，地平线附近依旧是橙色的，但天空暗了很多，不仅月景更加干净，星星也看到的更多了。那是木星、土星。我惊讶地发现自己依约能够识别出一些星星，使用手机软件对这天空一看，大多都是熟悉的名字。那一瞬间，感到星星是重逢故友。但人之渺小有何德何能与星星为友？能与星星连接，与自然连接，与崇高连接，心中反而怯怯的、空空的。 之前听过一个理论：怯魅的过程实际上是斩断了人与世界的连接感。就好比告诉小孩圣诞老人不存在，礼物是父母偷偷送的，小孩依旧收到礼物，但是心里总会空落落的。（应该是《刘擎》里的观点？）我发现我或许就在用与星星的连接去填补内心的空落，我在尝试与更大的世界产生联系，让自己的心与宇宙交融。 暑假里去了西藏，在高原上，我们两次出去看星空。我第一次用肉眼看到了银河，看到了更多的星星。那一瞬间的崇高感至今时时浮现，感觉那是我和世界联系得最紧密的时刻。 一起来看星星吧！
items.content_en: Stargazing Coincidentally, many of my favorite works are set in space-themed universes: StarCraft, Star Wars, Cowboy Bebop... Each star holds its own mystery and obscurity. For me, the appeal of stars lies not only in curiosity about the unknown but also in their sublime and tragic nature—a grandeur that human cognition can never fully grasp. When did I start stargazing? It was probably during those few nights at the beginning of my first year of high school. I got along well with Bill back then; I’ve forgotten what prompted us to go, but we discovered that we could see many stars from our school. So every night after evening self-study, we’d head to the school playground together, lie on the soft grass, and identify stars one by one. When we finally got up, we’d find our backsides and backs were completely wet. I told him at the time that years later, those moments of stargazing together might become hazy, and we might not be able to tell if they were dreams or reality—but we would never dare to forget them, because those moments were far too precious. The skies from October 2020 onward became very familiar to us over the next few months: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Altair, Vega, Deneb, Aldebaran, Capella, Rigel, Sirius, Fomalhaut, and the entire Orion constellation. These names that I had only read about in books suddenly took on a physical form in the real world. It was as if I looked up and found for the first time a crack in the door to that lofty unknown world; a beam of light shone through the crack. I couldn’t enter that world, but I could bask in its glow. Later, the main playground was renovated and closed for the rest of my high school years, and Bill and I stopped stargazing. After going a long time without watching the stars, I grew unfamiliar with the night sky. During the Mid-Autumn Festival of my senior year, my mother and I went out for a walk at midnight to find a good spot to admire the moon. Unfortunately, lights were everywhere, and the hazy glow of sodium lamps mercilessly obscured the moon’s brightness. Eventually, someone came up with an idea: we could go to the rooftop to view the moon. When we reached the rooftop, the horizon was still orange, but the sky was much darker; not only was the moonlit view clearer, but we could see more stars too—Jupiter and Saturn. To my surprise, I could still identify some stars as expected. When I used a mobile app to scan the sky, most of the stars had familiar names. In that moment, I felt as if the stars were old friends I reunited with. But how could a mere mortal like me deserve to befriend the stars? Connecting with the stars, with nature, with the sublime, left me feeling timid and empty-hearted. I once heard a theory: the process of disenchantment actually severs the sense of connection between humans and the world. It’s like telling a child that Santa Claus doesn’t exist and that the gifts are secretly given by their parents; the child still receives the gifts, but feels a sense of emptiness inside. (I think this is a view from Liu Qing’s writings?) I realized that I might be using my connection to the stars to fill the void in my heart; I’m trying to establish a link with a larger world and let my heart merge with the universe. During the summer vacation, I went to Tibet, where we went stargazing twice on the plateau. For the first time, I saw the Milky Way with my naked eye and observed even more stars. The sense of sublime awe I felt in that moment still lingers in my mind; it felt like the closest I’ve ever been to the world. Let’s go stargazing together!

items.title: 怀念高中
items.content: 怀念高中 今天看到朋友圈里很多团委后两届小朋友发的部门合照，一下子很感慨，也很怀念SHS。 说来好笑，高三的时候大家都口口声声说盼望高三毕业，但是读大学读了一个月出头，朋友圈不知为何却刮起了“想回高三”的风潮。想回高三，这又未尝不是一种斯德哥尔摩呢？高三很苦，但是苦中作乐显得尤其的珍贵。我永远怀念那几个逃课的夜晚，在中兴楼的万圣节之夜，在四楼楼梯间和一楼门厅外柱子后面怯生生地长（发）聊（疯），团代会后在教工之家喝着免费的热可可和热巧克力狂欢（发疯*2）。感觉高三给我的感觉就是大家都是集中精力在冲高考，别的方面已经毫无顾忌了：食堂不好吃就天天出去吃，天天在教室里“热狗”“小丑”地嘴炮。可以肆意地发泄自己的不满情绪而不会有人介意。 高三的印记也有一些留到了大学。对我而言，最重要的印记是音乐。高三听了很多作业钢琴曲和睡眠钢琴曲，而我现在还保留着学习时听钢琴曲的习惯。听到那些熟悉的旋律，恍惚间似乎真的回到了那些大家都很累，有时集中精神有时在“自我放松”的晚自修。又一件说来好笑的事，我尝尝可以把在追的《星球大战》系列与高三联系起来，因为高三后期意外地发现星战的几首main theme虽然有些吵，但是能够帮助我集中注意力。打开Apple Music给我的推歌，本来想听点新的流行音乐的，结果全都是新的钢琴曲。感慨。有时候，记忆浮现需要一个契机，对我来说，其实最好的契机反而是嗅觉和听觉，没有视觉那样直白，但更加扣人心弦。 现在常常回SHS，几乎是每周回一次，去看望czy小姐，和她一起吃顿饭。每次回去我都有一种错觉，总觉得我是在和高三的自己重逢，就像电影里那种转头看见年轻的自己的镜头一样。我很感谢czy小姐在我高三时给我的陪伴，让我的高三生活不至于那样两点一线，给我带来了更多活力。现在，我想陪czy小姐一起度过她的高三，我说实话也并不确定这样经常去看她会不会影响她的学习，但我真的很希望她好，不仅仅是学业上，希望她在高三不要那样苦，依旧开心可爱，也希望我们最终能走到一起。 怀念SHS的日子 Po一些照片吧 万圣节之夜 拍部门合照时摊出来的一片，中间的是女儿送的抽象生日礼物 艺术节大合唱被哪个学长拍到的，唱的很投入，撕心裂肺。不论歌有多烂，作为高三大合唱的歌，总会有点感情的 再po一次Bill美照 Apple fans和胡老师和两个史蒂夫的合照 给董老师的最好的礼物！！ 不敢发和czy小姐的照片🥹 哎看到朋友圈那么多合照，突然情绪化，想今晚就写点东西出来，虽然文笔很烂，，，，但是真的怀念怀念 主要还是照片比较有趣 最后一张： 我拍的最好的龙门楼 祝下一届高三牲“要去到你心中向往的地方”😁
items.content_en: Nostalgia for High School Today I saw group photos of the past two batches of Youth League committee members posted by my WeChat friends, which instantly filled me with emotion and made me miss SHS deeply. It’s funny to think about it: in senior year of high school, everyone kept saying they couldn’t wait to graduate, but after starting university for just over a month, a trend of “wanting to go back to senior year” suddenly took off on WeChat Moments. Wanting to return to senior year—could this be a form of Stockholm syndrome? Senior year was tough, but finding joy in hardship made those moments especially precious. I will always cherish those nights we skipped class, the Halloween party at Zhongxing Building, the shy long chats we had in the stairwell on the fourth floor and behind the pillars outside the first-floor lobby, and the wild celebrations (two rounds of madness) drinking free hot cocoa and hot chocolate at the staff lounge after the Youth League congress. What I remember most about senior year is how everyone focused solely on preparing for the college entrance exam, with no worries about anything else: if the cafeteria food wasn’t good, we’d eat out every day, and we’d spend all our time in class arguing about random topics like “hot dog” and “clown”. We could freely vent our frustrations without anyone caring. Some traces of senior year also stayed with me in university. For me, the most important trace is music. I listened to a lot of piano pieces for homework and sleep during senior year, and I still keep the habit of listening to piano music while studying. Hearing those familiar melodies makes me feel as if I’ve returned to those evening self-study sessions where everyone was exhausted, sometimes concentrating and sometimes “relaxing”. Another funny thing: I often associate the Star Wars series I follow with senior year, because I unexpectedly discovered later that although a few of the main themes from Star Wars are a bit noisy, they help me focus. I opened Apple Music to get recommendations, intending to listen to some new pop songs, but instead I found only new piano pieces. How nostalgic. Sometimes, memories need a trigger to surface; for me, the best triggers are actually smell and hearing—less direct than sight, but far more touching. I now visit SHS frequently, almost once a week, to see Miss CZY and have a meal with her. Every time I go back, I have an illusion that I’m reuniting with my senior-year self, just like those scenes in movies where you turn your head and see your younger self. I’m very grateful to Miss CZY for accompanying me during senior year, which prevented my life from being limited to a dull routine and brought me more vitality. Now, I want to spend her senior year with her. To be honest, I’m not sure if visiting her so often will affect her studies, but I truly hope she does well—not just academically. I hope she doesn’t suffer too much in senior year, that she stays happy and adorable, and that we can eventually end up together. Nostalgia for my days at SHS Let me share a few photos. Halloween night A spread from a department group photo; the abstract birthday gift in the middle was given by my daughter. This was taken by a senior during the art festival chorus performance—we were singing so intently, with all our hearts. No matter how bad the song is, as the chorus song for senior year, it always holds special meaning. Let me post Bill’s photo one more time. A group photo of Apple fans, Teacher Hu, and the two Steves. The best gift for Teacher Dong!! I dare not post photos of me and Miss CZY 🥹 Sigh, seeing so many group photos on WeChat Moments made me emotional, so I decided to write something tonight. My writing isn’t great... but I really miss those days. Mostly, the photos are quite interesting. Last photo: My best shot of Longmen Building Wishing the next batch of senior students “the ability to reach the places they dream of” 😁

items.title: 抢果子首发的经历
items.title_en: My experience with the iPhone launch sale
items.content: 抢果子首发的经历 2023.9.15，晚上8时整，惊心动魄的抢首发环节 国区参赛选手：Leo, Bill, Ryan 港区参赛选手：Hertz 先介绍一下背景： Leo: 最富的富哥，竟然是从iPhone13换成iPhone15 pro (2021->2023) Ryan: iPhone X换成iPhone 15 pro （2018->2023) Hertz: 最为重量级，iPhone 6s换成iPhone15 pro（2017->2023) Bill: 最有商业头脑，帮我和Leo抢iPhone pro，多出来的挂闲鱼卖掉 19:48，Hertz早已蓄势待发，迫不及待，库克告诉他：“我们也同样急不及待（要骗钱）。” 我安抚Hertz： 19:57分，我俩开始倒计时： 倒计时十分🌭️，我们俩不约而同地在10s停下了 然后是沉默的20s 20s啊！多少操场人已经排在我们前面了！ 万念俱灰时，库克安抚我们： 真是贴心呢，能不能现在就好 22:03： but 哎哎，更加绝望。Apple store堪比选课平台 突然， 除了Leo，大成功 Leo很🌭️，，我接了电话，Leo告诉我他有钱花不出去 他的银行卡有限额 完蛋 于是他来向别人乞讨 很🤡 最后也成功的 我们都获得订单，但是预计送货时间迟迟不来 Hertz 第一个获得预计到达时间：9/22 第一批！！他第一个上岸 可是别人杳无音讯 在半夜，我写昨天那篇稿子的时候： 耳机里突然“叮”一声 “我抢到了！”吓了那我正在打原神的室友一跳 战果：四个人抢了5台iPhone，全部成功！全部9/22首发！ 其中一台iPhone15 pro max，三台iPhone 15 pro， 全部8+256 Leo： 由于Bill把抢到的两台iPhone 15 pro寄给我倒卖，我将收到3台iPhone 15 pro倒卖，先成为交大苹果经销商 以及： 如果能靠闲鱼倒卖赚到钱，那明年再抢 完//
items.content_en: My experience with the iPhone launch sale September 15, 2023, 8 PM: The thrilling iPhone launch rush Mainland China participants: Leo, Bill, Ryan Hong Kong region participant: Hertz Let me first give you some background: Leo: The richest guy among us, who switched from an iPhone 13 to an iPhone 15 Pro (from 2021 to 2023) Ryan: Switched from an iPhone X to an iPhone 15 Pro (from 2018 to 2023) Hertz: The most hardcore user, upgraded from an iPhone 6s to an iPhone 15 Pro (from 2017 to 2023) Bill: The most business-savvy one; he helped me and Leo grab iPhones Pro, then sold the extra units on Xianyu. At 7:48 PM, Hertz was already fully prepared and eager to go. Cook told him, "We’re just as impatient (to make money) as you are." I tried to calm Hertz down: At 7:57 PM, the two of us started counting down: Ten seconds left 🌭️, and we both stopped at the 10-second mark. Then came 20 seconds of silence. Twenty seconds! So many people had already queued up ahead of us! Just when we were utterly despairing, Cook comforted us: How thoughtful! Could it happen right now? At 10:03 PM: But Ugh, even more hopeless. The Apple Store is just like a course registration platform. Suddenly, Except for Leo, everyone succeeded. Leo was super 🌭️. I picked up the phone, and he told me he had too much money to spend. His bank card had a spending limit. All hope was lost. So he ended up begging others for help. How 🤡. In the end, he also succeeded. We all got orders, but the estimated delivery time never came. Hertz was the first to get an estimated arrival time: the first batch on September 22!! He was the first to succeed. But no news came from others. In the middle of the night, while I was writing yesterday’s draft: Suddenly, there was a "ding" in my earphones. "I got one!" It startled my roommate who was playing Genshin Impact. The results: Four of us grabbed 5 iPhones, all successfully! All were part of the September 22 launch batch! One iPhone 15 Pro Max and three iPhone 15 Pro models, all with 8+256GB storage. Leo: Since Bill sent the two iPhones 15 Pro he grabbed to me for resale, I’ll receive 3 iPhone 15 Pro units to resell, and thus become an Apple dealer at Jiaotong University. Also: If we can make a profit from reselling on Xianyu, we’ll try again next year. End //

items.title: 好奇心上头
items.content: 好奇心上头 2023.9.13北京时间凌晨1点，加州来电如约而至，随便聊聊这次发布会： iPhone 15 &15 plus iPhone有些无聊，15和15plus又是14pro se 和14 pro max se，如果买15系列真的不如买14pro系列。但是厨子刀法精准，14pro没有type c，15有type c，这就又要斟酌斟酌了。不过有一说一，这次标准版的颜色真的很好看！！有当年iPhone 5C的感觉了。 iPhone pro & pro max pro系列换了A17 pro芯片。首先这个命名很有意思，以前的A系列芯片都不会带“pro"后缀，但是这次的名字叫做“A17 pro”，那么A17芯片放在哪里呢？现在用A系列芯片的产品也就只有iPhone全系列、iPad数字系列和iPad mini系列。iPhone 16大概率会使用iPhone 15pro的芯片，iPhone16pro也会有新的A18 pro芯片，而最新的芯片是不太可能下方给iPad数字版的，结合一下发布时间，A17大概率会给iPad mini7？（这次发布会也没有iPad和Mac新品，应当意味着还会有10月发布会。） A17pro系列用了3nm的制程，照理说是性能更好，也更节能，但是，按照苹果发布会的说法，CPU只有10%的提升，GPU只有20%的提升，但是NPU（神经网络处理器）有100%的提升，说明苹果非常重视AI的性能了。 此外，苹果还是是否重视游戏性能的提升，开始支持硬件级光追了，甚至还有自己的dlss了（但忘记叫什么名字了）。生化危机这种3A大作都能跑了！星穹铁道和原神都被请来了。期待更多3A级游戏登陆iOS平台。 （iPhone 15 pro❎Apple switch ✅） USB3的type-c口以及摄像支持直接存入硬盘补全了iPhone视频的最后短板。 Action button和5倍长焦都算是小更新吧，，而且大多数用户又不会去折腾这些的。 Watch 续航没提升=没什么升级 有一个超宽频技术，没什么用的
items.content_en: Wonderlust At 1 AM Beijing time on September 13, 2023, the call from California came as expected. Let’s chat casually about this launch event: iPhone 15 & 15 Plus The iPhone lineup is a bit boring this year. The 15 and 15 Plus are essentially rebranded versions of the 14 Pro SE and 14 Pro Max SE. If you’re buying an iPhone 15 series model, it’s really not worth it compared to the 14 Pro series. However, Apple’s pricing strategy is precise: the 14 Pro still uses a Lightning port, while the 15 series adopts USB-C, which gives us something to think about. That said, to be fair, the colors of the standard models this time are really nice! They give off the vibe of the old iPhone 5C. iPhone Pro & Pro Max The Pro series now comes with the A17 Pro chip. First off, the naming is quite interesting: previous A-series chips never had a “Pro” suffix, but this one is called the “A17 Pro”. So where will the regular A17 chip be used? Currently, products using A-series chips include the entire iPhone lineup, iPad (non-Pro) series, and iPad mini series. The iPhone 16 will most likely use the chip from the iPhone 15 Pro, and the iPhone 16 Pro will get a new A18 Pro chip. It’s highly unlikely for the latest chip to be downgraded for the iPad (non-Pro) series. Considering the timing of the launch, the A17 chip will probably go to the iPad mini 7? (There were no new iPad or Mac models announced at this event, which suggests there will be another launch event in October.) The A17 Pro series uses a 3nm manufacturing process, which should theoretically deliver better performance and higher energy efficiency. However, according to Apple’s presentation, the CPU performance only improves by 10%, and the GPU performance by 20%. In contrast, the NPU (Neural Processing Unit) sees a 100% performance boost, indicating that Apple places great emphasis on AI capabilities. In addition, Apple also cares about improving gaming performance and now supports hardware-level ray tracing, and even has its own version of DLSS (though I forgot what it’s called). AAA titles like Resident Evil can now run on these devices! Honkai: Star Rail and Genshin Impact were also showcased. We look forward to more AAA games coming to the iOS platform. (iPhone 15 Pro ❎ Apple Switch ✅) The USB 3.0 USB-C port and the ability to directly save camera footage to external storage finally address the last major shortcoming of iPhones when it comes to video handling. The Action button and 5x telephoto lens count as minor updates; most users won’t bother tinkering with these features anyway. Watch No improvement in battery life means no meaningful upgrades. There’s a ultra-wideband technology, but it’s not very useful.

items.title: 影评：《流浪地球2》
items.title_en: Movie Review: The Wandering Earth II
items.content: 是好的 流浪地球2确实比1好很多，首当其冲，感情戏不尴尬，不刻意，不在规训，非常真实，尤其是图桓宇在14年之后重新见到丫丫的那种激动的神态，刘德华真的演得太好了，很令人动容。还有最后老航天人牺牲自己用机械引线引爆核弹，也是非常让人敬畏的。而且这部电影的最大危机不像1那样来的莫名其妙（片尾也解释了1的危机的来源，也算是填坑？），剧情更加完整、连续。 科幻特效方面，依旧保持了1的水准。各种车辆、飞船都很有机械感，也有设计的连续性。尤其是片首太空电梯的部分，这或许是大银幕上首次展现太空电梯？还有方舟号空间站坠毁的镜头，真的太震撼了！唯有两个特效我不太满意；月球引爆核弹时核弹的动画缺少细节，看上去不像是核弹，只是一个个白色的光球膨胀开来而已。或许没有氧气环境下的核武爆炸是这样的？求科普。另外，月球爆炸那段，总感觉一开始给的远视核弹爆炸的画面没做好。虽然核弹爆炸的范围确实就这么小，但是它的连锁反应是巨大的，应当同一个镜头继续刻画月球爆炸的场景。可是实际上，月球爆炸的镜头被拉近了，导致月球坍塌的画面似乎有些小气。 缺点也是有的。我尤其不喜欢一个个过场中“xx事件，倒计时xx时间”。它把对于电影的沉浸感完全破坏掉了，就像是在提醒我：这不是真的，你是在电影院里！而且，它像官方剧透一样，我还在想接下来会发生什么呢，它就告诉我了，这不就没有悬疑感了吗？ 这部电影让我失望的一点在于它没有把上传智能的伦理问题探讨。上传智能的伦理问题应该是很有讨论空间的，而且也确实是一个电影的主线之一。关于上传智能是否是人？上传的人和物理的人之间的关系？上传智能被复制了怎么办？似乎电影并没有深入地讨论下去。而且既然上传智能已经几乎成功了，只是缺一个合适地运行环境（550C/550W），为什么不把没能进入地下城地人变成上传智能？这些没有肉体的上传智能和地下城居民地矛盾？这其实可以挖得挺深的。 我觉得电影的色彩也没有做好。不知是否是我去的影院的问题，总感觉对比度好低，亮度也略微有些低，像没有开启HDR一样，总让人感觉不是很舒服 总之，片子是好片子，值得去巨幕厅一看，没有失掉1的水准。有提升空间，但总体还是不错的。 可惜片尾不如1的震撼。1的片尾流浪地球在书页中间飞太美了！感觉可以超过漫威的片头。
items.content_en: It's a good film The Wandering Earth II is indeed much better than the first installment. First of all, the romantic scenes are natural, unforced, and free from artificiality – they feel very real. In particular, Liu Dehua’s portrayal of Tu Hengyu’s excited expression when he reunites with Yaya after 14 years is truly moving. The scene where the veteran astronauts sacrifice themselves to detonate the nuclear bomb using a mechanical fuse is also deeply awe-inspiring. Moreover, unlike the first film, the main crisis in this one isn’t introduced in a random way (the origin of the crisis in the first film is explained at the end, which serves as a plot closure?). The storyline is more coherent and continuous. In terms of sci-fi special effects, it maintains the same level as the first film. All the vehicles and spaceships have a strong mechanical feel, and their designs are consistent. The space elevator scene at the beginning might be the first time such a concept has been shown on the big screen! The shot of the Arch spaceship crashing is absolutely stunning! There are just two aspects of the special effects I’m less satisfied with: the animation of the nuclear bomb during the lunar detonation lacks detail; it doesn’t look like a real nuclear bomb, but rather just white orbs expanding outward. Is this how a nuclear explosion looks in an oxygen-free environment? I’d love to learn more about this. Also, for the lunar explosion sequence, I feel the wide-angle shot of the initial nuclear explosion wasn’t well-executed. Although the actual explosion range is indeed small, its chain reaction is massive, so the scene of the lunar explosion should have been continued in the same shot. But in reality, the camera zooms in, making the footage of the moon’s collapse seem rather underwhelming. There are also some flaws. I particularly dislike the “Event XX, countdown XX” text that appears between scenes – it completely ruins the immersive experience of the film. It’s like a reminder that ‘this isn’t real, you’re in a cinema!’ Moreover, it acts like an official spoiler: just as I’m wondering what will happen next, it tells me, destroying all the suspense. One thing that disappointed me about this film is its failure to explore the ethical issues surrounding mind uploading. These issues offer plenty of room for discussion and are actually one of the main storylines. Questions like whether a uploaded mind counts as a person, the relationship between the uploaded person and the physical body, and what happens if an uploaded mind is replicated – the film doesn’t delve deeply into any of these topics. Also, since the mind uploading technology is already nearly successful, lacking only a suitable operating environment (550C/550W), why weren’t the people who couldn’t enter the underground city turned into uploaded minds? The conflicts between these bodiless uploaded minds and the underground city residents could have been explored in great depth. I also think the color grading of the film isn’t ideal. Whether it’s due to the theater I went to or not, the contrast feels very low and the brightness is slightly insufficient, as if HDR wasn’t enabled – it’s quite uncomfortable to watch. Overall, it’s a great film worth watching in an IMAX theater; it lives up to the standard set by the first installment. There’s room for improvement, but it’s still a solid movie. It’s a shame the ending isn’t as stunning as that of the first film. The scene of the Wandering Earth flying between the pages at the end of the first film was simply breathtaking – it even surpasses Marvel’s opening sequences!

items.title: 影评：《隐入尘烟》
items.content: 没有感情，只有善意 今天终于赶上档期的尾巴去院线看了这部电影。确实是好电影，不过我估计电影能过审是因为演员表后有一句“马有铁在政府和热心村民份帮助下，住了新房子，过上了新生活。” 怎么说呢，看完电影心情复杂。这部电影我感到没有亲情，没有爱情，邻里情有一点点，只有那种最朴素的善良，让人心动，又让人心碎。 关于爱情 马有铁和曹贵英之间有爱情吗？我认为自始至终都是没有的。两个农村弃儿的婚姻来源于包办，他们努力生活，挣扎中萌生的不是爱情，而是依赖感和亲情。他们两个人的角色换成兄妹换成朋友完全是不违和的，唯一不同的在于婚姻的责任与郑重——这从那始终不变的“喜喜”上可以看出来。 他们见面时是冷淡、害怕的，甚至连结婚照上都是满脸的不高兴。突破口在于有铁给侄子拉家具后回来，贵英送开水。在贵英制作孵小鸡的灯，他们发现灯光变成星星点点的时候，情感汹涌而出。在破房子里竟然也有些浪漫。（感动哭了）两个人在雨中抢救泥土砖的时候两人彻底同心意了（又哭了，原谅我多情）。他们终于有了归属感。 手上印花的图案，草编的驴…这些就是前后呼应的刀了…… 关于亲情 三哥有爱过四弟吗？没有。四弟只是一个工具人，甚至就像是那一头驴子。从电影中看不出四弟对于三哥的看法，但是却可以看到他对于父母、大哥、二哥的尊重。可是我其实很怀疑三哥对于四弟的态度真是反映了他们还在世时对四弟的态度，多么可悲啊。 亲情被彻底解构成了“钱”，可笑的是，这种对于亲情的亵渎遮遮掩掩后仍然显得虚情假意。是已经烂到根里了吗？连装都装不出了？ 关于献血 这不就是一个“吃人肉”的明显的隐喻吗？唯一的缺点就是那个富人的儿子太脸谱化，不过这是一个可以接受的缺点。不表。 关于马有铁其人 他就是一个极度善良、对于自己伤害迟钝（或许是隐忍？），对于别人伤害敏感的人。他体谅驴，照顾燕子，还钱爽气。但估计这样的人只会被归结为老实人、憨人和傻子吧？可是，到底是疯子疯了，还是别人全疯了呢？ 他最后卖掉了所有东西，放走了相依为命的驴，似乎已是看穿一切，超然物外。我更喜欢到这里就戛然而止：马有铁放走了驴，在无垠的沙漠上走着，消失了。 关于运镜 几个印象很深的镜头（不专业） 马有铁在前面用驴犁田，后面的邻居用拖拉机 驴车挡了汽车的路 背景音乐里不时的燕子叫声 新房落成，下半是黄色土房，上半竹月色的天 孵化小鸡灯泡的星光 暴雨中两人互相扶不起来，一起又哭又笑 关于暗示与比喻 我注意到的有两个 曹贵英不小心挖出了麦苗，马有铁说就丢掉吧，当肥料，这是它的命，就像人一样，曹贵英又把它种了下去 马有铁和曹贵英蹭电视，再放食人鱼。我觉得是在比喻亲人、有钱人家和部分邻居 很欣慰看到这样的电影能上线。其实现在我们中国好的剧本不少的，但演得好的真的太少了。到处都是歌颂太平，没人去揭露问题。
items.content_en: No emotions, only kindness I finally caught this film during the tail end of its theatrical run. It’s indeed a great movie. I suspect it passed the censorship review because there’s a line after the cast list that says, “With the help of the government and kind villagers, Ma YouTie moved into a new house and started a new life.” How should I put it? My feelings after watching the film were quite complex. There’s no family love, no romantic love, and only a little neighborly affection here. Only that most simple form of kindness is touching and heartbreaking at the same time. About romance Was there any romance between Ma YouTie and Cao Guiying? I don’t think so from start to finish. The marriage of these two abandoned rural children stemmed from an arranged match; their efforts to live and struggle gave rise not to love, but to a sense of dependence and familial bond. It wouldn’t feel out of place if they were siblings or friends instead — the only difference lies in the responsibility and solemnity of marriage, which can be seen from the ever-present character “Xi Xi” (a homophone for “happy wedding” in Chinese). They were cold and fearful when they first met, and even looked unhappy in their wedding photo. The turning point came when YouTie returned after helping his nephew move furniture, and Guiying brought him hot water. When Guiying made a lamp to incubate chicks and they noticed the light turned into tiny stars, their emotions surged. There was even a touch of romance in that dilapidated house. (I was moved to tears.) When they rushed to save the adobe bricks in the rain, they became completely united in spirit (I cried again, forgive my sentimentality). Finally, they found a sense of belonging. The patterns printed on their hands, the straw-made donkey... these are all elements that echo throughout the film... About family love Did the third brother ever love his fourth brother? No. The fourth brother was just a tool, almost like that donkey. We can’t tell what the fourth brother thought of the third brother from the film, but we can see his respect for his parents, eldest brother, and second brother. However, I seriously doubt that the third brother’s attitude toward the fourth brother reflects how they treated him when they were alive — how tragic. Family love has been completely reduced to “money”. The irony is that this desecration of family love still appears hypocritical even when hidden behind a facade. Has it rotted to the core? So much so that they can’t even pretend anymore? About blood donation Isn’t this an obvious metaphor for “cannibalism”? The only flaw is that the rich man’s son is too stereotypical, but this is an acceptable shortcoming. I won’t elaborate on it. About Ma YouTie He is an extremely kind person who is insensitive to the harm done to himself (or perhaps he’s just forbearing) but sensitive to the harm done to others. He shows mercy to the donkey, takes care of the swallows, and repays debts readily. But probably people would only label him as an honest, simple-minded fool. Yet, is it the madman who went mad, or are all the others mad? In the end, he sold everything and set free the donkey he depended on for survival, as if he had seen through everything and become detached from the world. I prefer the film to stop right here: Ma YouTie lets the donkey go and walks away into the vast desert until he disappears. About cinematography Here are a few scenes that left a deep impression on me (I’m no professional): Ma YouTie plows the field with a donkey in front, while a neighbor uses a tractor behind. The donkey cart blocks the road for a car. The chirping of swallows can be heard occasionally in the background music. When the new house was completed, the lower half was a yellow earthen house, and the upper half was a sky tinged with bamboo-green and moonlight. The starlight from the bulb used to incubate chicks. In the heavy rain, the two couldn’t support each other and ended up crying and laughing together. About hints and metaphors I noticed two: Cao Guiying accidentally dug up wheat seedlings. Ma YouTie said to just throw them away and use them as fertilizer; that’s their fate, just like humans. But Guiying planted them back. Ma YouTie and Cao Guiying watched TV together, and then a piranha scene played. I think this metaphorizes relatives, wealthy families, and some neighbors. I’m glad to see such a film get released. In fact, there are many good scripts in China nowadays, but very few well-performed ones. Everywhere there’s praise for peace and stability, but no one bothers to expose the problems.

items.title: 漫谈电子书
items.content: 漫谈电子书 第一篇知乎长文，聊聊我以前折腾过的电子书。 本人kindle voyage重度用户 格式 之前我有朋友问我电子书这么多格式有什么区别，我以前的瞎折腾结果和理解如下： pdf、docx、txt不是好格式！！！ Epub：其为市面上最通用的格式，有广泛支持，但kindle不支持。（亚马逊嫌弃Epub更新太慢，自己过于先进，因此自己创造自由格式） azw3：亚马逊格式，把任何格式的书传到kindle云端，再从kindle下载，这本书的格式就会被自动转换为了azw3。在kindle上可以更换自己喜欢的字体，但不支持直接上传kindle云端，只能用USB拷到kindle里。 Mobi：分为两类 旧版的kf-7，支持上传kindle云端，兼容性更好，但不支持使用自己的字体。网上大多数.mobi文件都是kf-7，据说可以通过calibre把kf-7转换为kf-8，亲测无用，我的方法是先转换为epub，再用kindle官方的kindle previewer转换为kf-8。 新版kf-8，支持上传kindle云端。支持使用自己的字体。是的，为了好看的字体，我愿意折腾。“自己的字体”指的是我自己拷到电脑的个性化字体，而不是自带的。自带的字体无论什么格式都可以自由转换。（azw3似乎也算一种kf8） Kfx：这个网上应该基本找不到吧？这是亚马逊官方的kindle previewer的内部格式，没啥用，比其他格式用kindle previewer打开更快一些。 fb2：似乎是俄罗斯的一种格式？没有用过，不通用。 如果你有kindle，追求最佳的阅读体验——直接买kindle商店里的电子书。 如果你有kindle，追求最佳阅读体验，但是不想付钱——下载最大的epub格式电子书(可能包含更多图像)，再通过kindle previewer转换为kf-8 mobi。(有时，下载的epub不符合规范协议，无法转换，那么就换几个epub多试试。） 如果你没有kindle，kf8不是很有必要，几个格式都可。 apple自带的图书，据说对epub的规范性要求很高，可能需要试很多epub 有的epub是pdf直接转换来的，格式不规范显得凌乱（有很多奇怪的换行以及突然出现的数字（页码？）），要留个心眼。 资源 至于哪里找到电子书？（按我自己常用度排名） Z-Library 519资源网 sobooks 鸠摩搜索 公众号：吾为书狂、周读书社、心慕流霞、力哥的英语小站 Project Gutenberg 强推zlibrary！不过有时会出现一些小问题，解决方法见这篇文章(https://pangniao.net/Z-Library-meiyouzhaodaokeyongdeyuming.html?replyTo=234) 这里给的是zlibrary的登陆窗，因为这个网址是固定的，而主网站网址一直在变 以及电子书咨询站书伴，里面有各类咨询、图书与字典资源、刷机教程、购买指南 更新： kindle离开中国了，我不离不弃，但是我实在等不下去了，高考之后买了文石leaf2，就无所谓格式了，基本上都能下载到epub kindle真的让我意难平了，尤其是现在：其实我需要的只是一台有实体键和type c的kindle，但是到现在也没有过——我本来期待的是换上type c的Kindle Oasis，结果亚马逊端上来了Kindle Scribe和Kindle ColorSoft 文石的体验很好，虽然确实有色偏的问题，但是小问题 我的kindle voyage: 2015-2023 我的boox leaf 2: 2023-？ 换设备了再更新吧
items.content_en: A Casual Talk about E-books This is my first long-form Zhihu post, sharing my past experiences with e-books. I'm a heavy user of the Kindle Voyage. Formats A friend once asked me about the differences between various e-book formats, and here’s what I learned from my past experiments and understanding: PDF, DOCX, and TXT are not ideal formats!!! EPUB: It’s the most widely supported format on the market, but Kindle doesn’t support it. (Amazon dislikes EPUB for being too slow to update and considers it outdated compared to their own advanced formats, so they created their own proprietary format.) AZW3: This is Amazon’s format. When you upload any book format to the Kindle cloud and then download it to your Kindle, it will be automatically converted to AZW3. You can change the font you like on Kindle, but you can’t upload books directly to the Kindle cloud; you have to copy them to Kindle via USB. MOBI: There are two types: The older KF-7 version supports uploading to the Kindle cloud and has better compatibility, but it doesn’t support custom fonts. Most .mobi files online are KF-7. I heard that KF-7 can be converted to KF-8 using Calibre, but I found it useless. My method is to first convert it to EPUB, then use Amazon’s official Kindle Previewer to convert it to KF-8. The newer KF-8 version supports uploading to the Kindle cloud and allows the use of custom fonts. Yes, for the sake of nice-looking fonts, I’m willing to go through the trouble. “Custom fonts” refer to personalized fonts I copy to my computer, not the built-in ones. Built-in fonts can be freely converted regardless of the original format. (It seems AZW3 is also a type of KF-8.) KFX: You probably won’t find this format online. It’s an internal format used by Amazon’s official Kindle Previewer. It’s not very useful and only opens faster in Kindle Previewer than other formats. FB2: I think this is a Russian format? I’ve never used it, and it’s not very universal. If you have a Kindle and want the best reading experience — just buy e-books from the Kindle store. If you have a Kindle, want the best reading experience but don’t want to pay — download large EPUB-format e-books (which may contain more images), then use Kindle Previewer to convert them to KF-8 MOBI. (Sometimes, downloaded EPUBs do not comply with standard protocols and cannot be converted, so try a few different EPUBs.) If you don’t have a Kindle, KF-8 isn’t very necessary; most formats work fine. Apple’s built-in Books app reportedly has strict requirements for EPUB standards, so you might need to try many EPUBs. Some EPUBs are directly converted from PDFs, resulting in messy formatting (with strange line breaks and randomly appearing numbers (page numbers?)). Keep this in mind. Resources Where can you find e-books? (Ranked by my personal usage frequency) Z-Library 519 Resource Network sobooks Jiumodiary Search WeChat official accounts: WuweishuKuang, ZhouduShushe, XinmuLiuxia, Lige's English Station Project Gutenberg I highly recommend Z-Library! However, it sometimes has minor issues; solutions can be found in this article: https://pangniao.net/Z-Library-meiyouzhaodaokeyongdeyuming.html?replyTo=234 The link above leads to Z-Library’s login page, as this URL is fixed while the main website address keeps changing. There’s also the e-book info site BookFere, which offers various guides, book and dictionary resources, firmware flashing tutorials, and purchasing advice. Update: Kindle has left China. I stayed loyal to it, but I couldn’t wait any longer. I bought a Boox Leaf 2 after the college entrance exam, so format is no longer a concern — almost all books can be downloaded in EPUB format. Kindle really leaves me with mixed feelings, especially now: All I wanted was a Kindle with physical buttons and a Type-C port, but none has been released yet — I was expecting a Kindle Oasis with Type-C, but instead Amazon launched the Kindle Scribe and Kindle ColorSoft. The Boox experience is great; although there are color deviation issues, they’re minor problems. My Kindle Voyage: 2015–2023 My Boox Leaf 2: 2023–? I’ll update again if I switch devices.
